jobs.title: 23916 Migrant Protection Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)/ Case Management) (P)
jobs.description:
IOM’s Approach to Protection promotes a coherent and accountable organizational role in safeguarding the rights of individuals across operational contexts, in line with the Inter-Agency Standing Committee definition. Working with States as primary duty bearers, IOM programmes aim to ensure respect for individual rights, reduce and address exposure to protection risks, and ensure that rights are upheld and needs fulfilled. The IOM Mission in the Central African Republic (CAR) implements migrant protection activities for vulnerable migrants, including third-country nationals, migrants in transit, returnees and persons requiring assisted voluntary return and reintegration support.

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and the direct supervision of the Migrant Protection Officer (Head of Unit), the Migrant Protection Officer (Assisted Voluntary Return (AVR)/ Case Management) will coordinate the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of migrant protection, case management, and assisted voluntary return activities. The Migrant Protection Officer (AVR/ Case Management) will provide technical guidance on protection mainstreaming, safe and dignified assistance, referral pathways, and case management, coordinate with relevant stakeholders, and promote and monitor the consistent application of IOM policies and protection standards, including requirements related to informed consent, confidentiality, and data protection.

**Responsibilities**

1. Coordinate migrant protection assessments and identify and recommend practical risk-mitigation measures related to operational conditions, access to essential services, accommodation, legal identity, specific vulnerabilities, referral pathways, and safe environments across post-arrival, return, and reintegration activities.
2. Coordinate and monitor the overall implementation of IOM CAR’s migrant protection and assisted voluntary return activities, including work planning, risk mitigation, accountability to affected populations, protection mainstreaming, and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (PSEAH)-related safeguards.
3. Coordinate operational case management and provide technical guidance to caseworkers and support staff, ensuring safe, dignified, timely, and needs-based assistance in accordance with IOM policies and procedures.
4. Coordinate protection information management and ensure the accuracy, completeness, and appropriate maintenance of records in IOM-approved systems, including Migrant Management Operational System Application (MiMOSA) where applicable, in line with confidentiality, informed consent, and data-protection requirements.
5. Coordinate complex case-related referrals and follow-up with competent Central African authorities, diplomatic and consular representations, relevant IOM missions, United Nations agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) and specialized service providers, including for documentation, health, MHPSS, family tracing and child or Gender-Based Violence (GBV)-related protection services.
6. Maintain and periodically update referral pathways and service mapping for migrant protection and assisted voluntary return activities in the Central African Republic.
7. Provide technical inputs to project development, results frameworks, donor reporting and resource requirements in line with IOM strategies, emerging operational needs and donor requirements.
8. Coordinate with relevant staff in the Country Office, Regional Office and other IOM missions to support continuity of assistance and smooth coordination of post-arrival and voluntary return processes.
9. Prepare and review operational updates, case summaries, weekly and periodic reports, briefing notes and technical materials, ensuring accuracy, appropriate analysis and protection of personally identifiable information.
10. Participate in relevant local and national coordination mechanisms and technical discussions, as assigned, and support liaison with government counterparts, UN agencies, NGOs, diplomatic missions and other stakeholders.
11. Analyse progress and results of protection activities against agreed objectives, indicators and targets, and identify and analyse trends, operational risks and implementation gaps, and recommend appropriate follow-up actions to the supervisor.
12. Keep abreast of developments in IOM and inter-agency protection standards and promote and facilitate their consistent application in day-to-day operations.
13. Undertake duty travel as required for field visits, airport movements, monitoring, and liaison with counterparts.
14. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Social Sciences, International Relations/Affairs, Migration Studies, Research, Law, Human Rights, Psychology, Social Work, or a related field from an accredited academic institution, with two years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience supporting migrant protection, case management, assisted voluntary return and reintegration, or related humanitarian or migration programming;
- Experience providing protection and assistance to migrants in vulnerable situations and communicating with individuals who have complex needs;
- Experience coordinating with government authorities, civil society organizations, United Nations agencies, diplomatic or consular representations and service providers;
- Experience in referrals, documentation, protection information management and monitoring of activities or project indicators;
- Experience in programmes that include movement operations or post-arrival assistance is an advantage; and,
- Experience with IOM or another United Nations agency is desirable.

**Skills**

- Good knowledge of IOM and inter-agency protection standards, operational procedures and case-management principles;
- Good coordination, analytical and organizational skills;
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and digital case-management or reporting tools; knowledge of MiMOSA is an advantage;
- Demonstrated judgment, initiative and ability to work independently within assigned responsibilities; and,
- Demonstrated interpersonal and teamwork skills and ability to work effectively with people from diverse cultural and professional backgrounds.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Sango or another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) or any relevant language in the Central African Republic is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23650 Programme Support Officer (Migration Health) (P)
jobs.description:
Since 2016, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has supported migration health initiatives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Within its Health, Border, and Mobility Management (HBMM) framework, IOM delivers and promotes comprehensive, immediate and longer-term preventive and curative health programmes that are beneficial, accessible and equitable for migrants, mobile populations, displaced communities and other vulnerable and hard-to-reach populations. IOM works within the existing health framework with government authorities and the health cluster coordination mechanism to address the health needs of mobile communities, including migrants, internally displaced populations, cross-border communities and the populations they interact with. IOM also provides comprehensive pre-migration health assessments and emergency life-saving assistance, while contributing to strengthening the health system, which has been disrupted by long-term conflict, frequent public health and chronic humanitarian emergencies, and continuous underfunding.

In recent years, IOM DRC has intensified its support to the Ministry of Health to strengthen health security capacity at borders to effectively prevent, detect, and respond to infectious diseases and other public health threats. IOM provides integrated disease surveillance and control capacity building for the frontline health staff working in border areas, necessary medical and health commodities for the border posts and health facilities, analyses on population mobility patterns in priority health zones to inform preparedness efforts, health service delivery, including vaccination, as well as risk communication and community engagement targeting mobile populations and communities living along the mobility continuum.

Through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA)-funded project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach”, IOM will support health security over an 84-month implementation period, with the objective of reinforcing community-based surveillance, preparedness and response capacities in Kalemie and Nyunzu health zones, including Port Kalemie and the Moba and Kabimba points of entry.

​​Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in the DRC and direct supervision of the Programme Support Unit (PSU) Coordinator, and in close coordination with the Migration Health Coordinator, the Programme Support Officer (Migration Health) will be responsible for supporting all aspects of the KOICA projects, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E), as well as reporting requirements.​

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical inputs to support the development of new projects in compliance with the donor’s interests and requirements and IOM’s procedures and priorities, and ensure alignment with the Strategic Results Framework.
2. Draft and/or coordinate the preparation of interim and final donor reports as well as mission, regional and Headquarters periodic and project-specific reports, for the Migration Health Department, as may be required in accordance with IOM procedures and donor requirements.
3. Coordinate the administrative aspects of the project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach”, including record-keeping, to support donor contract management in line with specific IOM internal requirements and procedures.
4. Maintain and update reporting systems and schedules, including ensuring revisions to the Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) are done in a timely manner and reflect changes to reporting schedules.
5. Contribute to the development of communication products for the project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach” based on the Migration Health operations and results in close coordination with the Project Manager and the Media and Communication Officer.
6. Maintain accurate and updated records of all correspondence, project files, and administration information to support knowledge management and learning.
7. Provide and/or consolidate inputs for the development of programmatic responses, recommendations and approaches, in line with the Migration Health’s strategy.
8. Work closely with the Project Manager to assist in the overall integration of M&E outputs for the project “Strengthening the public health system in Tanganyika Province to effectively prevent, detect and respond to public health threats through community-based surveillance and the One Health approach”.
9. Provide technical inputs and draft specific sections of strategic documents, presentations, and other documents in line with IOM Corporate Policy in close consultation with the Senior Migration Health Programme Manager.
10. Organize and ensure administrative and logistical arrangements are made for events and visits of partners and the donor.
11. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Public Health, Political or Social Science, International Relations, or other relevant sciences with two years of experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in project support, coordination and/or implementation in a crisis context;
- Experience in M&E rules, regulations, and procedures;
- Experience in humanitarian/development-related activities, budget drafting, research, report writing, liaison with governments and international agencies, reporting, and donor relations; and,
- Experience with project planning, scheduling and deployment of resources, and evaluation and assessment.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM’s services, IOM’s reporting format and styles.
- Knowledge and familiarity with humanitarian and development coordination mechanisms and experience in liaison with other UN, non-UN humanitarian actors and donors;
- Excellent strategic, analysis and drafting skills;
- Excellent writing, editorial and communication skills for the drafting of texts and reports; and,
- Demonstrated interpersonal ability.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of Korean and other official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Final Evaluation of BPPS2 Program in Bangladesh
jobs.description:
**About the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is a non-profit, autonomous regional organization, international in status and non-political in management, staffing, and operations, established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as an outreach center of the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), ADPC has grown and diversified its expertise across the social and physical sciences. ADPC is governed by its Charter, signed in 2005 by its nine Founding Members (Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Nepal, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Thailand), and has its seat in Thailand. Governed by its Board of Trustees, it supports sustainable solutions for disaster risk reduction across a broad range of specialist areas, with a wide range of professional expertise from atmospheric scientists to social scientists with experience across all levels of engagement required for effective Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC’s Strategy 2030 guides the organization in providing comprehensive risk reduction support to countries and communities in Asia and the Pacific, with various programs implemented under 15 Priority Areas of Action by three departments, namely Preparedness and Climate Action, Risk Analytics and Climate Services, and Risk Governance and Financing. The Strategy is operationalized through ADPC's Strategic Action Plan (SAP) 2026–2030, which sets out three strategic goals and nine Result Areas, tracked through an institutional Strategic Indicator Framework. In addition, ADPC integrates three cross-cutting enablers throughout all Priority Areas of Action: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Innovation, and Transboundary Cooperation. Through the SAP, ADPC supports countries in implementing the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the Paris Agreement, as well as regional frameworks. These activities are supported by proactive individual departments of Finance, Human Resources, and Administration. ADPC recognizes the importance of examining the linkages between disaster risk management, poverty reduction, gender equality, sustainability, rights-based approaches, climate change, and regional cooperation. For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net.

**About the Preparedness and Climate Action Department:**

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC advances ADPC Strategy 2030 by strengthening disaster preparedness, anticipatory action, emergency response, resilient recovery, and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. PCA supports governments, response organizations, volunteers, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, communities, and other actors in developing and operationalizing preparedness, response, recovery, and climate action frameworks, plans, systems, and capacities before, during, and after disasters. Its work contributes to the SAP 2026–2030 Priority Areas of Action on Preparedness and Anticipatory Actions, Effective Localization for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Health Risk Management, and Private Sector Engagement, in all which Bangladesh is a priority country. BPP is implemented by PCA as part of its portfolio of multi-stakeholder preparedness partnerships.

**Purpose and Objectives:**

ADPC is implementing the Phase 2 of the Bangladesh Preparedness Partnership (BPP) under the overall guidance of the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief (MoDMR), Bangladesh. BPP is an innovative partnership instrumental in supporting the government of Bangladesh in leading and operationalizing its flagship policy, the Standing Orders on Disaster (SOD) 2019, through a multi-stakeholder model. Phase 2 of BPP aspires to strengthen the multi-stakeholder partnership platform at the national and sub-national levels in Kurigram, Bagerhat, and Cox’s Bazar districts by building operational and technical capacities, research applications, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms.

In line with this, ADPC seeks a consultant to evaluate the ongoing Phase II of BPP, which is being implemented from September 2023 to March 2027. The Consultant will work with the program team to evaluate the program relative to its results framework.

The proposed evaluation is expected to assess how BPP, its processes, outputs, and outcomes have contributed to operationalizing the multi-sectoral partnership model at national and sub-national levels to prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters in Bangladesh. The evaluation will focus on key aspects related to the objectives of BPP, namely:

1. Strengthened inclusive BPP following the whole-of-society approach;
2. Institutionalized technical and operational capacity for disaster preparedness and response at the sub-national level; and
3. Enhanced knowledge sharing and joint research mechanisms to amplify and accelerate BPP implementation.

The learnings from the evaluation and the documentation will inform the BPP Phase III and shape similar projects in countries where ADPC is currently working and where there are synergies in scaling up activities.

The evaluation shall be guided by the six evaluation criteria developed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Network on Development Evaluation (EvalNet), namely relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability. It will adopt a mixed-methods and participatory approach, drawing on program documents and monitoring data, stakeholder consultations, key informant interviews, and field observations, including of simulation exercises or recent disaster response operations where feasible. The evaluation will also consider the progression from Phase 1 to Phase 2 of BPP, using available baseline and monitoring data to assess change over time. The evaluation/learning questions will be finalized in consultation with the BPP program team, and they shall include quantitative and qualitative aspects. Further, it is expected to document the impact of the program through three case studies using the collected data during the evaluation process.

In addition, the evaluation shall assess the strategic alignment and contribution of BPPS2 to the following frameworks, and the final report shall include a dedicated section on these findings:

- **ADPC Strategic Action Plan (SAP) 2026–2030:** the extent to which BPPS2 contributes to ADPC's three strategic goals, in particular Goal 2 (communities are aware of, prepared for, and able to respond to and recover from disasters effectively) and Goal 3 (a fair and prosperous future for all through inclusive disaster and climate risk governance systems); to the relevant Result Areas and Strategic Indicators, notably the policy and institutional environment, local actors' influence, capacity strengthening, multistakeholder engagement for a whole-of-society approach, marginalized groups' influence, and partnerships; to the most relevant Priority Areas of Action, notably Preparedness and Anticipatory Actions, Effective Localization for Resilience, and Private Sector Engagement; and to the cross-cutting enablers of GESI, Innovation, and Transboundary Cooperation. Findings should be framed to inform the SAP mid-term review in 2028, and endline values for the relevant SAP strategic outcome indicators should be reported using ADPC's standardized M&E tools.
- **Gates Foundation:** the extent to which BPPS2 contributes, directly or through plausible pathways, to the Foundation's three goals for 2045 (that no mother, child, or baby dies of a preventable cause; that the next generation grows up in a world free of deadly infectious diseases; and that hundreds of millions of people break free from poverty), and to its Emergency Response strategy. The latter includes strengthening the capacity of local, national, and regional emergency responders and institutions; supporting locally led preparedness planning and public health emergency response capacity; fostering peer learning and innovation; and shifting from reactive response towards proactive preparedness and resilience.

Additionally, indicative evaluation questions include:

- **Relevance:** To what extent have BPPS2's objectives and activities responded to the priorities of MoDMR and the disaster management committees in Kurigram, Bagerhat, and Cox's Bazar, and to the needs of women, persons with disabilities, and other at-risk groups?
- **Coherence:** How well has BPPS2 aligned with and complemented the SOD 2019, national disaster management plans, and other preparedness initiatives of government, humanitarian, and development actors, while avoiding duplication?
- **Effectiveness:** To what extent has BPPS2 achieved its three objectives, and how effectively has the multi-stakeholder partnership model, bringing together government, the private sector, humanitarian and civil society actors, and academia, functioned at national and sub-national levels?
- **Effectiveness:** How have the technical and operational capacities built under BPPS2 been applied in actual preparedness and response, for example during recent cyclones, floods, or other events in the target districts?
- **Effectiveness:** To what extent have the joint research and knowledge-sharing mechanisms generated evidence that partners have used to inform policy, planning, or practice?
- **Efficiency:** How efficiently have resources, time, and partnership arrangements been used to deliver results, and what factors have affected timeliness and value for money?
- **Impact:** What intended and unintended changes, positive or negative, can be plausibly linked to BPPS2 in the speed, coordination, and inclusiveness of disaster preparedness and response?
- **Sustainability:** To what extent have BPPS2 mechanisms, tools, and capacities been institutionalized in government systems, plans, and budgets, and how likely are the partnership platforms to continue after March 2027 without external support?
- **Cross-cutting:** How effectively has BPPS2 integrated GESI, applied innovative approaches, and contributed to regional and South-South learning, including through the Asian Preparedness Partnership (APP) where relevant?
- **Strategic alignment (ADPC):** How and to what extent has BPPS2 contributed to the SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas, particularly multistakeholder engagement, local actors' and marginalized groups' influence, and partnerships, and what does this imply for ADPC's preparedness and localization programming?
- **Strategic alignment (Gates Foundation):** Through what pathways has BPPS2 contributed to the Gates Foundation's 2045 goals and Emergency Response strategy, for example by strengthening responder capacity, protecting women, children, and other vulnerable groups in emergencies, supporting health emergency preparedness, or reducing disaster-related livelihood losses, and how strong is the evidence for each pathway?
- **Learning:** What lessons and good practices should inform the design of BPP Phase III and the replication of the model in other countries where ADPC works?

**Expected Outputs:**

The Consultant is expected to deliver the below outputs / deliverables within the given timelines.

**Key Deliverables and Timeline**

**Deliverable 1 :** Inception report, including an outline of the evaluation report with a defined methodology, work plan, and sampling approach including key learning questions / questionnaires for data collection and an evaluation matrix linking them to the OECD criteria, the BPP objectives, the SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas, and the Gates Foundation goals and Emergency Response strategy, in consultation with the project team. It should also include the template to be used in developing the case studies.

**Timeline:** December 2026

**Deliverable 2 :** First draft of the evaluation report along with the first draft of the three case studies that highlight the impact of the program.

**Timeline:** February 2027

**Deliverable 3 :** Validation workshop with ADPC program team and key BPP stakeholders.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Deliverable 4 :** Final copies of the three case studies.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Deliverable 5 :** Final copy of the evaluation report, with methodology, findings, conclusions, recommendations, and supporting annexes (including endline values for the relevant SAP strategic indicators, and anonymized datasets and data collection tools), along with a presentation deck summarizing the key findings and recommendations.

**Timeline:** March 2027

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

The consultant is expected to assess and document the processes, mechanisms, and practices related to the implementation of the BPP program using secondary data and primary data from Bangladesh. Therefore, it is proposed for the consultant to use the following methods to carry out the documentation and provide the analysis:

- Desk study to review all BPP-related documents, including program framework, progress reports, knowledge products, and meeting minutes, as well as the ADPC Strategy 2030, the SAP 2026–2030, and relevant Gates Foundation strategy documents;
- In-depth interviews and focus group discussions with key stakeholders and beneficiaries using structured questionnaires and guides;
- Interviews with key informants (who will be identified in consultation with the project team and BPP partner agencies); and
- Observations through field visits to project sites as possible and necessary.

Found below is a list of specific tasks expected from the consultant:

- Design and finalize the evaluation methodology, and work plan, in consultation with the ADPC project team;
- Conduct desk research reviewing the BPP Phase 1 and Phase 2 program documents and available monitoring evidence;
- Collect primary data through interviews and discussions;
- Conduct field visits/observations in the target communities based on the work plan and the agreed methodology;
- Analyze the gathered information and summarize the findings, including program performance, institutionalization and sustainability, and contribution to the SAP 2026–2030 Result Areas and the Gates Foundation goals and Emergency Response strategy;
- Compare available evidence across BPP phases and target districts, and explain differences in progress;
- Draft the evaluation report and the three case studies;
- Conduct a validation workshop with ADPC program team and relevant BPP partners; and
- Finalize the evaluation report and the three case studies.

**Working Principles:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities indicated above, the Consultant will be
supervised by the Program Manager from ADPC under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Climate Actions and Impact of the Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC. The Consultant will work closely with other program team members, as applicable. ADPC will review the inception report, draft deliverables, and final outputs, and ADPC and BPP partner agencies will facilitate access to relevant documents, stakeholders, and project sites.

**Participation and independence:**

The evaluation will encourage the participation of government, partner, and community stakeholders in assessing progress and validating findings. The consultant must ensure that participation is voluntary, inclusive, and based on informed consent; that data are disaggregated by sex, age, and disability where feasible; and that confidentiality, do-no-harm, and safeguarding standards are upheld, while maintaining independence in the analysis, findings, and recommendations.

**General requirements:**

The consultant must operate within all ADPC guidelines, procedures, and policies and within the specific program needs.

**Qualifications:**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

- Master’s degree in the field of Community Development, Social Work, Social Sciences, Disaster Management, Program Evaluation, or any other related field.
- At least 10 years of work experience in development work, with at least 5
years in research, monitoring, and evaluation.
- Demonstrated experience with mixed-methods evaluation and community-based or participatory assessment approaches.
- Proven technical specialization in research and evaluation, including theory-based or contribution analysis approaches.
- Good understanding of disaster preparedness and response systems in Bangladesh, including the SOD 2019, and of multi-stakeholder partnerships involving government, the private sector, and humanitarian actors.
- Excellent command of English, both written and spoken.
- Excellent technical writing skills in English.

***Preferred Qualifications***

- Self-motivated, proactive, and takes initiative.
- Demonstrated ability to plan and organize work and time independently.
- Familiarity with Bangla for field consultations.
- Prior evaluation or program experience in Bangladesh.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, team-oriented work style,
and experience working in a multi-cultural environment.
- Strong networking capacity and understanding of humanitarian and
development nexus at local and regional levels.
- Strong desire to learn, undertake new challenges, work hard, and be a creative
problem-solver.
- With self-confidence and good sense of humor, but serious about the quality
and excellence of work.

**Duty Station:** Home-based, with travel to Bangladesh

**Duration:** December 2026 to March 2027

**CDD | 6 mois | ASAP**

## Acted

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## Acted République Démocratique du Congo

La République Démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire prolongée, marquée par la persistance des conflits armés, des déplacements massifs de populations, des chocs climatiques et des chocs épidémiques récurrents, tels que le choléra, le mpox ou la rougeole. Ces dynamiques combinées affectent durablement les conditions de vie des populations déplacées, retournées et hôtes, en particulier dans les provinces de l’Est et certaines zones de l’Ouest du pays.

Dans ce contexte, Acted intervient principalement dans les provinces du Sud-Kivu, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika, Nord-Ubangi et Sud-Ubangi, à travers des projets financés notamment par le Department of State / US, ECHO, FCDO, SDC, le Fonds Humanitaire, ainsi que le CDCS, afin de répondre aux besoins humanitaires immédiats et aux vulnérabilités persistantes des populations les plus affectées. Afin de renforcer la couverture et la complémentarité de ses interventions, Acted intervient en coordination avec plusieurs partenaires opérationnels, et est membre de consortiums humanitaires.

Cette coordination permet à Acted de mettre en œuvre des réponses d’urgence rapides et multisectorielles pour couvrir les besoins vitaux liés aux conflits, aux déplacements forcés, aux catastrophes naturelles et aux crises sanitaires. Les interventions portent notamment sur l’assistance alimentaire, les abris et articles ménagers essentiels, l’Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA), la gestion et coordination des sites (CCCM) ainsi que l’éducation en situation d’urgence, avec une attention particulière portée, dès le premier kilomètre humanitaire, à la protection et à la dignité des personnes vulnérables. Au Sud-Kivu, Acted est par ailleurs un acteur clé du Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM), contribuant à des réponses rapides et coordonnées en lien avec les déplacements de populations et aux chocs soudains.

En parallèle, Acted développe des interventions visant à renforcer la résilience des communautés, à travers le soutien aux moyens d’existence, la relance agricole, la sécurité alimentaire et la relance économique locale, afin de réduire la vulnérabilité face aux chocs récurrents.

Acted apporte également un appui structurant aux organisations de la société civile (OSC) en renforçant leurs capacités organisationnelles et opérationnelles. Cet accompagnement inclut l’appui à la structuration des initiatives locales ainsi que la mise en place de mécanismes de financement en cascade, permettant aux OSC de développer des activités directement liées aux problématiques locales et aux priorités identifiées par les communautés.

Enfin, Acted intègre progressivement dans ses programmes des approches sensibles à l’environnement, visant à la préservation des écosystèmes et des aires protégées, à la réduction de l’empreinte environnementale des interventions et à la promotion de solutions à faible émission de carbone. À travers l’appui aux communautés, Acted encourage le développement d’activités génératrices de revenus durables et d’une économie locale plus verte, contribuant à la protection des ressources naturelles tout en renforçant les moyens d’existence.

## Rôle et responsabilités principales

Le/la Chargé(e) Suivi, Evaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage et Développement de Projets est responsable du développement et de la mise en œuvre de systèmes de suivi, d’évaluation, de redevabilité et d’apprentissage appropriés et viables, conformes aux procédures globales MEAL d’Acted, et contribuant à garantir que les projets et programmes d’Acted fonctionnent comme prévu.

**1. Systèmes de suivi, d’évaluation, de redevabilité et d’apprentissage**
*1.1. Développement technique et des systèmes*
a) S’assurer que le système de collecte, contrôle et vérification des données est en place et que tous les
partenaires l’ont integré
b) Contribuer au développement et à la mise à jour de la stratégie nationale MEAL, du plan de travail
consolidé MEAL et des cadres MEAL pour tous les partenaires du consortium ;
c) S’assurer que les conclusions de MEAL sont reflétées et que leurs recommandations sont intégrées
dans les futures notes conceptuelles, propositions et plans de mise en œuvre ;
d) Mettre en œuvre les politiques et procédures MEAL telles que décrites dans les directives standard
d’Acted MEAL et s’assurer que les outils sont suivis selon les cas ;
a) Contribuer à un déploiement efficace des systèmes de collecte et d’établissement de rapports de S&E
pour l’ensemble du personnel et des partenaires par le biais de formations, de visites sur site, de
manuels et d’autres formes de soutien technique, le cas échéant.

*1.2. Mise en œuvre et gestion du S&E*
a) Maintenir des systèmes MIS électroniques et/ou papier pour le suivi et le reporting de toutes les
données et informations quantitatives, y compris le reporting sur les 28 indicateurs stratégiques
globaux du programme d’Acted ;
b) Analyser les données MEAL et produire des rapports, des fiches d’information avec des analyses et des
présentations statistiques utiles (graphiques, tableaux, histogrammes, box plots) selon les besoins et
en temps voulu ;
c) Mesurer et rendre compte des indicateurs de performance qualitatifs et quantitatifs au niveau des
entrées, des processus, des sorties, des résultats, de l’impact, des objectifs et des buts pour tous les
projets ;
d) Fournir des données à l’équipe de développement du projet pour qu’elles soient utilisées dans la
préparation des rapports destinés aux donateurs et aux autres parties prenantes, selon les besoins ;
e) Contribuer aux propositions des donateurs et aux efforts de collecte de fonds (notamment la
conception de cadres logiques, la formulation d’indicateurs SMART et de budgets MEAL) et aux
rapports ;

**2. Fundraising**

*2.1. Relations Externes*
a) Entretenir des relations de travail actives et régulières avec les bailleurs ;
b) Maintenir des relations de travail actives et régulières avec les autres ONG, les agences onusiennes, les
groupes de travail, Alliance2015, les consortiums/associations et les cercles de recherche
c) S’assurer de la mise en place et mettre à jour régulièrement un répertoire des bailleurs, des ONG
internationales et nationales, des autres partenaires et parties prenantes ;
d) Contribuer au reporting auprès des autorités nationales et locales selon les exigences de
l’enregistrement d’Acted et le statut légal dans le pays.
e) En l’absence de coordinateurs techniques, représenter Acted dans les clusters clés et les réunions des
groupes de travail ;

*2.2. Suivi de la contractualisation*
a) Contribuer à la transmission en temps opportuns des commentaires des bailleurs sur les propositions
en liaison avec les équipes pertinentes dans le pays et les départements Grant Management et Finances
du HQ d’Acted.
b) Lire rigoureusement tous les contrats avant signature, demander les conseils des départements du
Grant Management et de la Finance du HQ d’Acted quand nécessaire

**3. Grant Management**
*3.1. Suivi des contrats*
a) S’assurer que les obligations contractuelles (notamment les exigences de visibilité) et les délais de reporting sont connus et intégrés par l’équipe programme, AME et FLATS.
b) Quand en réunion un problème est identifié par rapport aux livrables attendus dans un délai et un budget donnés, informer le staff pays compétent et demander l’avis du département programme du HQ sur les éventuelles solutions qui seraient en ligne avec les règles des bailleurs.

*3.2. Reporting*
a) Participer et faire les comptes-rendus des réunions de lancement et de clôture pour chaque projet ;
b) Rédiger des rapports narratifs de qualité, retraçant les avancées et les étapes des projets de façon
professionnelle, transparente et dans les délais, en lien avec l’unité grant management et Finance du
siège d’Acted, ce qui contribuera in fine à une arrivée régulière de trésorerie.
c) Travailler en relation étroite avec les équipes AME pour intégrer les données AME (notamment les
données sur les apports, les process, les livrables, les résultats et les indicateurs d’impact, les leçons
apprises et les meilleures pratiques) dans les rapports et les revues des rapports M&E de l’unité AME.
d) Faire la liaison avec les équipes FLATS lors de la préparation des rapports, en particulier avec la Finance
pour garantir la plus grande cohérence entre les rapports narratifs et financiers, en vérifiant la
correspondance des données.
e) Contribuer à la mise à jour mensuelle des Rapports de Suivi (RFU) et garantir une communication fluide
et régulière avec le Grant Management du siège d’Acted ;
f) S’assurer qu’il est répondu aux demandes ad hoc des bailleurs en lien avec le directeur pays, les équipes
programme et support

**4. Autre**
a) Fournir des mises à jour régulières et opportunes sur les progrès et les défis aux superviseurs et aux
autres membres de l’équipe ;
b) Participer aux conférences et ateliers liés au MEAL lorsque cela est possible et se tenir au courant des
meilleures pratiques et des nouvelles connaissances créées dans le domaine du MEAL ;
c) Effectuer toute autre activité connexe assignée par le superviseur immédiat

## Qualifications et compétences requises

- Formation de niveau master dans un domaine pertinent tel que les relations internationales, le développement ou les sciences politiques;
- 1 à 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle antérieure dans un poste pertinent ;
- Expérience professionnelle antérieure dans un domaine connexe, avec une connaissance de la conception de projets, de la rédaction de propositions et de la gestion des subventions ;
- Connaissance du système d’aide humanitaire et capacité à comprendre les systèmes des donateurs ;
- Solides compétences en communication orale et écrite, compétences analytiques ;
- Solides compétences en matière de coordination et de relations interpersonnelles ;
- Capacité à travailler dans un environnement multiculturel et à un rythme soutenu ;
- Capacité à travailler sous pression ;
- Bon esprit d’équipe et capacité à travailler avec des profils variés.

## Conditions

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 1700 et 1900€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Possibilité d’avoir un appel de 30minutes avec un.e consultant.e en fiscalité
- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)
- Ce poste est classé comme un poste international dans la grille de recrutement d’Acted. L’éligibilité à un contrat international est donc requise.

Title: Monitoring and Evaluation Programme Officer NTDs

Location: Burkina Faso, Ouagadougou

- Cultural awareness, patience, and flexibility.
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
