**Benefits**

Sightsavers offers a reward package based on local pay, local contracts and local benefits and will not normally offer international contracts. Sightsavers is committed to investing in the training and development of its employees and offers a supportive work environment.

jobs.title: Retention Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**EXTERNAL RELATIONS AND THE PRIVATE FUNDRAISING FUNCTION**

The External Relations (ER) department is comprised of four complementary functions, including Private fundraising, under which this role falls. To enable IRC to deliver its organizational commitments, the ER department has established a bold new approach that will enhance its ability to raise diverse and flexible funding aligned with IRC’s top priorities, while raising our profile and influence. The ER team is an international team, with colleagues in more than 10 offices globally.

Within Private Fundraising sits the Mass Markets unit. This unit is currently made up of seven teams – US, UK, Germany, Sweden, Digital & Remote Markets and our Supporter Journey and Acquisition teams. Mass Market’s primary goal is to increase the number of sustainers we have globally, via targeted and cost effective acquisition and by building meaningful connections with our donors to ensure we can retain them. By increasing our sustainer numbers and capitalizing on cash giving moments we will grow unrestricted revenue for IRC and the people we serve.

**The Purpose of the Role**

The Mass Market team’s mission is to inspire the Korea public to financially support the IRC in order to help people impacted by conflict and disaster. The main purpose of this role is to support the MM Fundraising Lead, IRC Korea in generating long-term sustainable growth, maximizing income and developing a supporter-centric fundraising model.

As the Retention Marketing Manager, you will be responsible for leading and developing the Retention strategy and program and supporter care. You will be responsible for maximizing revenue and donor development activities – as well as future-proofing the program in line with our supporter’s needs and expectations.

The position has 2 line management responsibility.

You will be joining a team focused on excellence and growth, with significant opportunity to lead on change and drive impact.

**Key Working Relationships**

Internal:

- MM Fundraising Lead, IRC Korea
- F2F Fundraising Manager
- Campaign Fundraising Manager
- Senior Director, Global Retention and Supporter Journeys
- Data and Analytics
- Financial Planning and Analysis
- Comms, Digital Engagement and Creative Studio teams
- Mass Market equivalents in other markets e.g., Sweden
- Martech Systems & Platforms teams

External: Agencies, and other key suppliers

**KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**Strategic and program development (50%)**

- In consultation with Executive Director of IRC Korea lead on the development, implementation and monitoring of the Retention strategy and operational plan
- Maintain and develop a monitoring and reporting framework for retention activity and associated KPIs that show the performance of the acquisition strategy
- Oversee revenue activities across cash, regular giving and the mid-level portfolio ensuring all activity is designed to inspire and engage supporters
- Lead emergency appeals for Retention and ensure processes and activities are optimized for immediate launch
- Oversee supporter development activities to increase loyalty, product holdings and, ultimately, lifetime value
- Be accountable for activity being produced on time, in budget and within departmental strategic objectives
- Ensure best-in-class supporter care that is focused on the long-term relationship with donors
- Work closely with equivalent teams in other national markets (i.e. UK, Germany, Sweden, US) and central support teams to ensure all engagement is coordinated, and where appropriate, synchronized.

**Budgeting and planning (20%)**

- Manage the annual retention planning and budgeting process, advising the Executive Director of IRC Korea on new investment opportunities, and ensuring all activity and project work is aligned with strategic objectives and balanced against team resources
- Review the effectiveness of activity on an ongoing basis and propose investment / disinvestment where appropriate
- Balance in-year income with life-time value as appropriate to ensure all activity is driven by maximizing longer term income
- Manage the income and expenditure tracking, reconciliation and monthly variance reporting
- Focus on maximizing return on investment at all times, and take contingency action as necessary to achieve budgeted income target

**Leadership and management (10%)**

- Lead and develop the Retention Marketing Part
- Be an active part of IRC Korea’s team, modelling leadership behaviors and supporting the Executive Director of IRC Korea in developing a team culture of high performance, continuous improvement and constructive feedback
- Be the retention expert in cross-market working groups and committees
- Manage 3rd party supplier relationships and contracts, ensuring all work carried out is to a high standard and represents good value for money
- Work closely with the Senior Acquisition Marketing Manager to develop a seamless progression for new donors and prospects into further cultivation
- Forge excellent relationships across all areas of the IRC to identify opportunities for collaboration where appropriate
- Network and build external profile of the IRC Korea
- Work closely with the creative studio to develop content is appropriate for the UK strategy and audience
- Work collaboratively with digital engagement and communications colleagues to maximise fundraising and engagement opportunities

**Insight, analysis and data management (10%)**

- Ensure all work undertaken by the retention team is insight driven
- Work closely with the data teams and external agencies and services in order to gain a detailed understanding of IRC supporters, both behaviorally and attitudinally, and use this insight to inform targeting and marketing activity
- Balance in-year income with life-time value as appropriate to ensure all retention activity is driven by maximizing longer term income
- Maintain an up-to-date knowledge of current data protection legislation and ensure all retention activity is compliant

**General (10%)**

- Keep up to date with the sector developments and benchmarking in individual giving to ensure IRC is at the forefront of fundraising developments.
- Maintain an up-to-date knowledge of current legislation, best practice and industry standards and adhere to all relevant regulation. Ensure all fundraising and marketing is ethical, effective and supporter centric
- This post may involve some national and international travel, overnight stays and very occasional working outside core office hours
- Undertake any other additional tasks as requested by the Executive Director of IRC Korea

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Essential** **Skills, Knowledge and Qualifications:**

- Driven and proactive with a solutions-based attitude and the ability to motivate a team
- Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to manage, influence and negotiate with stakeholders at all levels
- Ability to manage sophisticated budgets and performance forecasting models
- Comprehensive understanding and experience of audience segmentation, analytical modelling such as LTV and use of insights to drive strategy and performance
- Commercial mindset, with the ability to set and evaluate short and long-term strategic objectives and pivot based on results
- Numerate with excellent data analysis and interpretation skills
- Excellent organizational skills, especially the ability to manage a complex, varied and substantial team workload
- Excellent verbal and written English and the ability to produce well designed and high quality proposals and reports

**Experience:**

- More than 5+yrs experience in Supporter(customer) Development / Retention Marketing/ Experience marketing functions in corporate or NGO sector.
- Detailed understanding of cash and recurring revenue business models and budgets
- Experience and understanding of creative process and relationship with brand identity through different channels and audiences
- Experience of working in a fast-paced, high performing team
- Experience working for a centralized, international organization would be a strong advantage
- Experience using a CRM system

**Language Skills:** Korean speaker, Fluent in English.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: National Fsal Sector Co-Coordinator
jobs.description:
**VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**

**NATIONAL FSAL SECTOR CO-COORDINATOR**

**Organization**

IHH Humanitarian Relief Foundation

**Number of Vacancies**

1

**Duty Station**

IHH Office, Damascus, Syria

**Employment Type**

Full-time

**Reporting Line**

This position maintains a dual reporting line to IHH and the FSAL Sector Coordination Team.

## ABOUT IHH

IHH Humanitarian Relief Foundation is a humanitarian organization dedicated to supporting vulnerable communities affected by conflict, disasters and humanitarian crises. The organization delivers humanitarian assistance and recovery programmes to address essential needs, strengthen resilience and support dignified living conditions.

## ABOUT THE ROLE

The Food Security and Agricultural-Livelihoods (FSAL) Sector in Syria is a humanitarian coordination mechanism that brings together relevant organizations and stakeholders to improve the quality, coherence and effectiveness of the response across Syria.

The National FSAL Sector Co-Coordinator supports the national-level coordination of FSAL Coordination Team consisting of two Sector Coordinators and two Information Managers, as well as with focal points from the Ministry of Agriculture. The FSAL is part of the humanitarian coordination structure and has the mandate to facilitate coordination at national and subnational levels, share information, engage in joint analysis, response planning and collaboration with various humanitarian actors at the sector and inter-sectoral levels, with the aim of identifying needs and gaps, reducing duplication, and promoting a coordinated, needs-based response.

IHH was elected by the majority of FSAL sector partners in May 2026 to take the role of the co-coordination support for the foreseeable future.

## JOB SUMMARY

IHH is seeking an experienced humanitarian professional to contribute to the national-level coordination of the FSAL response throughout Syria. The Co-Coordinator will support effective engagement among UN agencies, international and national NGOs, local actors, technical partners and relevant authorities, while promoting principled, transparent and inclusive coordination.

The position focuses on facilitating coordination rather than directly managing the implementation of individual organizations’ projects. The successful candidate will support the FSAL Coordination Team with organizing sector meetings, supervising information management, follow up with needs and response analysis, strategic planning, inter-sector engagement, partner participation and follow-up on agreed actions. The role will work in line with the applicable FSAL coordination arrangements and agreed terms of reference.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

### National-Level Coordination and Partner Engagement

- Support the FSAL Coordination Team in facilitating national-level coordination among FSAL partners operating across Syria, including governmental instituation lead by the Ministry of Agriculture, UN agencies, international and national NGOs, local organizations and relevant technical actors.
- Organize and facilitate sector meetings, workshops and consultations; prepare agendas, presentations and minutes, and maintain action trackers to follow up on agreed decisions.
- Promote inclusive participation of national and local organizations and ensure that partners from different geographic areas can contribute to sector discussions and planning.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with partners and relevant coordination bodies, supporting consensus-building and timely information exchange.
- Represent the FSAL coordination mechanism in inter-sectoral and other relevant coordination meetings, as agreed with the Sector Coordinators and in accordance with the sector’s governance arrangements.
- Support the FSAL Coordination Team in supervising subnational level coordination teams in the current four hubs in Syria: North, East, Central (including Coastal) and South with similar support at the national level, where needed.

### Needs Analysis, Response Monitoring and Gap Identification

- Support the collection, review and analysis of information on humanitarian needs, partner presence, planned and ongoing activities, geographical coverage and response achievements across Syria.
- Identify potential gaps, overlaps and under-served locations or population groups, and share evidence-based findings with partners to inform collective decisions and prioritization.
- Contribute to joint needs assessments, response monitoring exercises, analytical products and other sector information products, coordinating with relevant information-management and assessment colleagues.
- Encourage partners to submit timely, accurate and consistent activity information and support the use of agreed reporting tools, indicators and methodologies.
- Promote appropriate disaggregation of information, including by location, population group, sex, age and disability where relevant and feasible.

### Strategic Planning and Response Prioritization

- Contribute to the development, review and monitoring of FSAL sector strategies, response plans, priorities and workplans for Syria.
- Support the translation of needs and response analysis into practical recommendations and collective priorities, taking account of access constraints, emerging risks and differences between geographic areas.
- Facilitate partner consultations on response priorities, technical approaches, standards, guidance and operational challenges.
- Support coordinated preparedness and contingency planning for shocks and emergencies affecting food security and agricultural-livelihoods.
- Contribute to relevant humanitarian planning and funding processes, including needs overviews, response plans and allocation-related consultations, as requested through the agreed coordination structure.

### Technical Coordination and Inter-Sector Engagement

- Facilitate information sharing and technical discussion on food assistance, agricultural production, livestock where relevant, livelihoods recovery, market-based approaches and other FSAL interventions.
- Promote complementarity between food security, agricultural-livelihoods’ activities and related sectors, including Nutrition, WASH, Protection (including various Areas of Responsibilities), Health, Education, Shelter/NFI and other relevant coordination working groups, such as Cash, AAP, and Solutions Working Groups.
- Help identify cross-cutting issues and promote the integration of protection, gender, age, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and environmental considerations into sector discussions and guidance.
- Support the dissemination and consistent application of relevant technical guidance, minimum standards and agreed sector approaches, while recognizing partners’ operational mandates and context-specific needs.
- Escalate strategic, technical or operational issues that require sector-level discussion or inter-sector decision-making through the established coordination channels.

### Information Management, Communication and Reporting

- Support the maintenance and regular updating of partner contact lists, 5W or equivalent activity mapping, meeting records, action trackers and other sector coordination tools.
- Prepare clear and timely meeting summaries, situation updates, briefing notes, presentations and other coordination products in English and Arabic as required.
- Ensure that sector information is shared in a timely, accurate and accessible manner, respecting confidentiality, data-protection requirements and agreed information-sharing protocols.
- Document key challenges, lessons learned, good practices and emerging trends, and share these with partners to support evidence-based decision-making.
- Support communication between national coordination structures and relevant sub-national coordination mechanisms to ensure that field-level information informs national analysis and priorities.

### Accountability, Localization and Humanitarian Principles

- Promote principled, impartial, needs-based and transparent coordination, respecting the mandates and independence of participating organizations.
- Encourage meaningful participation of local and national actors in analysis, planning, decision-making and technical discussions.
- Promote the integration of accountability to affected populations, community feedback, protection mainstreaming, gender equality and inclusion in sector priorities and partner approaches.
- Support the identification and appropriate referral of cross-cutting concerns through established coordination and protection mechanisms, without undertaking specialized service provision outside the role’s mandate.
- Maintain professional integrity, confidentiality and respectful engagement, and comply with IHH policies, safeguarding standards, PSEA requirements and the code of conduct.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

- Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, agricultural economics, food security, economics, development studies, international relations or another relevant discipline. A relevant postgraduate qualification is an advantage.
- At least five years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian or development programming, including substantial experience in food security, agriculture, livelihoods or related sectors.
- Demonstrated experience in inter-agency or inter-organizational coordination, partnership engagement, facilitation of meetings or working groups, and follow-up on agreed actions.
- Strong understanding of the humanitarian coordination system, sector/cluster approaches, response planning and inter-sector coordination.
- Experience in needs analysis, response monitoring, gap and overlap analysis, information management or preparation of sector-level analytical products.
- Experience working with national and international NGOs, UN agencies, local organizations and relevant authorities in complex humanitarian contexts; knowledge of Syria is highly desirable.
- Experience supporting strategy development, response prioritization, contingency planning or humanitarian funding and planning processes is an advantage.
- Excellent facilitation, communication, negotiation, analytical, writing and presentation skills, with the ability to build consensus among diverse stakeholders.
- Fluency in Arabic and excellent written and spoken English are essential. Additional languages are an advantage. Knowledge of Turkish is also an advantage.
- Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and PowerPoint. Familiarity with humanitarian information-management systems and data visualization tools is an advantage.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles, impartiality, inclusion, accountability, safeguarding and respectful collaboration with diverse partners.

## CORE COMPETENCIES

- Neutral and inclusive coordination, facilitation and consensus-building.
- Strategic analysis, evidence-based planning and identification of response gaps.
- Strong written communication, reporting and presentation skills in Arabic and English.
- Partnership management and effective engagement with diverse humanitarian actors.
- Information management, data interpretation and attention to accuracy.
- Inter-sector collaboration, adaptability and problem-solving in a complex operating environment.
- Integrity, confidentiality, accountability and commitment to humanitarian principles.

## WORKING CONDITIONS

This is a national-level coordination role covering the entirety of Syria. The duty station will be confirmed by IHH in line with operational and coordination arrangements. The role may require travel and participation in meetings with partners and coordination bodies in different locations, subject to access, security and applicable organizational procedures.

**Dual Reporting Arrangement:** This position is based within IHH’s International Grants Unit, under the International Relations Department. In addition to the sector coordination responsibilities outlined above, the position holder will, in a limited capacity, double-hat to support the Grants Unit’s work as needed.

**Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.**

jobs.title: Innovative Finance Expert_Prosper Global_Kyiv, Ukraine
jobs.description:
NORCAP works to improve aid to better protect and empower people affected by crisis and climate change. We do this by providing expertise and solutions to humanitarian, development and peacebuilding partners, because we believe working together is the best way to reduce needs, risks and vulnerability over time. We seek and promote more effective ways of working at the global level and in the field. NORCAP’s aim is not only to reduce needs, but also to create choice and opportunity for vulnerable people. NORCAP works with and through our partners to improve aid in two complementary ways:

• We provide targeted expertise to strengthen our partners’ response.

• We collaborate with partners to develop solutions to un‑met gaps and challenges.

Prosper Global (formerly known as Mercy Corps) is a humanitarian organisation working alongside communities facing conflict, climate change, and economic hardship to meet urgent needs and create the conditions for lasting progress. Today's challenges demand new solutions, so we pair local knowledge with global resources to help communities build what's needed, test what's possible, and scale what's proven so that people everywhere can pursue a full life on their own terms. In 2026, we changed our name from Prosper Global to Prosper Global, to reflect our belief that when every community can prosper, all of humanity moves forward.

In 2022, NORCAP (Part of the Norwegian Refugee Council) and Prosper Global entered into a global Memorandum of Understanding. Under this partnership, the NORCAP Energy & Environment (E&E) programme is supporting Prosper Global Ukraine by strengthening its Climate Finance Portfolio through the deployment of a specialist with expertise in climate and energy finance, while also contributing to the ongoing emergency response. The selected expert will be contracted under NORCAP and adhere to NORCAP’s conditions of appointment, while working as part of Prosper Global Ukraine to deliver the tasks and outputs outlined in this Terms of Reference.

To support this work, we are seeking **an Innovative Finance Expert** based in **Kyiv**, **Ukraine** for 6 months, (with possibility of extension), with up to 20% travel in-country.

## Responsibilities

The Innovative Climate Finance Expert (Ukraine) supports recovery and resilience efforts through the identification, design, and deployment of green and innovative finance mechanisms. The role provides hands-on advisory expertise across climate finance instruments, including results-based finance, concessional loans, guarantees, insurance products, blended finance, and carbon credit mechanisms, supporting Prosper Global’s transition toward a diversified, multi-instrument climate finance portfolio.

The Expert will contribute to new program design and strategic positioning with donors and investors, including global climate funds, Development Finance Institutions (DFIs), and private sector partners. This includes partnership development, external representation, and engagement in relevant sector forums, while also strengthening program quality, innovation, and learning. The role will further support coordination and alignment with complementary energy and climate initiatives led by humanitarian and development actors in Ukraine and globally.

As the Innovative Finance Expert, you will take on the following responsibilities:

**Strategy Advisory, Finance Structuring and Program Design (45%)**

- Identify and advance opportunities for innovative climate and energy financing in Ukraine (results-based finance, concessional loans, guarantees, insurance, blended finance, carbon credits), building on Prosper Global’s existing portfolio and strategies.
- Advise on the design and structuring of climate mitigation and adaptation programs that combine public, concessional, and private capital.
- Contribute to project design and to competitive proposals and investment cases for climate funds, development finance institutions, and impact investors.
- Author or review knowledge products such as reports, briefs, tools, and guides.

**Partnerships and Technical Influence (45%)**

- Build strategic partnerships with climate and energy finance institutions, DFIs, governments, humanitarian and development actors, and private sector partners.
- Work with Prosper Global in Ukraine leadership to expand and strengthen the portfolio.
- Support negotiations with funders and financial partners on program design, financing terms, and implementation.
- Track donor and investor priorities to inform influencing and funding strategies on climate finance, energy transition, and green recovery.

**NORCAP Engagement (10%)**

Take part in NORCAP activities, including follow-up calls, Community of Practice sessions (online and annual in-person workshop, subject to funding), and timely reporting.

## Qualifications

To excel in this role, candidates should possess the following qualifications and skills:

- Master's or equivalent in finance, economics, climate studies or related field;
- At least 5-7 years of full-time work experience in climate finance in fragile settings, including blended finance, concessional instruments, and results-based approaches. Experience working in Ukraine is advantageous;
- Demonstrated experience in securing funding for climate initiatives from Development Finance Institutions and global climate finance mechanisms.
- Familiarity with economic and quantitative modeling related to climate, ecosystem services, and specific sectors such as forestry, agriculture, energy & energy efficiency;
- Strong networking and partnerships management skills;
- Fluency in English;
- Superior writing and analytic skills required, including the ability to tailor technical writing to the audience, with a track record of successful writing/analysis on proposal or grant development preferred;
- Demonstrated flexibility and creativity in planning and problem solving;
- Computer literacy and capacity to work with MS Office applications required.

**Success Factors**

The successful Expert will be a proactive relationship builder with strong climate finance expertise and the ability to turn technical knowledge into practical partnerships and funding opportunities. They will thrive in a fast-changing environment, manage multiple workstreams effectively, and communicate clearly with diverse stakeholders. A collaborative mindset, cultural sensitivity, and readiness to work in crisis affected settings are essential.

**We welcome applications from candidates worldwide, both international and national experts.**

For operational and administrative reasons, we particularly encourage applicants who are based in Europe or who hold valid European residency and are willing and able to be based in Ukraine. We also encourage candidates located in countries where NRC has an office such as Norway, the UK, Moldova, and Switzerland as this may facilitate smoother taxation and administrative processes, including potential contract continuation into 2027.

Please note that candidates who are Ukrainian nationals will be offered a national contract, with terms and remuneration based on national conditions.

**Terms of Reference:** [Innovative Climate Finance Expert, Prosper Global Ukraine\_NORCAP.docx](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil-my.sharepoint.com/:w:/g/personal/mariabeatriz_genty_nrc_no/IQBxfeYS3g4aTJ0FrM4OXNP-Ad4_VVU8aJuXwZAWxFKf9k0?e=ZBz4mJ)

**Candidates are strongly encouraged to review the Terms of Reference before applying, as they contain essential information on:**

- Responsibilities
- Tax Obligations and Compliance
- Rest & Recuperation
- Living Conditions / Security and Environmental Conditions

**What we offer**

In recognition of your expertise and contributions, we provide the following benefits and opportunities:

- Rewarding work for a renowned global organisation
- Access to a network of humanitarian, peace, and development professionals
- Join NORCAP’s team of experts and be considered for future assignments elsewhere
- A dedicated Staff Care Unit

**Our Values & Commitment**

All NRC employees are expected to act in accordance with the organisation’s values.
Being dedicated, innovative, inclusive, and accountable are behaviours and beliefs that guide how we work and how we build relationships. We are committed to creating a safe, respectful, and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, empowered, supported, and a genuine sense of belonging.

NORCAP values diversity, equity, and inclusion and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. We believe that a diverse workforce strengthens our ability to respond effectively to the needs of people affected by crisis.

NRC has a zero‑tolerance stance toward any form of exploitation or abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), and we do not tolerate inaction when concerns arise.

All offers are subject to reference and background checks conducted in line with our safeguarding standards, and NORCAP reserves the right to conduct a full background check on shortlisted candidates.

jobs.title: Climate Risk Specialist
jobs.description:
**About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to be for scientific, educational, developmental and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) in an effective manner.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/

The Risk Analytics and Climate Services Department is a multi-disciplinary team of experts committed to providing innovative, science-based solutions for actions to adapt to climate change and mitigate the impacts of disasters. These lead to risk-informed developments in the sectors such as agriculture, transportation, water resources, and health.

ADPC currently cooperates with Thailand’s Department of Climate Change and Environment (DCCE) on a Green Climate Fund (GCF) Readiness project, entitled “Enhancing Thailand’s Capacity for Climate Adaptation through Risk-informed Anticipatory Actions to Flood and Drought,” until July 2027. The project aims to support Thailand, specifically the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation and the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning, to strengthen the ability to anticipate and respond to climate-induced disasters. It focuses on improving disaster risk management through enhanced early warning systems, anticipatory action planning, and climate resilience financing mechanisms.

ADPC seeks a qualified candidate to provide subject-matter expertise and substantial input to the project’s climate change related activities in Thailand.

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

- Lead the development of knowledge products on the lessons learned and best practices for GCF Readiness projects in Thailand, drawing from the project experience as well as international recommendations.
- Participate in the project prioritization workshop and the following bilateral meetings with selected sectoral organizations, to support ADPC in prioritizing project concepts for DCCE and GCF.
- Contribute to the pre-feasibility studies of the possible projects, under the leadership of the Emergency Preparedness Specialist.
- Participate as a resource person in the project pipeline validation workshop.
- Contribute to the analysis of existing frameworks for inter-agency collaboration in climate data and early warning information sharing and applications; Identify barriers to effective collaboration and propose collaboration and formal cooperation mechanisms to overcome the barriers.
- Review and provide input for improvement on the report “a comprehensive review of Thailand’s current climate surveillance systems and early warning mechanisms as well as the recommendations for upgrading the systems and mechanisms.”
- Take part in project workshops and events, delivery of sessions/discussions, and event reporting.
- Collaborate with the project’s GEDSI Specialist.
- Join project team meetings.
- Provide inputs on the design, development, and dissemination of communications materials.

**Specific Outputs:**

- A knowledge product on the lessons learned and best practices for GCF Readiness projects in Thailand;
- Sections of the report of the pre-feasibility studies of the possible projects;
- Sections of the report on the analysis of existing frameworks for inter-agency collaboration in climate data and early warning information sharing and applications and the proposed means to improve them;

**Working Principles:**

The Consultant will report to ADPC’s Project Manager of the Enhancing Thailand’s Capacity for Climate Adaptation through Risk-informed Anticipatory Actions to Flood and Drought project, while working closely with other team members of the project as well as external partners.

**Qualifications:**

The Consultant is expected to possess the following qualifications.

- Minimum 10 years of experience in developing and managing DRR, climate change adaptation or mitigation projects.
- Strong expertise in DRR and resilience-building; Experience in integrating these strategies into national and local preparedness/adaptation plans and their application to climate adaptation and resilience efforts in Thailand.
- Good understanding of the priorities of donors and development organizations.
- Demonstrated experience in assessing the capacity/needs of and engaging with communities and local governments in climate and disaster resilience building.
- Demonstrated experience engaging with Thai Government agencies.
- Fluency in Thai (reading, writing, and speaking).
- Strong English communication skill.
- Proven experience of working in a diverse and multicultural environment is preferred.
- Proven ability to work with tight deadlines and flexibility is preferred.
- Strong interpersonal skills are desirable.

**Duty Station:**

Home-based with occasionally meetings at ADPC Office in Bangkok and at stakeholders’ locations

**Duration:**

The duration of this assignment will be from November 2026, and will run through June 2027

**Itinerary**:

Official travel may be required; all work-related travel costs will be covered by ADPC such as economy class flight ticket, land transportation, DSA and other related costs as applicable as per the ADPC policies.

**Condition of payment:**

The consultant will be paid monthly, based on the daily rate.

jobs.title: Foundation Relations Manager
jobs.description:
**WHO YOU ARE**

You're someone who people can rely on, and you're always there when they need a helping hand. You're looking for a new position where you can make a difference in your life, the lives of others, and the world. In return, you seek an organization that appreciates your individuality and supports you as a member of a diverse and talented team.

**WHO WE ARE**

MAGNA is a private, non-profit, international humanitarian organization whose objective is to provide medical aid to populations in crisis. MAGNA organizes humanitarian medical projects to help people in need, whether through poverty, disease, war, or ecological disaster and regardless of ethnicity, religion or nationality. MAGNA is independent of all states and institutions, as well as of all political, economic or religious influences.

MAGNA recruits medical and non-medical personnel, collects private and institutional funds and raises awareness among the public about populations in danger. Using a small but highly committed group of staff and volunteers, MAGNA has achieved respectable results. MAGNA for over 25 years has focused on providing medical care (primary, secondary, nutrition, sexual violence, HIV/AIDS and other infectious diseases) in countries such as Afghanistan, Democratic Republic of Congo, Lebanon, Ukraine and Cambodia among others.

**GENERAL DESCRIPTION**

**The Foundation Relations Manager is responsible for securing private and corporate foundation funding for MAGNA’s programs and activities and oversees the grant management and development process for our Corporate and Foundation Relations team.**

**SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

1\. Manage a Personal Portfolio of Foundation Funders Responsible for the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and management of a donor portfolio of foundations in the range of EUR5,000+, conducting the full range of activities required to prepare, submit, and manage timely grant proposals and sponsorship requests to private, public, and corporate foundations; building up our mid-level donor base.

2\. Administration of Grants and Data Oversee the grants management process, including but not limited to tracking all donor communications and activities, maintaining the grants calendar, compiling data, collecting success stories and narratives that support proposals and reports, and ensuring accurate donor records.

3\. Grant Reporting and Budget Monitoring Prepare, compile, and coordinate the submission of all components of grant reporting, including narrative reports, expense reports, and budget modifications that align with funding objectives, and ensure that all documents are submitted by deadlines.

4\. Events Support Support Resource Development team in implementation of signature events as well as other donor activities, including volunteer days, third-party events, and donor recognition events. Lead or support volunteer days for foundation and corporate donors.

**SUMMARY OF JOB QUALIFICATIONS**

- Must be able to successfully pass a drug test, background check, (credit) authorization, and a driving record check
- Bachelor’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Communications, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
- Minimum of 2 years of experience in foundation relations, grant writing, fundraising, or nonprofit development.
- Demonstrated success securing and managing foundation and/or corporate funding opportunities.
- Experience managing grant processes including proposal development, reporting, donor stewardship, and deadline management.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to develop compelling proposals and reports.
- Strong organizational, project management, and relationship-building skills with attention to detail.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Office and experience using donor databases or CRM systems preferred.
- Ability to support donor engagement activities, volunteer events, and occasional evening or weekend events as needed

**BENEFITS: WE TAKE CARE OF OUR EMPLOYEES**

**COMPENSATION**

Pay Range:

Salary offers are based on several factors, including job-related knowledge, experience, and qualifications.

jobs.title: OPERATIONAL FINANCE ADVISOR/TECHNICIAN
jobs.description:
**GENERAL CONTEXT**
MAGNA is a private, non-profit, international humanitarian organization whose objective is to provide medical aid to populations in crisis. MAGNA organizes humanitarian medical projects to help people in need, whether through poverty, disease, war, or ecological disaster and regardless of ethnicity, religion or nationality. MAGNA is independent of all states and institutions, as well as of all political, economic or religious influences.

MAGNA recruits medical and non-medical personnel, collects private and institutional funds and raises awareness among the public about populations in danger. Using a small but highly committed group of staff and volunteers, MAGNA has achieved respectable results. MAGNA for over 25 years has focused on providing medical care (primary, secondary, nutrition, sexual violence, HIV/AIDS and other infectious diseases) in countries such as Afghanistan, Democratic Republic of Congo, Lebanon, Ukraine and Cambodia among others.

The operations are implemented by field teams and the mission coordination teams; together with the operational centre based between Bratislava and Prague and decentralized around the world. The field operations are guided and supported by Operational Centre covering and services supporting operations, including the Operational Finance Services.

**JOB GENERAL OBJECTIVE AND CONTEXT**
Hierarchically dependant on the Operational Finance Service of MAGNA, the Operational Finances Technician will be in charge of following up and giving technical support to finance related issues and management within the projects run by Operation Centre (OC).

He/she will be responsible for applying and promoting the policies and regulations established by the Finance Department of MAGNA and for guaranteeing the quality of the programs. He/she will also have to ensure that the MAGNA humanitarian principles and finance ethics throughout all implementing stages within the projects are respected.

OC is responsible for approximately 12 projects in 4 countries, to which they relate through their respective Coordinators and teams.

The aim of the OC is to support the missions when identifying, planning, proposing, implementing and following up the projects ensuring their quality.

**MAIN TASKS**

The Operational Finance Technician will have to:

1. Assure the Principles of the Financial Policy of MAGNA and its financial operational strategy plan.

- To ensure respect for the Organization’s principles and financial policy guidelines.
- To support the team in the field when defining project proposals together with the other OC members.
- To justify the financial strategy of the projects in the Committee.
- Supervises and consolidates the field budgets of as well as the annual planning budget.
- Prepares the financing plan of the projects, together with: the field team, the operational centre and the responsible of the FINOP service.

1. Follow up the Projects

- To create the communication channels with the FinCo’s (Financial Coordinator) in the field and / or the rest of the team within the Financial Department of MAGNA, thus ensuring its correct functioning in coordination with the person in charge of the Operational Centre and his team.
- To provide the feedback, within a previously established timeframe, on financial issues to the teams in the field with the agreement of the corresponding responsible of the Operational Centre (so as to guarantee a coherent message shared with all the members of OC).
- To provide the OC Financial Analysis.
- Makes periodical follow-up visits to the countries of his/her responsibility.
- Carries out the administrative duties related to his job position.
- Ensure the Quality of the financial standards
- Supervises the budgetary follow-up and forecast (BFUF) of the project and controls its authorized limits.
- Coordinates the corresponding budgetary reviews and the budget forecast.
- Controls the levels of treasury on the field.
- Coordinates the preparation process of proposals and reports to the fund providers, ensuring the defined quality level.
- Carries out the follow-up of financing contracts (implementation levels, reportingschedules….)
- Carries out internal audits of the projects he/she is in charge of (from headquarters “insitu”/in the field).
- Collaborates in the annual accounting close-up.

1. Ensure Technical Training

- He/she will be responsible for coaching the Fincos in the field.
- He/she will ensure that the Fincos and Administrators receive technical training and basic methodology by means of PPD, briefings, debriefings and information sessions.

**SELECTION CRITERIA**
**Education and experience**

- Accountant and/or degree in Business Administration or proven experience in financial management and accounting field.
- Consolidated experience in accounting, budgetary, control and budget planning.
- Minimum one year work experience in developing countries related to accounting and planning, follow-up and project financial evaluations with MAGNA field or other NGOs field will be an asset.
- Fluent spoken and written English and French.
- IT skills
- SAGA
- Availability to travel frequently and on short notice.
- Flexibility with working hours.

**Competencies**

- Commitment to MAGNA’s Principles
- Cross-cultural Awareness
- Behavioural Flexibility
- Strategic Vision
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Service Orientation
- Planning and Organizing
- Initiative and Innovation
- Teamwork and Cooperation
- Leadership
- Security Awareness and Management

**CONDITIONS**

- Based in Prague with occasional visits to the field (2-3 times per year)
- Salary based on MAGNAs salary scale starting from 2 361 EUR brutto based on experience
- Full time job
- Contract duration: Open Ended Contract.
- Starting date: ASAP

Logistic Manager - Haiti
jobs.description:
Description

Lieu : Port au Prince, Haïti
Date souhaitée de démarrage : 1er Janvier 2027
Durée de contrat : 6 mois

Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI) est une association de solidarité internationale indépendante et impartiale, qui intervient dans les situations de pauvreté et d’exclusion, de conflits et de catastrophes. Œuvrant aux côtés des personnes handicapées et vulnérabilisées, elle agit et témoigne pour répondre à leurs besoins essentiels et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Elle s’engage à promouvoir le respect de leur dignité et de leurs droits fondamentaux.

Depuis sa création en 1982, HI a mis en place des programmes de développement dans plus de 55 pays et intervient dans de nombreuses situations d’urgence. Aujourd'hui, nous avons un budget d'environ 200 millions d'euros, avec 4000 employés dans le monde.

Chez Handicap International, nous croyons fermement en l'importance de l'inclusion et de la diversité au sein de notre structure. C'est pourquoi nous sommes engagés dans une politique handicap afin de favoriser l'accueil et l'intégration de personnes en situation de handicap.

Merci d’indiquer si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement particulier, y compris pour participer aux 1ers entretiens. Retrouvez plus d’informations sur l’association : .

CONTEXTE :
Présente en Haïti depuis 2008, l’organisation met en œuvre des projets sur les thématiques suivantes :

\- La réadaptation fonctionnelle

\- La défense des droits des personnes handicapées et l’inclusion

\- Les réponses d’urgence (Cholera, déplacés internes, Cyclones, Séismes, etc.).

Les projets sont mis en œuvre avec de nombreux partenaires locaux dont des organisations de personnes handicapées, dans les départements de l’Ouest, du bas Nord-Ouest, du Nord, du Nord-Est, du Sud et du Sud-Est. Deux bases opérationnelles sont situées à Port-au-Prince et aux Cayes (ouverture de la base dans le cadre de la réponse au séisme d’aout 2021).

HI Haïti avait un budget global de 5 millions d’euros en 2026. L’équipe est composée de 92 membres du personnel (7 internationaux et 85 nationaux). Le programme est financé par la Coopération Belge au développement (DGD), Affaires Mondiales Canada (GAC), le ministère des Affaires étrangères du Luxembourg, ECHO, UNICEF, entre autres. HI Haïti s'intégrera à partir de janvier 2027 dans la région de l'Amérique latine et des Caraïbes d’HI, en tant que pays affilié.

Cette intégration représente une étape significative dans la consolidation d’une région plus connectée, plus collaborative et plus en phase avec le mandat de HI : travailler ensemble pour construire des sociétés plus inclusives, avec des réponses programmatiques cohérentes, et garantir notre action auprès des communautés qui en ont le plus besoin. Pendant neuf mois, l’équipe d’HI dans la région, en Haïti, ainsi que les responsables au siège ont analysé, domaine par domaine, la situation actuelle des opérations d’HI dans le pays : ses points forts et les domaines à renforcer. La collaboration s’est avérée efficace, avec de nombreuses missions menées par des collègues haïtiens à Bogotá. Jusqu’à la fin de l’année, nous continuerons à mener des actions afin d’être prêts pour l’intégration en 2027 et le poste de Logistique Manager doit contribuer à cette réussite.

La mission d’HI en Haïti dispose d’une vaste expérience et de compétences solides, notamment dans les contextes d’urgence, où elle a démontré une grande capacité de réaction et d’adaptation face à des situations complexes.

La collaboration sera bidirectionnelle : Haïti apportera son expérience et ses compétences, tandis que la région mettra à disposition ses connaissances et ses ressources afin de favoriser un apprentissage mutuel et le développement d’initiatives conjointes.

VOTRE MISSION :
Sous la responsabilité du directeur pays et en collaboration avec les services du siège puis du superviseur logistique régional, vous, en tant que Logistics Manager, assurez la gestion efficiente des ressources logistiques pour le programme dont vous êtes responsable.

Vous êtes la personne de contact du directeur pays et, à ce titre, l'informez de tout problème et lui proposez des solutions dans son domaine de responsabilité.

Vous êtes un acteur clé dans le déploiement et la mise en œuvre des standards logistiques de HI, consistant en un remaniement du positionnement de la logistique chez HI et l'affirmation du principe de la filière métier.

Vos aurez notamment comme responsabilités :

1 - Le management

2 - La définition de la partie Logistique de la stratégie du programme et le pilotage du plan d’action afférent

3 - Le déploiement des standards, la contribution à l’expertise et à la redevabilité de HI

4 - La mise en œuvre opérationnelle Logistique

5 - L’animation de la filière métier logistique sur son programme et la contribution à l’évolution de la filière métier logistique de l’organisation

6 - La préparation et réponses aux urgences

SPECIFICITES/PARTICULARITES DU POSTE :

La situation sécuritaire étant volatile, des restrictions existent concernant les déplacements, la marche, la conduite, qui peuvent être révisées en fonction des événements. Malgré tout, les conditions de vie sont bonnes (restaurants, salles de sports, activités culturelles, etc.). Couvre-feu à 21h00 et zones de déplacement limitées. Aménagement fréquent des horaires du couvre-feu en fonction de la situation sécuritaire. Le logement est en appartement partagé avec un autre Personnel International, Internet en wifi.
Exigences

· Vous avez déjà des expériences avérées dans la formation et le transfert de compétences ainsi que dans l’écriture de procédures logistiques

· Vous possédez déjà des expériences management, vous savez faire progresser et développer l’autonomie de vos collaborateurs, vous savez vous positionner pour avancer, vous savez simplifier et prioriser

· Vous possédez les compétences métiers indispensables : maintenance, sûreté, planification, achats, approvisionnement, gestion des stocks et des transports

· Vous êtes à l’aise dans la veille, la réponse et la préparation aux urgences

· Vous êtes capable de travailler sous pression avec de multiples sollicitations et à gérer le stress

· Vous parlez couramment français et avez un niveau professionnel en anglais, la maîtrise de l’espagnol étant également apprécié dans le cadre de l’intégration avec la région LAC
Avantages

Chez HI, les conditions de départ sont à la hauteur de votre engagement et adaptées au contexte de votre mission. Une attention particulière est portée aux questions de santé et à votre situation personnelle :

· Contrat International de 6 mois à compter de début janvier 2027 basé à Port au Prince ;

· Le contrat international permet une couverture sociale adaptée aux besoins de chacun :

Assurance chômage prélevée uniquement pour les ressortissants de l’UE ;
Assurance retraite ;
Couverture santé, rapatriement, prévoyance prises en charge par HI et par l’employé ;

· Salaire : à partir de 2869 € brut/mois ;

· Perdiem : 1008 € net/mois – versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;

· Hardship : 500 € net/mois

· Congés payés : 25 jours par an ;

· R&R : selon niveau de la mission : 5 Jours toutes les 8 semaines

· Poste : Non accompagné :

o A partir de 12 mois de mission : une allocation enfant de 100 € versée à partir de 2 enfants à charge, versé en monnaie locale sur le terrain ;

· Logement : Collectif pris en charge par HI ;

· Si vous êtes résident(e) dans le pays : package local

· Si vous êtes de nationalité haïtienne vivant en dehors du pays et que vous souhaitez revenir travailler en Haïti (impatriation) : prime de 20% du salaire de base les 6 premiers mois de contrat, puis 10% sur le deuxième trimestre + support financier de 900 USD pour le retour en Haïti

Org. Setting and Reporting
UNRWA, the largest United Nations operation in the Middle East with over 25,000 staff working
across five areas of operation, is looking for highly committed personnel wishing to make a change.
If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most
vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.
The incumbent reports to the Deputy Commissioner General (Programmes & Partnerships).

Responsibilities
Develops Agency-wide impactful integrated communications tailored for external and internal target
audiences; such strategies will directly support UNRWA positioning and branding, advocacy, resource
mobilization and communication with Palestine refugees and UNRWA staff.
Leads, evaluates and regularly adjusts the implementation of external communications strategies,
including the production and promotion of impactful content through the Communications Division
and the communications teams across the Agency (fields and HQ programme departments).
Serves as the head of media relations and the Agency's chief spokesperson, thus managing a pool of
spokespersons in different languages, producing media lines, and managing the monitoring of media
pick-ups and reputational risks, and suggesting ways to address them. In doing so, advises the
Commissioner-General directly on his/her media engagement and strategy.
Drives excellence in digital engagement, aligning closely with UNRWA efforts to gain digital traction,
mirrors and supports digital engagement for fundraising; oversees the development, production and
dissemination of content for use on institutional portals (websites and corporate social media in
English and Arabic).
Responsible for adequate storage of institutional historical images and products (photo archives and
multimedia), and for ensuring their inclusion in Agency-wide measures to protect UNRWA's historic
archives.
Protects the Agency's reputation by ensuring high quality standards for all communications products
and activities, putting in place brand risk management plans as necessary. Leads efforts to combat
mis/disinformation, including tracking, verifying and when agreed within ERCD and /or with the
Executive Office, responding to unfounded claims. Ensures quality control of all communications
products, in line with the corporate visual identity, corporate lexicon, and stylistic guidelines, and
clears materials including accurate Arabic translation - before publication or sharing with the
Executive Office.
Represents the Agency externally within the UN through the UN Global Communications Group and
provides communications support and dissemination of information about UNRWA to, UN agencies,
INGOs, and other stakeholders; collaborates closely with and provides strategic support to the various
functional units in the External Relations and Communications Department (ERCD) the Executive
Office (EO), and Representative Offices in their resource mobilization efforts and general outreach.
Leads and builds the capacity of a team of professional staff in the Communications Division and in
field offices to maximize impact; develops and monitors the implementation of annual operational
plans for the Communications Division and manages its resources, ensuring strategic alignment of
Agency-wide communications efforts.

Competencies
UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of

Functional
i. Adapting and Responding to Change
ii. Formulating Strategies and Concepts
iii. Persuading and influencing

i. Leading and Supervising

first level university degree in the specified fields of study, in combination with two additional years
of relevant work experience, may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.
\- Coursework or training in press relations management.

information and communication issues, including direct involvement with the international media and
the regional media, in a senior capacity is required. A first level university degree in the specified
fields of study, in combination with two additional years of relevant work experience, may be accepted
in lieu of the advanced university degree.

A strong public speaker and writer, able to articulate complex problems while generating support
among target audiences. Experience in crisis communication and strategies linked thereof is required.

Experience in general management and international relations, in management a diverse team of
professionals is required.
Experience as a journalist, editor or in publishing is required.

UNRWA, and outside the country(s) of which the candidate is a national or holds citizenship, a

Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

ACTIVITY MANAGERS (NAME AND POSITION) Emmeline Da Silva (Communications Manager) and Sandrine Désiré (RegionalProject Manager)

PLANNED PERIOD / DATES 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2027

## 1. CONTEXT AND RATIONALE

**1.1 PIRAC**
Established in 2005, PIRAC (Regional Intervention Platform for the Americas and the Caribbean) is the representative delegation of the French Red Cross (FRC) for the Caribbean region, based in Guadeloupe. It is also the operational mechanism through which the French Red Cross implements humanitarian action and regional cooperation in the Caribbean.

PIRAC provides support to populations affected by major disasters across the Caribbean and works to strengthen the resilience and preparedness capacities of populations in the French territories and countries of the Caribbean arc.

**1.2 THE READY 360° / 3 OCEANS PROGRAMME**

The **READY 360° / 3 Oceans programme** aims to build more comprehensive and greener resilience across Caribbean territories by strengthening disaster preparedness and response capacities at all levels, from individuals and families, to organisations and businesses, and up to regional institutional coordination for disaster risk management.

The programme's institutional partners are the **Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States (OECS)** and the **Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency (CDEMA).**

Eight Caribbean territories are involved in the programme:

- Antigua and Barbuda;
- Dominica;
- Grenada;
- Guadeloupe;
- Martinique;
- Saint Kitts and Nevis;
- Saint Lucia
- Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

One of the expected outcomes of the programme is to contribute to strengthening the resilience of Caribbean citizens through improved information, awareness and preparedness for disasters and crises.

To this end, several activities have been implemented to strengthen risk awareness and the resilience of Caribbean populations to natural hazards and the impacts of climate change, by ensuring the broad dissemination of disaster risk awareness messages and increasing the visibility of tools developed under the READY 360° / 3 Oceans programme.

These activities include the regional awareness campaign **"It's Your Move!"** and the regional **Caribbean Risks** portal. The It's Your Move! campaign uses a range of awareness-raising materials, including infographics, testimonial videos and posters, to make preparedness messages accessible and relevant to Caribbean populations. These materials are available in French and English.

The Caribbean Risks portal was developed as a regional reference resource for the general public. It brings together reliable, accessible information adapted to the realities of Caribbean territories, with the aim of informing, raising awareness and helping citizens prepare for the main natural hazards to which they are exposed. TV and radio awareness spots are also currently being produced and are scheduled for broadcast in November/December.

**1.3 THE AWARENESS-RAISING SONG**
As part of the awareness campaign, a regional song dedicated to natural hazard prevention is being produced in collaboration with S.Rise, a Caribbean artist (biography in the appendix).

Performed in English, Creole and French and combining dancehall and amapiano influences, the song conveys messages about natural hazards, the importance of communities, preparedness and the need to take action in response to disasters and the effects of climate change. Moving away from the usual codes of prevention campaigns, the song uses music as a different way of conveying these messages. It is a genuine artistic proposition designed to reach audiences without taking the form of an institutional message.

An official music video accompanies the release of the song and is directed by Dimitry Zandronis (biography in the appendix).

A choreography will also be associated with the song, supported by collaborations with Caribbean micro-influencers and content creators to encourage the song’s circulation and uptake on social media.

The song and its music video are awareness-raising tools in their own right, designed to reach a broad audience through a popular cultural format.

The purpose of this tender is to maximise the visibility of the song and music video in Caribbean media, particularly on radio stations and television channels, in order to reach the population as widely as possible.

1. OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

In summary: to secure as many broadcasts of the song and music video as possible across the eight territories, prioritising free broadcasts (earned media) while securing a proportion of broadcasts through a dedicated purchasing budget.

The assignment shall notably aim to:

- Secure broadcasts of the song on selected radio stations;
- Obtain broadcasts of the music video on relevant television channels;
- Identify and engage music programmers and broadcasters likely to feature the content voluntarily;
- Identify additional opportunities for interviews or appearances by the artist and project representatives on radio and TV programmes;
- Identify and develop partnerships with radio stations and/or television channels, which may include launch support, enhanced programming or regular promotion of the song and music video;
- Use the purchasing budget to fund or support broadcasts (see Section 6), in addition to media relations
activities.

## 3. BALANCE BETWEEN EDITORIAL COVERAGE AND PAID ADVERTISING

The strategy shall prioritise editorial coverage and unpaid broadcasts (earned media), drawing on the service provider’s network and relationships with local and regional media. This approach aims to encourage the song and music video to be included organically in radio and television programming, while also identifying opportunities for partnerships with broadcasters.

However, as such coverage depends on media editorial decisions, it cannot be guaranteed. The service provider shall therefore also propose a complementary paid advertising strategy to secure a proportion of broadcasts and strengthen coverage across the target territories.

1. GEOGRAPHICAL SCOPE AND LOT STRUCTURE

The tender is divided into two geographical lots. Both lots include the same services and differ only in their geographical scope.

LOT 1 – Guadeloupe and Martinique
The service provider shall promote and secure distribution of the song and music video in:

- Guadeloupe
- Martinique

LOT 2 – English-speaking Caribbean
The service provider shall promote and secure distribution of the song and music video in the following six territories:

- Antigua and Barbuda
- Dominica
- Grenada
- Saint Kitts and Nevis
- Saint Lucia
- Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Applicants may bid for one lot or both lots, provided they demonstrate their ability to deliver the services within the relevant geographical scope.

Coverage of all territories included in the lot for which the applicant is bidding is an essential requirement.

Subcontracting and joint bidding (consortium) are permitted, particularly to ensure coverage of all territories in Lot 2. In such cases, the proposal shall specify the lead partner, each partner’s role and the territories covered by each. The lead partner shall remain PIRAC’s sole point of contact.

1. SERVICES EXPECTED

For each lot, the service provider shall propose and implement a promotional strategy tailored to the media landscape of the territories concerned.

**5.1 DEVELOPMENT OF THE MEDIA STRATEGY**

The service provider shall:

- Analyse the radio and television landscape in the territories concerned;
- Identify priority radio stations, television channels, programmes and music programmers;
- Develop a strategy combining paid advertising with outreach to broadcasters to secure voluntary programming;
- Propose a broadcast schedule aligned with the release of the song and music video;
- Identify opportunities for media partnerships or collaborations.

Particular attention will be paid to the service provider’s ability to mobilise an existing network of contacts within radio stations and television channels.

**5.2 RADIO PROMOTION AND BROADCASTING**

Radio broadcasting is a priority component of the assignment.

The service provider shall:

- Identify relevant radio stations and TV channels in each territory;
- Negotiate paid advertising or any other paid arrangement that can secure broadcasts of the song, in line with each media outlet’s local practices (see Section 6);
- Approach music programmers and DJs to encourage the song’s voluntary inclusion in playlists and programmes;
- Arrange delivery of the song and the information required for its programming;
- Monitor broadcasts and manage relationships with broadcasters.

Applicants shall specify the radio stations targeted, the proposed broadcasting arrangements and the estimated number of plays they expect to secure, distinguishing between paid broadcasts and free editorial broadcasts. For free broadcasts, a reasoned estimate will be sufficient.

**5.3 TV PROMOTION AND BROADCASTING**

The service provider shall:

- Identify television channels and programmes likely to broadcast the music video;
- Propose paid advertising or any other paid arrangement to secure broadcasts of the music video, where relevant;
- Approach channels and programming managers to encourage free editorial broadcasts;
- Monitor the broadcasts secured.

Applicants shall specify the channels targeted, the proposed broadcasting arrangements and the proposed number of broadcasts, distinguishing between paid broadcasts and free editorial broadcasts. For free broadcasts, a reasoned estimate will be sufficient.

**5.4 ADDITIONAL PROMOTIONAL OPPORTUNITIES**

The service provider shall identify and propose opportunities for interviews or appearances by the artist, the music video director or project representatives on radio and television programmes.

These appearances will complement the broadcasting of the song and music video. They will notably provide an opportunity to present the project led by PIRAC, explain the approach behind this initiative and raise public awareness of the importance of understanding natural hazards and adopting appropriate protective actions.

They may also provide an opportunity to introduce the Caribbean Risks portal, which offers clear, reliable and up-to date information to help people better understand risks and prepare for them.

Interviews may be conducted remotely. The artist, director and PIRAC team will only be able to travel in person within Guadeloupe.

**5.5 PROMOTIONAL MATERIALS**

PIRAC will provide the service provider with the final audio and video files of the song and music video.

The press kit / EPK will be developed by PIRAC. The service provider may make recommendations to adapt or optimise this material to meet the expectations of the target media.

The service provider may also make recommendations regarding additional presentation materials to be shared with the media, as well as the provision of documents such as a letter of assignment.

1. BUDGET AND BROADCASTING OBJECTIVES

The indicative budget available for purchasing advertising space is between EUR 8,000 and EUR 12,000 for both
lots combined.

This budget will be allocated as follows: 60% to Lot 1 (Guadeloupe and Martinique, due to media costs) and 40% to Lot 2 (English-speaking Caribbean), i.e. approximately EUR 4,800 to EUR 7,200 for Lot 1 and EUR 3,200 to EUR 4,800 for Lot 2.

This budget does not include the service provider’s fees. No budget envelope has been specified for fees : each applicant shall include its fees in its financial proposal, clearly separate from the media purchasing budget. How the media purchasing budget will work: the purchasing budget is intended to secure additional broadcasts of the song and music video, alongside free broadcasts. Sales practices vary between media sales houses and outlets (advertising spots, sponsorship, paid programming or other arrangements). For each media outlet, the service provider shall propose the arrangement it considers most appropriate. Each purchase must be supported by proof of payment (invoice, signed quotation or insertion order), together with a broadcast log or broadcast certificate. The service provider shall be responsible for making payments for media purchases.

Applicants shall prioritise a strategy that maximises the number of broadcasts and geographical coverage, taking into account the earned media strategy and the available budget.

Paid broadcasts and free editorial broadcasts must be clearly distinguished. The latter cannot be guaranteed, as programming decisions are made by the broadcasters.

## 7. PROVISIONAL TIMELINE

The song and music video are scheduled for release on 11 January 2027.
Stage : Indicative period
Campaign scoping and preparation : December 2026 – early January 2027
Song and music video release : 11 January 2027
Main promotion and broadcasting : : January – February 2027
Broadcast monitoring and evaluation : Late February 2027

The service provider shall propose an operational schedule specifying broadcast periods, key milestones and monitoring arrangements.

## 8. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES

For each lot, the expected deliverables are:

1\. Media plan and broadcasting strategy

- Target media and broadcasters by territory;
- Proposed balance between editorial broadcasts and paid advertising;
- Estimated broadcast volumes and budget;
- Operational schedule.

2\. Campaign monitoring

- Tracking table of media contacted and negotiations;
- Monitoring of purchases and programming secured;
- Record of broadcasts actually delivered, by media outlet and territory.

3\. Final report

- Summary of activities carried out and broadcasts secured;
- Clear distinction between paid and free broadcasts;
- Number of broadcasts delivered and available audience figures;
- Any discrepancies between planned and actual broadcasts.

1. COORDINATION WITH PIRAC

The service provider shall work in close coordination with PIRAC’s Communications team.
In particular, the service provider shall:

- Attend a kick-off meeting at the start of the assignment;
- Submit the media plan and schedule for approval;
- Keep PIRAC regularly informed of the progress of negotiations and broadcasts;
- Promptly report any difficulty or change that may affect the campaign;
- Provide available proof of broadcast.

PIRAC will oversee the overall coordination of the assignment and remain the point of contact for approvals and
decisions.

1. SERVICE PROVIDER PROFILE

The service provider shall have:

- Demonstrable experience in music promotion and/or media planning and media buying;
- An established network of contacts with radio stations, music programmers and television channels in the territories concerned;
- Good knowledge of the local media landscape;
- The ability to negotiate broadcasting arrangements and secure editorial programming;
- The ability to work in French and/or English, depending on the lot concerned.

For Lot 2, knowledge of the six English-speaking territories concerned and the ability to mobilise a regional network will be particularly valued. These skills may be brought together through a consortium or subcontracting arrangements (see Section 4).

1. SELECTION CRITERIA

Criteria : Indicative weighting

Relevance of the strategy and understanding of the objectives : 30%

Experience and references in music promotion and media broadcasting : 15%

Quality and reach of the media and programmer network that can be mobilised : 15%

Timeline : 10%

Price / value for money : 30%
TOTAL 100%

The quality of the network will be assessed based on the media outlets and programmers the service provider can actually access, rather than solely on the number of contacts claimed.

12\. OWNERSHIP OF DELIVERABLES

Documents, tools and deliverables produced as part of the assignment may be used by the READY 360° / 3
Oceans programme and its partners for their communication and awareness-raising activities.

Rights relating to the song, music video and associated content are governed by the agreements concluded with
the relevant rights holders. The service provider shall comply with the terms of use and distribution communicated by PIRAC.

1. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Applicants shall submit a proposal including the following:

- Service provider presentation (Table 1)
- Presentation of the organisation and the team assigned to the project (Table 1);
- Two to three relevant references in music promotion and media broadcasting (Table 1);
- Experience in the territory or territories concerned;
- Presentation of the media and programmer network that can be mobilised (Table 2).
- Applicants may use the following tables to prepare their response:

Technical proposal

- The proposed methodology for prioritising media relations activities and securing unpaid editorial broadcasts before, if necessary, using additional paid advertising;
- The media outlets and broadcasters targeted in each territory, together with estimated broadcast volumes, clearly distinguishing between the editorial coverage sought and broadcasts that can be guaranteed through paid advertising;
- How the purchasing strategy will be adjusted in response to media feedback and identified editorial
broadcasting opportunities;
- The estimated budget for the proposed advertising purchases;
- Operational schedule;
- Monitoring and reporting arrangements.

Financial proposal

- Breakdown of fees and service-related costs;
- Budget allocated to radio and TV advertising purchases;
- Costs and broadcast volumes by territory and media outlet;
- Total proposed amount.
- Applicants bidding for both lots shall submit a separate financial proposal for each lot, specifying thenallocation of the overall available budget.

1. LISTENING TO THE SONG AS PART OF THE TENDER PROCESS

As the song has not yet been registered with SACEM, it cannot be freely distributed. To enable applicants to prepare a proposal without having listened to the song, the information required to assess the title is provided in Section 1.3 and Appendix 1 (biographies).

The song may be shared with applicants who wish to listen to it before submitting their technical proposal, so that they can assess the track and evaluate their interest in and ability to promote it to the media.

To access the song, applicants must request it by email from PIRAC and attach the confidentiality agreement included in the appendix to these Terms of Reference, duly completed and signed (electronic signatures are accepted).

The track is provided solely for listening purposes in connection with this tender. Any distribution, reproduction or sharing with third parties is prohibited.
