jobs.title: Venezuela: Coordinador/a de Apoyo Técnico (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Medialuna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales (Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad) la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

- El/La Coordinador(a) de Apoyo Técnico será responsable de brindar apoyo técnico y programático a la Delegación de la Cruz Roja Alemana en Venezuela para fortalecer la calidad del diseño, implementación, monitoreo y seguimiento de los proyectos humanitarios desarrollados en coordinación con la Cruz Roja Venezolana y otros socios del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja.
- El cargo contribuirá al fortalecimiento de la gestión basada en resultados mediante el acompañamiento técnico a los equipos de implementación, el análisis de información programática, la elaboración de documentos técnicos, el desarrollo de herramientas de monitoreo y evaluación, la realización de análisis de necesidades y contexto, y la generación de evidencia para apoyar la toma de decisiones.
- Asimismo, apoyará la planificación estratégica, el desarrollo de nuevas propuestas, la identificación de oportunidades de mejora, el fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales y la articulación entre las diferentes áreas programáticas, promoviendo una implementación integrada y de alta calidad de los proyectos, especialmente en los sectores de salud, gestión del riesgo de desastres y preparación para emergencias.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:
- Brindar apoyo técnico y programático a la Coordinación de Programas de la Cruz Roja Alemana para fortalecer la calidad del diseño, implementación, seguimiento, evaluación y cierre de los proyectos ejecutados en coordinación con la Cruz Roja Venezolana y otros socios del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja.
- Acompañar técnicamente a los equipos de implementación durante el desarrollo de actividades en terreno, realizando visitas de seguimiento, identificando oportunidades de mejora y promoviendo el cumplimiento de los estándares técnicos, operativos y de calidad establecidos por la Cruz Roja Alemana y los donantes.
- Liderar o apoyar la realización de análisis de contexto, evaluaciones de necesidades, análisis de brechas y estudios técnicos que orienten la formulación, implementación y adaptación de los proyectos.
- Contribuir al diseño técnico de nuevas propuestas de proyectos, marcos lógicos, teorías de cambio, planes operativos, indicadores y metodologías de implementación, de acuerdo con los lineamientos institucionales y los requisitos de los donantes.
- Coordinar el desarrollo, actualización e implementación de herramientas de planificación, monitoreo, evaluación, aprendizaje y aseguramiento de la calidad, promoviendo una gestión basada en resultados.
- Analizar información programática y operacional para apoyar la toma de decisiones, identificar tendencias, riesgos, brechas y oportunidades de mejora en la implementación de los proyectos.
- Diseñar, desarrollar y mantener tableros de control, bases de datos y herramientas de análisis utilizando Power BI, Excel u otras plataformas institucionales que faciliten el seguimiento de indicadores, resultados y avances programáticos.
- Coordinar la recopilación, validación, consolidación y análisis de información proveniente de los equipos de implementación, garantizando la calidad, consistencia, trazabilidad y disponibilidad de los datos para la gestión y la toma de decisiones.
- Apoyar la elaboración, revisión y control de calidad de informes narrativos para donantes, informes técnicos, reportes de avance, presentaciones ejecutivas, documentos estratégicos, estudios de caso, lecciones aprendidas y otros productos de gestión del conocimiento.
- Apoyar la preparación y coordinación de visitas de seguimiento, misiones técnicas, auditorías, evaluaciones externas, revisiones de proyectos y visitas de donantes, asegurando la disponibilidad de información técnica y documental.
- Promover el fortalecimiento de capacidades del personal y voluntariado mediante procesos de capacitación, asistencia técnica y acompañamiento en gestión de proyectos, monitoreo y evaluación, análisis de información, estándares humanitarios y gestión basada en resultados.
- Facilitar la articulación técnica entre las áreas de Salud, Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres, WASH, Logística, PMER y otras áreas involucradas en la implementación de los proyectos, promoviendo un enfoque programático integrado.
- Apoyar el desarrollo y actualización de procedimientos operativos, lineamientos técnicos, metodologías, herramientas y documentos institucionales que contribuyan a la estandarización y mejora continua de las intervenciones.
- Participar en ejercicios de aprendizaje institucional, revisiones posteriores a operaciones (After Action Reviews), evaluaciones en tiempo real (Real-Time Evaluations), procesos de capitalización de experiencias y otras iniciativas orientadas a fortalecer la calidad programática.
- Promover la incorporación transversal de los enfoques de protección, género e inclusión, participación comunitaria y rendición de cuentas hacia las poblaciones afectadas (CEA/AAP), acción climática, sostenibilidad ambiental y principios de “No Hacer Daño” en todas las fases del ciclo del proyecto.
- Mantener una coordinación técnica permanente con la Cruz Roja Venezolana para fortalecer la calidad y coherencia de las implementaciones.
- Asegurar el cumplimiento de los Principios Fundamentales del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja, el Código de Conducta, las políticas institucionales, los lineamientos de protección de datos, salvaguarda, seguridad y demás normativas aplicables durante la ejecución de sus funciones.
- Ejecutar otras funciones asignadas por la Coordinación de Programas de la Cruz Roja Alemana, acordes con la naturaleza del cargo y las necesidades operativas de la Delegación.

*Reporte*

El/La Coordinador Apoyo Técnico le reportará a la Coordinación de Programas.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas (Sede central de la Cruz Roja Venezolana), con disponibilidad para viajar a nivel nacional.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Título universitario en Ingeniería Industrial, Ingeniería de Procesos, Ingeniería de Sistemas, Ingeniería Ambiental, Estadística, Economía, Administración, Relaciones Internacionales, Sociología, Ciencia Política, Geografía, Desarrollo Internacional, Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres, Salud Pública u otras carreras afines.
- Experiencia mínima de cinco (5) años en la planificación, implementación, monitoreo, evaluación o coordinación de programas o proyectos humanitarios, de desarrollo o cooperación internacional.
- Experiencia demostrable en el diseño, implementación, seguimiento y evaluación de proyectos, preferiblemente en uno o más de los siguientes sectores: salud, gestión del riesgo de desastres, preparación para emergencias, fortalecimiento institucional, resiliencia comunitaria, WASH, protección o recuperación temprana.
- Experiencia en la realización de análisis de contexto, evaluaciones de necesidades, análisis de brechas, gestión de información y elaboración de recomendaciones técnicas para la toma de decisiones.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en metodologías de gestión basada en resultados (RBM), monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y aprendizaje (MEAL/PMER), incluyendo el desarrollo de indicadores, marcos lógicos, planes de monitoreo y herramientas de seguimiento.
- Experiencia en la elaboración y revisión de informes técnicos, informes narrativos para donantes, documentos estratégicos, presentaciones ejecutivas, sistematización de experiencias y otros productos de gestión del conocimiento.
- Experiencia en el diseño y formulación de propuestas de proyectos para donantes institucionales y en la revisión técnica de documentos programáticos será considerada una ventaja.
- Manejo avanzado de Microsoft Excel y experiencia en herramientas de análisis y visualización de datos como Power BI. Se valorará el conocimiento de plataformas de recolección y gestión de información como KoboToolbox, ODK, Survey123 u otras similares.
- Capacidad para analizar información cuantitativa y cualitativa, interpretar resultados y generar recomendaciones orientadas a fortalecer la calidad de los proyectos y la toma de decisiones.
- Experiencia acompañando técnicamente equipos multidisciplinarios y realizando visitas de seguimiento en terreno para fortalecer la implementación y el cumplimiento de estándares de calidad.
- Conocimiento de los estándares humanitarios internacionales, incluyendo el Manual Esfera, los enfoques de Protección, Género e Inclusión (PGI), Participación Comunitaria y Rendición de Cuentas hacia las Comunidades (CEA), protección de datos y el principio de "No Hacer Daño".
- Experiencia trabajando con organizaciones del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja o con organismos internacionales y organizaciones humanitarias será altamente valorada.
- Conocimiento del contexto humanitario venezolano, de los mecanismos nacionales de coordinación y de la arquitectura humanitaria del país será considerado una ventaja.
- Dominio de herramientas ofimáticas y plataformas colaborativas para la gestión de proyectos, seguimiento programático y elaboración de productos técnicos.
- Dominio del idioma español, con excelentes habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita. Se valorará el dominio del idioma inglés para la elaboración de documentos técnicos y la interacción con socios y donantes internacionales.
- Excelentes habilidades analíticas, de planificación, organización, coordinación, facilitación y redacción técnica, con capacidad para gestionar múltiples prioridades y trabajar en equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión, adaptarse a contextos cambiantes, realizar misiones al terreno y mantener altos estándares de calidad, confidencialidad, seguridad y responsabilidad institucional.
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja, el Código de Conducta y las políticas institucionales.
- Alto sentido de responsabilidad, pensamiento crítico, iniciativa, ética profesional, orientación a resultados y capacidad para trabajar de manera autónoma.

jobs.title: Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships
jobs.description:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Background/Overview:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) helps people affected by humanitarian crises to survive, recover and rebuild their lives. The Airbel Impact Lab is the research and innovation arm of the IRC. Airbel designs, tests, and scales cost-effective solutions for people affected by conflict and disaster, from new tools and technologies to cost analysis and rigorous research on what works. To keep innovating and deliver on its annual operating budget of about $25 million, Airbel relies on flexible private funding as well as project funding for impact and cost evidence generation in areas such as nutrition and immunization.

We are seeking a Senior Officer, Research & Innovation Partnerships to help raise this funding. This role supports the IRC’s high-value fundraising teams, who work with major individual donors, corporate partners, and foundations, to secure funding for research and innovation (R&I). It also helps Airbel put its work in front of the right donors without pulling the Airbel team away from their core work. You will turn technical findings into compelling, accurate donor-facing material, guide each opportunity from first lead to proposal submission, and keep both sides informed as awards are delivered.

**Major Responsibilities:**

You will work alongside the IRC’s high-value fundraisers, Airbel innovation project leads and researchers, program and technical experts, and finance and support teams to raise the profile of, and increase private funding for, the IRC’s research and innovation work. This role coordinates and connects technical expertise from Airbel’s experts with donor strategy and relationships led by fundraisers. Your job is to make sure both teams have what they need, when they need it, and to own the quality of what is produced along the way.

The major responsibilities will include:

**Turn research and innovation into donor-ready content (30%)**

- Draft donor-facing materials in partnership with Airbel teams, including pitch decks, one-pagers, briefing notes, and proposal narratives, tailored to each audience (individual philanthropists, corporate partners, foundations and trusts) so that what reaches reviewers is close to final rather than a blank template.
- Get involved at the start of each product, helping decide whether the audience needs a punchy high-level pitch or deeper technical content and shaping a clear outline, and at the end, rewriting dense technical content for external readers and polishing the final format.
- Build clear, evidence-based arguments that read as both visionary and grounded, using facts and figures accurately and without losing what is actually true about the work.
- Help fundraisers and Airbel leaders position Airbel’s funding priorities (core funding, pooled funds, and project funding) with the donors most likely to care about each, and shape project ideas and funding pitches that are ready for donor conversations.

**Share knowledge and build the pipeline (20%)**

- Be the fundraisers’ go-to source for what is happening in R&I right now: innovation opportunities, evidence generation priorities, project milestones, funding needs, and results worth sharing. Give fundraisers a heads-up on wins or risks before important donor conversations.
- Maintain and regularly update the tracker of private funding opportunities and awards for R&I, and flag new opportunities as soon as they are identified.
- Pass donor interest, feedback, and trends back to Airbel so teams know where to focus their pitch and proposal effort next.
- Support donor mapping, targeting, and briefings for R&I prospects, and help fundraisers track donor activity and progress toward revenue goals, including linkages with the organizations Impact at Scale funding priorities and other strategic initiatives.
- Work with Airbel leaders and fundraisers on strategy and pipeline development for priority areas, such as cost analysis, evidence generation, and innovative approaches that are ready to scale.
- Stay current on developments in humanitarian research and innovation, and on trends in private philanthropy, to inform fundraising efforts.

**Manage opportunities and proposals from first lead to submission (30%)**

- Run the go/no-go process (the decision on whether to pursue an opportunity) for R&I-linked funding opportunities: gather what the fundraiser knows about the gift, such as its value, timeline, donor restrictions, and likelihood; present it to Airbel in a format that supports a quick, clear decision; and start the internal approval workflow once a decision is made.
- Project-manage private donor proposals and reports from start to finish, including timelines, reviewers, and inputs from program, finance, and technical teams. Take ownership of content quality and the overall outcome, not just the workplan and reminders.
- Check draft proposals, budgets, and agreements against donor and IRC requirements before they go to the fundraiser, and confirm that internal approvals, waivers, and sign-offs happen at each stage so nothing stalls further down the line.
- Coordinate answers to donor questions and any revisions after a proposal is submitted. As needed, join donor meetings to provide technical expertise and strategy support.
- Ensure strong coordination with other Program Services team members and program units for decision-making and shared workflows on complex cross-departmental or multisectoral proposals

**Connect teams, improve how we work, and support active grants (20%)**

- Connect the right people at the right time. When a donor question, pitch, or site visit comes up, quickly route fundraisers to the right Airbel colleague, and route Airbel colleagues to the right fundraiser, setting up direct conversations between program leads and account managers rather than acting as a go-between. Help prepare Airbel colleagues for donor meetings.
- Help develop and document simple, clear ways of working between fundraising and Airbel teams, such as when each side should expect to hear from or update the other, and coordinate effective cross-team meetings with timely follow-up on decisions.
- For active awards, work with Airbel teams and fundraisers to track implementation and spending, and flag risks, delays, or amendment needs early. Coordinate reporting inputs and amendment documentation so donor reports are timely and high quality.
- Contribute to long-term donor relationships by ensuring donor requirements and compliance obligations are met throughout the life of a grant.
- Work closely with other Program Services team members to ensure ways of working for R&I fundraising are aligned with those of other departments such as Crisis Response, Recovery, and Development (CRRD), Resettlement, Asylum and Integration (RAI), et al.

**Essential Qualifications:**

- 6-7 years of related work experience in fundraising, partnerships, program development, or communications, preferably with a mission-driven organization
- Experience contributing directly to securing multi-million-dollar funding for evidence generation, innovation, or other technical programming, including with private philanthropy, such as major donors, corporate partners, or foundations,
- Outstanding writing skills, with a demonstrated ability to quickly get up to speed on technical content and turn highly technical or research content into clear, compelling material for non-expert audiences (a writing sample may be requested).
- Experience managing complex proposals, grants, or similar projects from start to finish, with a track record of delivering high-quality results under tight deadlines
- Experience with fundraising and grants management processes, including budgets, donor requirements, and reporting
- Excellent relationship management and communication skills, including the ability to build trust and influence senior colleagues without direct authority over them
- Experience working across diverse contexts with global, cross-cultural teams, including collaborating remotely

**Desired Qualifications:**

- Familiarity with how social innovation, evidence generation, or cost-effectiveness analysis is used in humanitarian or global development work
- Experience with customer relationship management (CRM) or pipeline tracking tools
- Knowledge of other IRC languages (Spanish, French, Arabic) would be an asset
- We strongly encourage applications from candidates who have lived experience in the contexts where the IRC operates

**Working Environment:**

This role may require working remotely, and occasional travel. If remote, applicants must have a home or alternate workspace they can effectively complete their work from during regularly scheduled hours.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $93,000-$106,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Mission France - Superviseur·euse d'activité Approvisionnement - Littoral Nord
jobs.description:
La mission France recherche un.e Superviseur·euse d'activité Approvisionnement - Littoral Nord

**CONTEXTE**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et l’Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**MISSION**

Sous la responsabilité du·de la Responsable Logistique et Approvisionnement, vous organisez et coordonnez les achats, les commandes, les stocks et les livraisons nécessaires au bon fonctionnement des activités du projet.
Votre défi : garantir la disponibilité des ressources au bon moment, au bon endroit, tout en optimisant les coûts, les délais et la qualité.

**Vos principales responsabilités**

**Organiser les commandes et anticiper les besoins**

- Centraliser, traiter et suivre les demandes d'approvisionnement des équipes.
- Anticiper les besoins en consommables et assurer un suivi régulier des commandes et des livraisons.

**Piloter les achats et les relations fournisseurs**

- Organiser les achats dans le respect des procédures MSF et des budgets.
- Identifier et évaluer les fournisseurs, négocier les meilleures conditions de qualité, de prix et de délai.
- Assurer le suivi des contrats et contribuer à l'amélioration des pratiques d'achat, en lien avec les équipes financières.

**Garantir une gestion fiable des stocks**

- Superviser les réceptions, le stockage, les inventaires et les livraisons.
- Anticiper les réapprovisionnements pour prévenir les ruptures et les surstocks.
- Proposer des améliorations pour renforcer l'efficacité de la chaîne d'approvisionnement.

**Contribuer au bon fonctionnement des activités terrain**

- Organiser les transports de marchandises et garantir leur traçabilité.
- Apporter un appui logistique aux activités mobiles et aux interventions sur le Littoral Nord.
- Participer à l'amélioration des outils et procédures d'approvisionnement, en collaboration avec les équipes du projet.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience**

- Diplôme de technicien·ne en chaîne d'approvisionnement ou formation équivalente.
- Première expérience de 1 à 2 ans dans les achats, la logistique ou la gestion des stocks.
- Une expérience dans le secteur humanitaire ou associatif constitue un atout.

**Compétences et qualités**

- Excellentes capacités d'organisation, de planification et d'anticipation.
- Rigueur, autonomie et sens du service aux équipes.
- Aisance dans les relations fournisseurs et capacité à rechercher des solutions.
- Esprit d'équipe, réactivité et adaptabilité dans un environnement opérationnel évolutif.
- Adhésion aux principes et aux valeurs de MSF.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise obligatoire du français et de l'anglais.
- Bonne maîtrise des outils bureautiques, notamment Excel et Word.
- Permis B obligatoire

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

**Statut non-cadre :** CDD de 12 mois.

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 106,23 €** brut mensuels sur 13 mois
- Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir :** 11 janvier 2027

*En raison de contraintes administratives liées à la durée du contrat, les candidats doivent déjà disposer d'une autorisation de travail en France (citoyen de l'Union européenne) ou d’un titre de séjour leur permettant de travailler sur le sol français.*

jobs.title: Medical Officer Cell 1 (f/m/x) - Brussels - MSF Belgium
jobs.description:
**CONTEXT**

The Operations Department of MSF OCB (Operational Centre Brussels) consists of 6 managerial and technical teams known asl Cell. Each cell manages a portfolio of countries and 1 Emergency Team (E-Pool) which manages major emergency interventions. These teams directly supervise and support project implementation.

Based in Brussels, the cell is expected to manage a portfolio focusing mainly on Central Africa, including the **Democratic Republic of Congo, Burundi, the Central African Republic and Sierra Leone**. (after the finalization of transfer of portfolio between Cell 1 and 2 finalized in March 2026). The countries listed are indicative, as a re-shuffling of the portfolio within the Operations department occurs regularly.

As a **Medical Officer**, you play a key role in ensuring the medical quality of the cell's projects. You support the Medical Coordinators, maintain an overview of medical activities across the portfolio, and contribute to project preparation and implementation. Your responsibilities cover the cell’s entire portfolio and are not linked to one specific country or context, unless otherwise agreed with the Deputy Coordinator of Operations.

You report to the cell’s Deputy Coordinator of Operations and have a functional reporting line to the Operational Deputy Medical Director in the Medical Department.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

The core purpose of the role is to enhance and optimize the operational support and guidance for projects, ensuring quality-of-care standards are achievable and adapted to each context.

**Strategy Implementation Planning**

- Co-develop the implementation plan for the Medical Operations strategy with the medical coordination teams and the DepCO
- Provide strategic input, leadership, and guidance to ensure plans are practical, achievable, and aligned with the medical priorities within the countries of intervention, in coordination with the DepCO

**Strategic Oversight and Monitoring**

- Monitor and follow up on the implementation of the medical strategy across all relevant projects, providing regular and ad hoc support to the medical coordination teams

**Project Implementation**

- Support Medical Coordinators in monitoring and implementing projects, in coordination with the DepCO
- Provide ad hoc support as needed and ensure that Medical Coordinators have the necessary resources and assistance, in agreement with the DepCO

**Policies and Guidelines Management**

- Ensure that medical resources, policies, and guidelines are relevant, appropriate, available, and effectively managed in the countries of intervention
- Coordinate regularly with medical referents to ensure that policies, guidelines and guidance are adapted to medical operations and to each project’s specific context and objectives.

**Quality of Care (QoC) implementation**

- Ensure and actively monitor the implementation of Quality of Care (QoC) standards and improvement plans across all projects
- Guide the medical teams in the programmes to develop and enforce quality monitoring and improvement initiatives

**Medical Activity Analysis**

- Monitor and analyse medical activities and promote data-driven decision-making in collaboration with the DepCO
- Review and analyse medical reports and data, provide constructive feedback, and involve the relevant medical referent when required.

**Tool improvement and development**

- Propose improvements to existing management and tracking tools (dashboards and internal control mechanisms, etc.) to make them user-friendly, effective and adapted to the context, and to strengthen oversight of medical programmes

**Medical stock strategy and management**

- Oversee the review, planning, and validation of the medical standard lists and medical forecasts, including emergency preparedness (EPREP)
- Revise and validate medical orders within the agreed framework (budget, activity scope, medical master, and standard list, etc.)
- Define the medical stock management strategy and monitor its implementation in accordance with Good Storage and Distribution Practices and standard operating procedures, in collaboration with the Supply Officer and project teams

**Human Resources planning and management**

- Oversee the regular follow-up of projects’ human resource needs, including the review and planning of HR requirements, together with the DepCO
- Ensure effective matching and follow-up with the Human Resources Officer (HRO) and Pool Managers (PMs), including the briefing and debriefing of key medical operations staff in the countries of the cell, in agreement with the DepCO

**Budget**

- Collaborate with the DepCO to promote cost-conscious medical decision-making, balancing quality of care with resource availability, contextual specificities and sustainability
- Participate in medical operations (MedOps) budget planning and management to ensure efficient allocation of resources for medical operations

**Emergency response**

- Participate in the medical support/guidance to the projects for emergency responses together with the DepCO and medical department referents
- Ensure rapid and effective deployment of resources and personnel in case of emergencies in the countries of operations of the cell, in collaboration with the DepCO

**Emergency preparedness and response**

- Ensure that the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPREP) strategy and scenarios are regularly updated and adapted to evolving contexts in collaboration with the DepCO

**Technical Files**

- Provide first-line follow-up and input on technical files, according to specific expertise and in agreement with the DepCO

**Staff Health**

- Review and validate health policies for both International Mobile Staff (IMS) and Country Based Staff (CBS), ensuring comprehensive and effective healthcare provision
- Facilitate the management of staff health files between the countries of intervention and the Staff Health Unit (SHU) (including medical evacuations) in coordination with the DepCO

- Act as deputy for the Deputy Coordinator of Operations during absences or when requested, ensuring continuity in technical medical and strategic decision-making

- Planning and organizing
- Strategic vision/oversight
- Negotiation and networking
- Coaching & mirroring with the teams
- Teamwork and cooperation
- Comprehensive knowledge of humanitarian interventions
- Results and quality orientation
- Able to set priorities, make choices, and assume decisions
- Strong cross-cultural awareness and adaptability

- Location: **Brussels, Belgium**
- Mobility: At least one visit of 2-3 weeks to each Cell 1 country per year
- Type of contract: Open-ended contract – Full-time
- Salary according to MSF HQ salary grid
- Meal Vouchers - Hospital Insurance (DKV) – Pension Plan – 100% reimbursement for public transportation costs
- Partial homeworking possible
- **Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment**
- **Adhere to the MSF Behavioral Commitments**

jobs.title: Senior Adviser, Asia-Pacific
jobs.company: Association for the Prevention of Torture
jobs.description:
**Position summary**

The Senior Adviser, Asia-Pacific, based in Bangkok, leads the APT’s work across the region and represents the organisation with governments, diplomatic missions, regional bodies, donors, National Human Rights Institutions, National Preventive Mechanisms and civil society partners. They are responsible for implementation of the APT’s strategy in the Asia-Pacific region, including advancing OPCAT ratification and implementation.

The Senior Adviser also co-leads the APT’s work on strengthening dignity and fairness in the criminal justice system, including the implementation of legal and procedural safeguards promoting effective and non-coercive interviewing in line with the Méndez Principles. In both of these primary areas of work, priority is given to the protection of persons at heightened risk of torture and ill-treatment.

Combining strong substantive and legal expertise with political judgement and diplomatic skills, the Senior Adviser, Asia-Pacific identifies opportunities for influence, develops trusted relationships with decisionmakers and partners, and mobilises resources for the APT’s regional priorities. The postholder reports to the Head of Operations and works closely with the APT’s thematic, fundraising, monitoring and communications colleagues.

The Senior Adviser, Asia-Pacific is based in Thailand, entitled to work there, and possessing institutional experience and networks in the region.

**Responsibilities:**

**A. Regional strategy and representation**

1. Lead the development, implementation and regular review of the APT’s Asia-Pacific strategy, translating institutional priorities into politically informed regional and country-level engagement.
2. Represent the APT with governments, diplomatic missions, ASEAN and other regional bodies, UN actors, NHRIs, NPMs, civil society organisations and other strategic partners.
3. Build and sustain trusted relationships with senior officials and other decision-makers, using sound political judgement and diplomatic engagement to create opportunities for policy, legislative and institutional change.
4. Monitor political, legal and funding developments across the region, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and advise APT management on strategic positioning and priorities.
5. Maintain and expand a strong network in Thailand and across priority Asia-Pacific countries, positioning the Bangkok presence as a platform for regional engagement.

**B. Co-leadership – safeguards in the criminal justice system**

1. In close coordination with the Senior Advisor, Law and Advocacy (based in Geneva), provide institutional and regional leadership on the APT’s work to strengthen implementation of legal and procedural safeguards against torture and ill-treatment throughout the criminal justice system.
2. Provide high-quality legal and policy analysis and develop practical tools, position papers and recommendations relevant to criminal justice reform and torture prevention.
3. Support APT colleagues and partners to apply the organisation’s criminal justice safeguards strategy consistently across different national and regional contexts, while ensuring that approaches remain locally relevant.

**C. Project management and donor engagement**

1. Oversee the strategic delivery of the APT’s operations in the Asia-Pacific region, ensuring programme quality, risk management, learning, financial management and compliance with donor requirements.
2. With support from fundraising and outreach colleagues and in consultation with the Head of Operations, communicate results and emerging opportunities to donors and partners through high-quality briefings, meetings, proposals and narrative reports.
3. Identify funding opportunities and contribute substantively to the design of compelling, contextually grounded project proposals, theories of change, results frameworks and budgets.
4. Develop and maintain strategic relationships with institutional donors and other funding partners in Thailand and the wider Asia-Pacific region.

**Essential qualifications and experience**

- Advanced university degree in international human rights law, international relations, criminal justice or a closely related field.
- At least eight years of progressively responsible experience in human rights, criminal justice reform, diplomacy, international cooperation or a related field, including significant experience in the Asia-Pacific region.
- Strong knowledge of the international human rights legal framework and regional political landscape, including ASEAN and relevant national, regional and international institutions.
- Substantial professional experience in Thailand or another country in the Asia-Pacific region relevant to the work of the APT, and established networks with relevant government institutions, diplomatic missions, donors, NHRIs, civil society and/or criminal justice actors.
- Proven ability to engage diplomatically and persuasively with senior government officials, diplomats, donors and institutional leaders, including on politically sensitive issues.
- Demonstrated experience in donor engagement, programme development and successful funding proposals.
- Experience in managing projects, including planning, budgeting, risk management, monitoring, reporting and partner coordination.
- Excellent analytical and drafting skills, with the ability to translate complex legal and policy issues into practical strategies and persuasive messages.
- Excellent spoken and written English and Thai, an Asian language of relevance to the position.
- Based in Bangkok with the legal right to work in Thailand.
- Availability for regular travel within the Asia-Pacific region and occasional travel to Geneva and other locations.
- Ability to participate in meetings occasionally outside of regular office hours.

**Desirable qualifications and experience**

- Demonstrated expertise in torture prevention and/or the implementation of legal and procedural safeguards in criminal justice systems, as foreseen in the Méndez Principles.
- Experience working directly with police, prosecutors, judicial institutions or professional training bodies.
- Practical experience working with NPMs, NHRIs or OPCAT implementation processes.
- Experience working with ASEAN bodies, UN mechanisms or diplomatic missions.

**Other expected competencies**

- Political judgement and diplomatic acumen
- Strategic thinking and ability to identify opportunities for influence
- Relationship-building across different institutional and cultural environments
- Collaborative and non-hierarchical working style

**What we offer**

We are an agile multicultural organisation who values commitment to the preventive approach, inclusion and equality, integrity and transparency, quality and perseverance, and continuous learning and creativity.

We offer flexible working hours, promote work-life balance and emphasise employee well-being.

The successful candidate will be working either from home or from a co-working space. The APT does not have any physical office in Thailand.

We provide equipment (computer and necessary collaborative tools), as well as IT support.

Our employees benefit from learning development opportunities. They all benefit from 20 days annual leave per year, plus national bank holidays.

Proposed gross salary : THB 1'600'000/year to THB 1’800’000/year according to experience

jobs.title: Training and Capacity Building Manager
jobs.location: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.description:
**Hours**: Full-time

**Pay**: £42,440 GBP gross per annum (dependent on experience)

**Duration:** Permanent contract

**Location**: UK-Med Office, Manchester, UK (hybrid working) with an expectation of approximately 40% international travel/deployment, as required by UK-Med

**Can you turn operational lessons into frontline skills and prepare global health workforces to respond to crises? Do you have the experience to deliver high-quality training and capacity building that strengthens emergency health responses worldwide?**

UK-Med is a frontline medical aid charity founded on the values and expertise of the NHS. For more than 30 years, we have worked towards a world where everyone gets the healthcare they need when emergencies overwhelm local health services.

We are looking for an experienced and passionate Training and Capacity Building Manager to help strengthen emergency preparedness through high-quality, evidence-based learning and capacity building for Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs), healthcare professionals and health systems globally.

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in shaping and delivering UK-Med's growing training and capacity building portfolio. From strengthening EMT capabilities through international twinning partnerships to supporting our emergency responses and longer-term programmes in Gaza and Ukraine, your work will contribute directly to building stronger, more prepared healthcare teams.

Working as part of our Learning & Capacity Building Department, you will support the delivery and continuous improvement of our training programmes, including our Core Training Programme, which prepares UK-Med's global workforce of core staff and approximately 1,500 healthcare professionals for work and deployment. You will also contribute to the strategic direction of our capacity building approach, ensuring quality, innovation and learning remain central to our work.

We are looking for an experienced learning professional and skilled project manager with a proven ability to manage complex projects, build strong stakeholder relationships and lead and develop teams. Ideally, you will bring experience in humanitarian or emergency health programming, alongside the flexibility to travel internationally, sometimes at short notice.

You will join a collaborative and dedicated team at an exciting time, with the opportunity to strengthen emergency preparedness and make a meaningful contribution to lifesaving humanitarian responses. We offer competitive benefits and a friendly, supportive working environment.

jobs.title: Head of Mission - Yemen
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Head of Mission

**Code:** SR-35-10204

**Duty station:** Aden / Sanaa with visits to the projects' sites

**Starting date:** 15/12/2026

**Contract duration:** 6 months (renewable)

**Reporting to:** Regional Director MENA

**Functional Supervisor:**

**Supervision of:** Senior Management Team

**Type of Duty Station:** Non-family duty station

## **General context of the project**

While the armed conflict entered its 12th year, Yemen remains one of the largest humanitarian crisis. The country’s deteriorating economy, the protracted conflict and crumbling basic services are exacerbating humanitarian needs across the country. Meanwhile, climate shocks, increased regional tensions and chronic underfunding of critical humanitarian sectors are further worsening people’s vulnerability and suffering.

Four years since the UN- brokered truce, international non-governmental organizations (INGOs) operating in Yemen warn that humanitarian conditions are more fragile than at any point since the peak years of the response. Over 22.2 million people 1 continue to face dire humanitarian conditions, struggling to meet basic needs and access essential services amid protracted crisis, economic deterioration, aid cuts, displacement and climate-related shocks. Furthermore, the escalating conflict in the Middle East and the wider region threatens to exacerbate the dire economic situation and could trigger a resumption of large-scale armed conflict within Yemen. These regional shifts risk disrupting vital humanitarian and commercial supply chains and inflating the cost of essential goods.

INTERSOS, in collaboration with local partners, has been providing essential health, nutrition, protection, water and sanitation, as well as livelihoods support for the vulnerable people across Yemen since 2008.
While INTERSOS operational presence has been impacted by the signficant funding downsize in the last few years, the integrated programming serving the most vulnerable communities (IDPs, migrants, people at hightened protection risks) continues providing essential lifesaving aid.

## **General purpose of the position**

The Head of Mission represents INTERSOS in the country and acts on behalf of the Director General, leading the organization’s response, including strategy design, planning resources, management and implementation of programs.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks**

**Strategy and vision**

- Is responsible for monitoring and analysing the political and humanitarian situation across the country and surrounding countries through established contacts and carrying out exploratory missions to identify potential fields of intervention. Design, propose, elaborate and develop new strategy of interventions in line with INTERSOS values and principles.
- Explore and present funding opportunities that integrate initiatives and leverage impact for the communities; support and direct fund-raising activities with institutional and private donors.
- Monitor donor’s priorities and intervention strategies in the country. Guarantee the strict observance and adherence to INTERSOS and donors’ procedures.
- Overview the development and implementation of projects and programs and through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, evaluate their evolution and quality as per internal and external standards and requirements, final results and achievements to ensure that organization’s technical and ethical standards are respected and objectives are achieved.
- Greenlight project proposals and response to emergencies to be submitted to HQ for approval. Evaluate potential emergency responses in the country and lead on developing additional programs in line with review and assessment results.
- Lead the detailed country strategy planning process and prioritising of actions and resources to achieve program objectives.

**Representation and advocacy**

- Represent the organisation and manage relations with the authorities ensuring smooth and timely implementation of planned interventions and safeguarding impartiality and independence.
- Follow up, guarantee and monitor government recognition procedures for the organisation in compliance with the host country formalities.
- Maintain a productive communication with donors and ensure that the assessed needs are communicated to impact on donors’ priorities.
- Represent INTERSOS in relevant fora.

**People management**

- Ensure that the senior management team is effective, mutually supporting and sufficiently involved in key decision-making processes.
- In coordination with the HR Coordinator, guide and supervise the staff performance process for international and national staff.
- Ensure the respect organisational values, Code of Ethics, Organization Management and Control Model, and INTERSOS procedures.
- Maintain high ethical standards and promote teamwork and ensure a productive working environment.
- Empower staff to meet organizational goals and work as a highly functioning and cooperative team.

**Finance, logistics and supply**

- Together with the Finance Coordinator, define and oversee the overall financial management of the mission, striving towards financial sustainability and assume responsibility for the mission funds management (NGO budget).
- Ensure that allocated resources are managed effectively and transparently.
- Together with the Logistics and Supply Coordinator, ensure that required and efficient supply services and processes are in place.

**Safety and security**

- Hold final accountability for security, including development and validation of country security plan and ensuring adherence to procedures, monitoring of the context development, analysis and provision of recommendations.
- Regularly interact with the Regional Office and the Security Advisor on security issues.
- Hold final responsibility for any decision concerning security in the country.

**Accountability and quality control**

- In collaboration with the SMT is responsible to produce and submit the mission monthly activity reports.
- Continuously assess, analyse and evaluate the impact of the country program and operations, also through periodic visits to the areas of intervention, in collaboration with the Program Coordinator and MEAL.
- Ensure all the policies within INTERSOS Safeguarding Framework are respected by the staff
- Together with MEAL Department, supervise the effectiveness of a complaint feedback mechanism
- Oversee program quality and impact in line with established strategic objectives and related indicators.
- Oversee program reporting, ensuring compliance with INTERSOS policies and procedures, donor regulations and national requirements.

## **Required profile and experience**

**Education**

- University degree Project management, International Affairs, Development, International Political Economy or other relevant field

**Professional experience**

- At minimum eight years experience in management positions in humanitarian contexts
- Previous experience working in Yemen and/or other countries in the Middle East is considered a strong asset

**Professional requirements**

- Experience with NGOs in humanitarian response contexts
- Experience with major grants and international donors (e.g., ECHO, etc)
- Experience of working within an insecure environment with responsibility for security planning, monitoring and management
- Experience in managing humanitarian access in complex contexts
- Essential computer literacy (word, excel and internet)

**Languages**

- Full fluency in English language
- Arabic language is considered an asset

**Personal requirements**

- Strategic vision
- Good organizational and planning skills
- Leadership, team management and cooperation
- Behavioral flexibility
- Networking, negotiation skills and decision-making skills
- Diplomatic, interpersonal and good communication skills
- Ability to take initiative and work independently
- Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills
- Commitment to INTERSOS principles.

## **General conditions and benefits**

- **Salary range:** 14 - 4.505€ - 5.182€ monthly gross
- **Accommodation:** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R:** 7 days of psycho-physical recovery every 8 weeks + 1000€ allowance.
- **Annual Leave:** 2.5 days per month
- **Medical insurance** for the staff
- **Transportation and visa:** Round-trip flights. For missions lasting at *least 9 months,* an additional flight ticket to the Country of residence and return to the mission will also be provided.
- **Induction:** one week of online induction before the deployment

jobs.title: Security Multi-country Project Manager
jobs.description:
**About Oxfam**

At Oxfam we respond to emergencies and advocate for people in crisis, partnering with local organizations to deliver essentials and help rebuild communities. We work with activists and partners to fight poverty and injustice. We campaign for economic, gender, climate justice and accountable governance, striving for sustainable growth and transformation. **We fight for a future that is equal, just and fair** – one in which people have more equal opportunities and rights, and one in which we can all flourish, not just survive.

**About The Role**

**Hub Purpose:** The Global Programs Hub enables coherent, accountable, and impactful programming by connecting countries, clusters, regions, affiliates, and global teams around shared priorities, learning, and delivery. It anchors thematic leadership and fosters mutual accountability, supporting locally led, people-centred programming.

**Team Purpose:** The Security Team provides security and crisis management support to Oxfam, helping to strengthen security across all operations. It offers strategic security, travel safety, and safe programming advice to OIS (Oxfam International Secretariat), affiliates, countries, and regions. The team develops and implements security policies and standards, leads incident monitoring and risk management processes, supports risk assessments and follow-up actions, and promotes learning and development in security management. It also engages in external networking, contributes to sector-wide discussions, and represents Oxfam in relevant external forums.

**Job Purpose:** The Project Manager will coordinate the activities and the implementation of the project “Global Security Evidence, Local Risk Management Leadership” funded by the European Union Humanitarian Office (ECHO) in Chad, South Sudan and Myanmar. The purpose is to coordinate the needs assessments of local partners, foster the creation of security communities of practice, participate in the creation and delivery of training activities and in the provision of technical and material support to partners.

**Role reports to:** Programmes Learning and Development Global Security Advisor of the Global Security Team.

**Roles eporting to this post:** 3 Security managers for the project in Chad, South Sudan and Myanmar.

jobs.title: Research and Monitoring Coordinator (Explosive Weapons Monitor)
jobs.description:
**About INEW and the Explosive Weapons Monitor**

The [International Network on Explosive Weapons (INEW)](https://www.inew.org) is a global network of civil society organisations working to prevent human suffering from the use of explosive weapons in populated areas.

The [Explosive Weapons Monitor](https://explosiveweaponsmonitor.org) is INEW’s research project. It documents civilian harm from the use of explosive weapons in populated areas and monitors how states are responding to the issue, including through the implementation of the 2022 Political Declaration. Its work includes an [annual report](https://explosiveweaponsmonitor.org/reports/9/explosive-weapons-monitor-2025/) on civilian harm, quarterly data bulletins with an online dashboard, the Fragments series of articles, and monitoring of the Political Declaration’s implementation.

INEW is hosted by [Article 36](https://article36.org), a UK-based non-profit organisation working to reduce harm from weapons.

The [International Network on Explosive Weapons (INEW)](https://www.inew.org/) is a global network of civil society organisations working to prevent human suffering from the use of explosive weapons in populated areas.

INEW is hosted by [Article 36](https://article36.org/), a UK-based non-profit organisation working to reduce harm from weapons. Article 36 will be the formal employer for this position.

The [Explosive Weapons Monitor](https://explosiveweaponsmonitor.org/) is the research arm of the [International Network on Explosive Weapons (INEW)](https://www.inew.org/), a network of organisations calling for immediate action to prevent human suffering from the use of explosive weapons in populated areas. The Monitor documents civilian harm from explosive weapons in populated areas and tracks how states respond, including through the implementation of the [2022 Political Declaration](https://ewipa.org/the-political-declaration).

**The role**

INEW is looking for an experienced **Research and Monitoring Coordinator** to lead the delivery of the Explosive Weapons Monitor’s programme of work. The role involves coordinating research with partner organisations and consultants, overseeing research quality and data analysis, managing publications and ensuring that the Monitor’s findings inform policy discussions and action to protect civilians.

The majority of the Monitor’s research is produced with partners and consultants, drawing on data from [ACLED](https://acleddata.com/) and [Insecurity Insight](https://insecurityinsight.org/) and contributions from NGOs and researchers. We are looking for an experienced project manager with a strong grasp of research methods and data to bring this work together: commissioning and editing others’ work, managing partners and consultants, keeping outputs on schedule, and making sure every figure the Monitor publishes holds up and its findings reach the people who need them. A strong candidate will have expertise in data collection and analysis alongside a background in weapons and disarmament, the protection of civilians or humanitarian action.

**Project management and coordination (40%)**

- Lead the planning and delivery of the Monitor’s programme of work, keeping outputs on time, on budget and in line with grant obligations.
- Draft terms of reference for consultants and research partners, run their procurement in line with donor rules with the INEW Global Lead, and manage their contracts and deliverables.
- Oversee the Monitor’s casualty data consultant on the quarterly data bulletins and the online dashboard.
- Coordinate external partners commissioned for specific products.
- Convene and lead the Monitor’s editorial board, working closely with its members, and run the sign-off process for all Monitor products.
- Track expenditure against the Monitor’s budgets and update the INEW Global Lead.
- Draft donor reports and contribute to fundraising by identifying opportunities and drafting project proposals.
- Make sure the Monitor’s work aligns with INEW’s strategy, in consultation with the INEW Global Lead, Steering Committee and editorial board.
- Organise the Monitor’s in-person and virtual meetings, events and activities.

**Research quality, data and editorial oversight (40%)**

- Develop the Monitor’s research agenda with the editorial board: the questions it will pursue over the strategy period and how its outputs answer them.
- Coordinate and edit the [annual report](https://explosiveweaponsmonitor.org/our-research) on civilian harm from explosive weapons, drawing on data and contributions from partner organisations, including fact-checking it and making sure states and other actors are presented consistently throughout, and lead its launch with a supporting communications and outreach plan.
- Oversee the quarterly data bulletins and matching [dashboard](https://explosiveweaponsmonitor.org/global-figures/) updates, published at the end of each quarter.
- Commission and edit two editions of [Fragments](https://explosiveweaponsmonitor.org/fragments) a year, each with two to three longer research articles, including ensuring contributions meet methodological standards, coordinating feedback from reviewers and sharing comments with the author, and editing contributions to meet stylistic standards.
- Manage monitoring of the Political Declaration’s implementation, including developing a framework to track and visualise progress and coordinating the monitoring work of an external research partner or consultant.
- Write and contribute to Monitor products where needed, including short analyses, case studies and briefing papers.
- Work directly with the Monitor’s data, checking figures against their sources before publication, and make sure they are consistent across the Monitor’s products and from one year to the next.
- Review the methodologies of partners and consultants, including how incidents are coded, attributed and counted, and make the limits of the data clear in what the Monitor publishes.
- Maintain the Monitor’s methodology documentation and a clear record of data sources and versions, and manage corrections where needed.
- Work with the INEW Global Lead to track state statements, positions and policy developments, and report on relevant meetings (including Protection of Civilians week, the UN General Assembly First Committee and meetings on the Declaration).

**External relations and communications (20%)**

- Present the Monitor’s research at conferences, in media interviews and in other fora.
- With INEW’s Global Lead, plan and coordinate the dissemination of the Monitor’s outputs, including its newsletter, mail-outs and social media content, and maintain the Monitor’s website.
- Record and assess the reach and use of the Monitor’s research.
- Maintain collaborative relations with research staff at partner organisations, including on joint products, and coordinate with the Landmine and Cluster Munition Monitor where data and research work is shared.
- Maintain good relations with governments, donors, international organisations and civil society.
- Act as focal point for the INEW Steering Committee and network on Monitor matters.

**Person specification**

- A university degree plus at least five years of relevant experience in an advocacy, research, humanitarian or non-profit organisation.
- Proven experience managing research or data projects with several partners, consultants and contributors, to deadlines and budgets.
- Experience conducting qualitative and quantitative data collection, monitoring, reporting and analysis on topics related to human rights abuses or civilian harm, including hands-on work with large datasets and a strong working understanding of conflict and civilian harm data and their limits.
- Experience drafting reports based on desk- or field-based research for a policy audience.
- International experience in humanitarian disarmament, the protection of civilians or humanitarian action, and an understanding of the issue of explosive weapons in populated areas will be highly valued.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills, including editing others’ work. Fluent in English; additional languages an advantage.
- Effective time management, with the ability to manage several time-sensitive priorities and to make sure others do the same.
- Flexibility and adaptability to shifting priorities, changing circumstances and new tasks.
- Ability to work to tight deadlines, in a self-directed way and within a small, remote team.
- Knowledge of NGO systems, including proposal writing, financial record keeping, grant management and donor reporting.
- Proficient computer skills, including website content management.
- Ability and willingness to travel, occasionally to high-risk environments.

Weapons and armed violence often disproportionately affect marginalised groups who continue to be under-represented in international policymaking; these groups include black people and other people of colour, women, LGBTQ+ people, people with disabilities and people of different faiths and beliefs. Consequently, we are committed to diversifying our team and strongly encourage applications from people who can bring new and different ideas and perspectives to our work.

jobs.title: Senior Grant Manager – Ebola Response
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Organizational Background**

The IRC’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads the organization’s global emergency preparedness and response activities. Its mission is to meet immediate survival needs and reduce the suffering of affected populations during the acute phase of an emergency.

**Response Background**

The Ministry of Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo officially declared the country’s 17th Ebola virus disease outbreak on 15 May 2026, after confirming cases caused by the Bundibugyo virus species (BDBV) in Ituri Province. The outbreak was initially detected in and around the Mongbwalu, Rwampara and Bunia health zones.

On 17 May 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) assessed the outbreak as a public health emergency of international concern, owing to the risk of regional spread and the challenging operational context. The IRC is preparing its support to contain the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. The response rests on three complementary pillars: infection prevention and control and WASH (IPC/WASH); risk communication and community engagement (RCCE); and integrated protection, including safeguarding, PSEA, MHPSS, GBV referral mechanisms and protection risk mitigation.

**Scope of the Position**

The Senior Grant Manager will contribute to overall grants management at IRC DRC. The position reports to the Emergency Programme Lead and is based in Bunia, with occasional trips to field sites as needed. The Senior Grant Manager will work collaboratively with all members of the DRC Country Program, Grants and Partnerships Unit, the Technical Coordinators, the Operations and Finance teams. The IRC DRC portfolio consists mostly of grants from the EU, US DoS, OCHA, Irish Aid and private foundations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Proposal and business development:**

- Support the Emergency Program Lead to proactively identify new funding opportunities by monitoring donor strategies, polices and funding trends
- Prepare for and lead Go/No-Go meetings for funding opportunities
- Lead coordination of concept note and proposal development and amendments (including design meetings) working with program staff and ensuring proper review at the HQ level, gathering input from technical coordinators, technical advisors, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) staff, and the Regional Unit.
- Lead and coordinate budget development for newly assigned proposals and amendments, working with program staff, other members of the Grants and Partnerships Unit, the Finance Department and Regional Program and Business Development Units.
- Ensure proper review of new budgets and realignment/modification budgets at both HQ and DRC levels, incorporating all feedback and ensuring that budgets are accurate.
- Coordinate and develop budget narratives, edit proposals, and ensure proper proposal and grant management procedures are followed through clear roles, responsibilities and timelines for each department
- Act as the focal point for in-country donors during the proposal development process, as needed.
- Liaise with IRC New York, UK and Germany grant units in order to ensure proposals meet internal standards, apply IRC’s Outcomes Evidence Framework (OEF), are in line with IRC DRC’s Strategic Action Plan (SAP) and are donor compliant.

**2. Reporting**

- Ensure that reports to donors are submitted on time; that reports are coherent and accurate (quarterly, interim or final reports); and that the internal reporting tracker and OTIS reporting information is up to date.
- Lead Project Cycle Meetings, as well as monthly/regular grants management meetings (BVA meetings) which include representation from each unit (finance, programs, logistics) and ensure proper follow up of issues raised.
- Monitor and support the use of project cycle management tools such as Project Dashboard, Budget vs. Actual (BVA) for the proper monitoring and the successful implementation of programs and early warning in case of obstacles or challenges.

**3. Donor Compliance**

- Work closely with the Response Program Lead and the EmU Finance and Grant Team to support research on donor compliance issues for new opportunities or existing grants, as needed, within the assigned portfolio of IRC DRC.
- With the support of the EmU and the Country Program Grant and Partnership Units, review donor agreements,coordinate their review with the relevant IRC HQ office and coordinate approval of pre-award spending as required.
- Ensure that grants are implemented in compliance with IRC and relevant donor regulations.
- Raise compliance issues early with program staff, the Emergency Program Lead and senior management, and flag any projected inability to meet contractual obligations.
- Maintain and update grant files related to all donor contractual documents, reports and key correspondence are filed consistently in up-to-date shared libraries.

**4. Communication and Information Management**

- Communicate with donors and attend donor meetings in order to share IRC’s accomplishments as well as to stay up to date on the latest donor developments and requirements.
- Distribute to IRC staff all documentation (grant proposals, reports, budget, etc.) related to their specific programs.
- Keep an updated inventory of all communications related to programs/donors and ensure communication and visibility requirements are met.

**5. Management and Capacity Building**

- Provide orientation to Program team members. Topics may include donor compliance rules and regulations, BVA, OTIS, project design, proposal development, budget development, and Grant Opening and Grant Closing meetings.

**6. Administrative/Other**

- Ensure OTIS data is up to date for all assigned new proposals. Secure all OTIS approvals for the assigned new proposals prior to submission to the donor.
- Keep an accurate Grants Filing system on the Shared Drive (Box), OTIS and hardcopy folder.

**Requirements**

Education: BA degree required; master’s degree in accounting, economics, international affairs, social sciences or a STEM field (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) strongly preferred.

Experience: At least 4 years of experience in program management, grants management and/or proposal/business development and design.

**Skills and Abilities**

- Professional proficiency in French, written and spoken, is required. Good working knowledge of English is required for reporting and technical exchanges.
- Swahili and/or Lingala is an asset; knowledge of local languages of Ituri is a plus.
- Advanced MS Excel and mathematical skills are required (to be tested through an exam) and are the most important requirement for this position.
- Prior knowledge of donor regulations (e.g., ECHO, EU, US DoS, OCHA, private foundations) and government regulations preferred.
- Good communicator with strong organizational, time management and analytical skills.
- Excellent interpersonal, cultural and diplomatic skills.
- Flexibility to adapt to changing requirements.
- Strong capacity to mentor and build the capacity of staff.
- Ability to prioritize competing priorities, meet demanding deadlines and work under pressure in unstable security environments.
- Strong computer skills required.
- Previous successful experience developing projects and writing winning proposals and donor reports preferred.
- Qualified DRC nationals are strongly encouraged to apply.
- Female applicants are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Work Environment**

- The position is based in Bunia, with occasional travel to other areas and intervention sites (e.g., Beni and Butembo) as needed.
- The context is complex and evolving, marked by the risk of Ebola transmission, insecurity, population movements, community mistrust, stigma, logistical constraints and access difficulties.
- The post holder must strictly comply with IRC safety and security protocols, travel procedures, infection prevention and control measures, safeguarding standards and public health guidance.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.
