jobs.title: Finance Coordinator– Business Development and Partnership Lead
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background/IRC Summary:**

The IRC has worked in Sudan for decades, delivering life-saving and recovery programmes in health, nutrition, protection, women's protection and empowerment, education, and economic recovery. Today we deliver as a single country programme, providing vital assistance to communities across the country.

Sudan is experiencing one of the world's largest and most severe humanitarian crises. More than 12 million people have been displaced across all 18 states, around 30 million people need humanitarian assistance, and some 25 million face acute food insecurity — including hundreds of thousands of children with severe acute malnutrition. Most health facilities are no longer fully functional and humanitarian access remains constrained. The IRC has scaled up its response to meet these growing needs.

We know that we serve communities better when our own teams reflect the diversity of the people we work alongside, and when every colleague is able to do their best work and be themselves at work.

**Position Summary**

The Finance Coordinator – Business Development & Partnerships provides financial leadership and technical support for proposal development, donor budgeting, partner financial management, and grant start-up processes. The role is responsible for ensuring that proposal budgets, funding applications, partnership financial arrangements, and donor cost proposals are accurate, competitive, compliant, and aligned with organizational financial policies and donor requirements.

As a member of the senior finance leadership team East, the position serves as a strategic partner to SMT and closely works closely with Programs, Grants, Partnerships, Awards Management, and Technical Teams to strengthen resource mobilization efforts, improve financial sustainability, and ensure effective financial management of donor-funded programs for the Country Program.

**Overall Responsibilities**

**1. Proposal Budgeting & Resource Mobilization**

**Summary**

Serve as a focal person to Country Program financial planning and budgeting for funding opportunities, budget revisions, realignment and budget top ups.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Support formulation of Annual Operating budget and regular reforecast ensure the country program planning reflects accurate portfolio and financial position.
- Maintain standard budget development tools, assumptions, and costing methodologies. Ensure proposal budgets accurately reflect staffing, operational, procurement, logistics, and support costs.
- Lead the development of proposal budgets, budget revisions, and top ups for institutional and private donors.
- Coordinate with relevant teams to develop realistic and compliant project budgets aligned with program activities and implementation plans.
- Analyze funding opportunities and advise management on financial viability and cost implications.
- Coordinate finance reviews and approvals of proposal submissions.

**2. Donor Finance & Award Management Support**

**Summary**

Provide financial oversight and compliance support throughout the project life cycle.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Review donor regulations and ensure proposal budgets comply with donor requirements and organizational policies.
- Support pre-award and post-award financial assessments and reviews.
- Participate in grant start-up meetings and ensure approved budgets are accurately reflected in financial systems.
- Ensure budget coding accurate and upload completed timely and maintained in the system uptodate to support smooth project monitoring and review.
- Support award modifications, realignments, cost extensions, and donor budget amendments.
- Review donor agreements and identify financial risks, restrictions, and compliance requirements.
- Monitor cost recovery and donor funding utilization.
- Support grant closeout activities and final financial reporting requirements.

**3. Partner Financial Management**

**Summary**

Strengthen financial oversight and risk management of implementing partners and sub-recipients.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Conduct financial due diligence and capacity assessments of prospective and existing partners.
- Review partner budgets during proposal development and implementation stages.
- Assess partner financial systems, internal controls, and compliance capacity.
- Review partner financial reports and monitor financial performance.
- Identify financial risks related to partner management and recommend mitigation measures.
- Provide financial guidance and capacity-building support to partners.
- Support development and review of sub-award budgets and financial agreements.
- Ensure compliance with partner management and donor requirements.
- Support partner monitoring visit and follow up implementation of recommendations and document

**4. Financial Analysis & Cost Recovery**

**Summary**

Support sustainable program growth through sound financial analysis and cost recovery strategies.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Conduct financial analysis of funding opportunities and strategic initiatives.
- Evaluate project cost structures and recommend appropriate recovery mechanisms.
- Support development of shared cost allocations recovery strategies and monitor recovery of support costs and shared services expenses.
- Analyze project funding gaps, and budget efficiency. Develop financial scenarios and models to support decision-making.
- Regularly review and provide recommendations to improve financial sustainability.
- As a focal person for East operation, ensure strong follow up on accounts and reporting tasks to support sector leads and other functional areas.

**5. Donor Compliance & Risk Management**

**Summary**

Ensure financial compliance with donor regulations and minimize risks associated with funding opportunities and awards.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Ensure proposal budgets comply with donor regulations, cost principles, and organizational policies.
- Review financial compliance requirements associated with donor opportunities.
- Identify and assess financial risks during proposal development and award negotiations.
- Provide guidance on eligible and non-eligible donor costs.
- Support compliance reviews and donor financial monitoring visits.
- Maintain awareness of donor regulations and emerging compliance requirements.
- Review and follow up financial risk related to project management and implementation.
- Support risk mitigation measures related to accounts and reporting section.

**6. Financial Planning & Coordination**

**Summary**

Facilitate effective coordination between finance and non-finance teams throughout the proposal and award cycle. Strengthen staff capacity in donor budgeting, financial compliance, and grant financial management.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Serve as the primary finance focal point for proposal development and partnership initiatives.
- Work closely with Program, Awards, Grants, HR, Supply Chain, and Technical teams during budget development.
- Maintain proposal budget archives and supporting documentation.
- Train program, grants, and partnership staff on donor budgeting requirements.
- Provide guidance on donor regulations and financial compliance standards.
- Develop budget preparation tools, templates, and guidance materials.
- Support onboarding of staff involved in proposal development and grant management.
- Promote best practices in donor budgeting and financial planning.
- Share lessons learned and emerging donor finance requirements across teams.

jobs.title: Area Manager Maradi Niger
jobs.description:
**Background**

The humanitarian crisis in the Central Sahel remains severe, complex and fast evolving, driven by conflict, displacement, climate shocks, food insecurity and shrinking operational space. In Niger and Burkina Faso, millions of people continue to require humanitarian assistance; while underfunding, insecurity and access constraints place sustained pressure on principled humanitarian action and programme quality.

Niger continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by insecurity, climate-related events, and chronic poverty, disrupting livelihoods for families and communities. Nearly one million displaced people, including refugees and internally displaced persons, are living in Niger, many of them in the regions of Tillabéri, Tahoua and Diffa.

NRC is currently working in Niger, with staff dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict. Its humanitarian interventions are based on programming expertise in core competencies including Education, WASH, Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Protection from Violence, and Shelter to vulnerable displaced people.

Within the Central Sahel Multi-Country Office (MCO) model, Burkina Faso and Niger are managed under a unified structure led by the Central Sahel MCO Country Director, while maintaining strong Area Office delivery hubs.

The Area Manager – Maradi is responsible for leading NRC’s area operations in the Maradi / Tillabéri / Dosso / Tahoua area, ensures high standard of project delivery and contributes to multi-country coherence through participation in the Multi-Country Management Group (MCMG).

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The purpose of the Area Manager position is to ensure high quality and cost-effective programme/project implementation in the Maradi, Tillabéri, and Tahoua Regions of Niger. The Area Manager supervises several field offices/antennas – Tillabéri, Tahoua, Dosso (non-exhaustive).

**What you will do**

- Overall responsibility of managing the Maradi / Tillabéri Area Office including potential sub offices, with close supervision of the Field Manager in Tillabéri
- Responsible for overall staff security, including completing security risk assessments for the area and possible new areas of intervention
- Support needs assessment in the region, ensure the implementation of all projects active in the area in line with the agreed standards and donors’ requirements; this includes ensuring that NRC’s data collection systems are in place and information is properly stored and analyzed
- Support the team in identifying the gaps for further programming and development, and participate in assessments for new areas of operation, possible areas of intervention, aiding the development of program strategy for implementation.
- Lead on access strategy and its implementation in hard-to-reach areas, in close collaboration with CD and relevant colleagues at the country level. This includes contextualizing, adapting, and implementing SOPs and procedures to ensure effective provision of assistance to hard-to-reach areas
- In conjunction with Country Office, liaise with donors on new funding and operational areas of programming, liaise regularly with local authorities (political and security), donors and humanitarian actors in the operational area. This includes support in the development of concept notes, project proposals, and budgets for scale-up of post emergency activities
- Represent NRC at coordination platforms at area level and provide regular feedback and input to advocacy initiatives
- Overall responsibility for staff management. Recruitment of qualified staff for the area office, in close collaboration with HR and support team in the Country Office, lead by example the teams on the ground on NRC’s core values (dedication, innovation, inclusion and accountability). Ensuring training is provided to all staff and capacity building initiatives are in place, work and development plans are completed by all staff in the operational area, and performance feedback sessions are conducted on a minimum quarterly basis
- Ensure sound financial management, including the Master Budget is covered and up to date, reflecting cost-efficient use of the available funding

Please download the detailed job description to learn more about the [JD Area Manager Maradi-Tillabéri Niger .pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBHy7h6uVMuQ6WNdVjh2jUiAXcbCfRs-sXSEBD6a1lIVN4?e=3ZheyZ)

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- Minimum 3-5 years of experience working as a Senior Project Manager / field manager in a humanitarian and recovery context
- Previous experience working in complex and volatile contexts
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in French and proficiency in English, both written and verbal

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Knowledge of the context in West Africa and Niger in particular
- Experience working in insecure / hard to reach locations
- Experience managing safety and security
- Competencies in humanitarian and access negotiations

**2. Behavioural competencies**

- Handling insecure environments
- Strategic thinking
- Empowering and building trust
- Managing performance and development
- Managing resources to optimise results
- Coping with change

***Leadership profile***

- Building meaningful relations
- Acting with integrity
- Empowering people
- Delivering results

**What we offer**

- **Duty station**: Maradi,Niger
- **Contract**: Fixed term for 12 months with possibility of extension
- **Salary&Benefits**: Grade 10 on NRC’s National salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

**Female Applicants are Highly encouraged to Apply**

jobs.title: Child Protection Awareness-Raising daily Worker (4) (On Call Position) - Raqqa
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Child Protection Awareness-Raising daily Worker will deliver child-friendly, age-appropriate awareness sessions for children aged 6–14, caregivers, and community members in targeted locations in Raqqa Governorate. Sessions will cover child abuse and neglect, violence against children, child labour, child marriage, children's rights, positive parenting, protective behaviours, safe reporting, and available referral services. The Child Protection Awareness-Raising daily Worker will conduct community outreach, promote inclusive participation, identify and safely refer protection concerns, coordinate with child protection and PSS teams, and maintain accurate activity records and reports in accordance with WVSR's safeguarding, confidentiality, and data-protection procedures.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Conduct child protection awareness-raising activities throughout the project period, For children, caregivers, and community members in the targeted locations.
- Deliver child-friendly sessions on child protection risks, children's rights, positive parenting, and protective behaviours.
- Raise awareness of safe reporting options and available child protection services.
- Identify protection concerns disclosed or observed during activities and refer them promptly to designated referral pathway in line with established procedures.
- Coordinate with PSS , case workers, school staff, and community representatives to ensure consistent messaging and appropriate referrals.
- Ensure that all activities adhere to child safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent and assent, data protection, and do-no-harm principles.
- When appropriate, support the dissemination of approved child protection messages through authorized digital channels, including WhatsApp and Telegram, without collecting or sharing personal or sensitive information.
- Maintain accurate attendance sheets and activity records, distinguishing unique beneficiaries from repeat participants in accordance with project reporting requirements.
- Prepare and submit timely activity reports, highlighting sessions conducted, participants reached, challenges, and community feedback
- Participate in team meetings, training, and supervision sessions, and contribute to improving awareness materials and activities.

- Remain available on an on-call basis and report for duty as requested, depending on operational needs.

**Working Hours:**

The position requires regular field visits and activities within the targeted schools and communities. The role may also require working on weekends, including Fridays and Saturdays, based on project requirements and operational needs.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

**Preferred Skills:**

jobs.description:
Position title: Data Systems and Business Intelligence Officer

Team: Performance and Impact

Required FTE: 80%

Required travel: Some travel, up to 10% of time

Reports to: Head – Performance and Impact

**Scope of the role**

Violent extremism is a direct threat to international security, economic growth, and development. GCERF works to prevent violent extremism by investing in people. As the only global fund dedicated to preventing violent extremism (PVE), we connect local communities to global resources and support grassroots initiatives that are often out of reach for international donors. We fund community-centric initiatives led by civil society organisations to address the local social, economic, and political drivers of violent extremism.

The Data Systems and Business Intelligence Officer will be part of GCERF’s dynamic and high-performing team of Monitoring and Evaluation experts. This role is responsible for managing, maintaining, and expanding the data infrastructure and systems, with a focus on grant performance and programmatic information, including descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics.

**Principal accountabilities and ownership**

**Data Architecture, Integration and Infrastructure:** Responsible for designing, maintaining and improving GCERF’s data architecture, databases and (automated) ETL pipelines, connecting grant management, programme, results and financial data. Monitor system performance, reliability, access and scalability, and coordinate the resolution of integration and technical issues

**Grant Management System and Data Product Ownership:** Responsible for functional development of the data and results components in Salesforce, including requirement gathering, user acceptance criteria and testing, and leading historical data migration initiatives into the CRM.

**Data Quality and Documentation:** Responsible for establishing data definitions, business glossaries, calculation logic and SoPs across systems. Maintain system documentation, user guidance, data marketplace documentation, and administrative manuals to support self-service analytics.

**Business Intelligence, Analytics and Reporting:** Responsible for designing and maintaining user-centred dashboards and analytical products in Power BI or other approved platforms. Produce and interpret data on organisational KPIs, grants and portfolio performance for management, the Governing Board and donors, documenting sources, methods, calculations and limitations.

**Artificial Intelligence:** Explore practical uses of AI and automation in data processing, validation, retrieval, analysis and reporting, while also supporting pilot projects.

**Knowledge/Experience/Qualifications**

- Strong experience with IT and Business Intelligence tools (Python, SQL, Linux/Unix, Tableau, MSOffice/PowerBI), with at least five years of previous, progressive experience in a similar role.
- Excellent report-writing skills.
- Fluency in English; working knowledge of French is an advantage (B2-level). Russian and Arabic are also an asset.
- Master’s degree in Economics, Data Science, Statistics, International Relations, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Experience integrating AI into data systems is an asset.
- Previous experience or demonstrated interest in the prevention of radicalisation to violent extremism will be an asset.
- Detail-oriented, excellent coordination skills, must be able to work independently and have a keen interest in seeking tech solutions to improve efficiency.

**Values**

Demonstration of alignment with GCERF’s key values is a critical component of the selection process:

Make a difference

Achieve together

Uphold integrity

Respect yourself and others

Learn and improve

Be Kind

**Personal attributes based on GCERF competencies**

Be proactive

Work collaboratively

Be accountable and drive for solutions and results

Communicate effectively

Embrace learning and entrepreneurial spirit

**General information**: Our office is located in Geneva, Switzerland. Swiss residency or work eligibility is not a requirement.

GCERF values diversity, equality and inclusion, and we hire globally. We are committed to hiring qualified candidates irrespective of age, disability, ethnicity, national origin, family status, sex, gender identity or expression, physical characteristics, race, religion, spirituality or sexual orientation. GCERF has a zero tolerance policy towards sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as any form of discrimination or harassment. GCERF stands by its commitment to welcoming persons of all backgrounds into a safe work environment.

All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference checks and anti-terrorism screening.

Contract: 1 year, renewable. Part-time (32 hours per week). The arrangement of days and hours worked is flexible.

GCERF allows a limited number of remote working days per week.

Competitive compensation package.

jobs.title: Regional Coordinator, Programme - Danish RC

jobs.description:
## **Organizational Context**

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191-member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.
IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

DRC has been present in the Middle East & North Africa (MENA) region since 2002 and is implementing projects with National Society partners in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Yemen and oPt, and is working towards three main breakthroughs: 1) Healthy lives, 2) Disasters damage fewer lives and 3) Included and safe people.

The DRC Regional management is led by the Head of MENA, HoR Deputy and MENA HR manager. The management team ensures overall prioritization and leadership and is accountable for progress according to contractual and legal obligations. The regional management team ensures productive relations and alignment with Red Cross and Red Crescent movement and external partners.

## **Job Purpose**

The post-holder will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination and implementation of regional programmes and projects, working closely with the relevant Country Managers and country delegates, particularly in relation to the implementation of the NCD programme. The role will provide guidance and support to programme implementers and facilitate coordination with relevant programme and technical colleagues, with a particular focus on regional programmes in North Africa. The post-holder will also support country teams throughout the project cycle, including needs assessments, project design, implementation, monitoring and reporting.

## **Job Duties and Responsibilities**

Programme design and development (15%)

- Lead the strategic and innovative development of all relevant programme documents, especially but not limited to regional programs such as NCD and P2P
- Facilitate and coordinate assessments, baseline and end-line studies, mid-term reviews and evaluations for programme management and development.
- Organize, host and brief relevant technical assessment/evaluation missions, and communications visits.
- Facilitate NCD research initiatives together with the DRC NCD technical team, DRC country teams and NSs.
- Be involved in relevant NCD / P2P network in the region and with relevant RC partners, UN partners and other NCD actors.
- Ensure a strong focus on adaptive learning and evidence-based knowledge management.

Programme management (50%)

- Ensure implementation of country projects for the NCD and other regional initiatives on track, and that funds are utilized in accordance with budgets / plans, in close cooperation with the rest of the relevant Country Office Teams.
- Maintain an overview of the programme and corresponding country projects and alert Technical NCD leader or Deputy Head of Region if there are issues of concern.
- Participate in and contribute to the bi-monthly DRC Regional PPFU meeting and coordinate with Finance Officer for the programme as well as those related to North Africa.
- Support all programme reporting, including the annual Project Progress Reports (PPR) process – are completed on time and at high quality, allowing for technical reviews in advance of submission.
- Ensure consolidated programme reports are submitted to donors on time.
- Conduct field level programme monitoring in coordination with the relevant DRC CMs and NSs Specially on NCD and P2P programs
- Contribute to the DRCs effort to engage in wider coordination with relevant thematic activities in-countries and/or at regional level
- Consolidation results across all project locations and serves as the central point for overall reporting requirements (NCD)

## **Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)**

Capacity building of implementing partners (15%)

- Establish strong working relationships with the DRC country teams and help identify areas of support in the implementing NSs.
- Support implementing partners to strengthen their capacity for improved Health technical and Project Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (PMER) and learning and innovation skills.
- Provide programme management support to Country Offices, including temporary gap-filling support when required.
- Guide and support programme implementers and facilitate coordination with relevant programme and technical colleagues, particularly for regional programmes in North Africa.

Programme coordination and visibility (10%)

- Coordinate with key stakeholder internal or external to ensure the connection of the regional programmes.
- Represent the programme in relevant national, regional, and international fora
- Ensure visibility of the programme based on captured LL
- Facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing for Integrated programme initiatives and processes, including trainings, at regional and national level as per require in coordination with DRC HQ colleagues.

General programme support (10%)

- Support DHoR in preparing key documents, operational project documents and country project agreements.
- Explore fundraising possibilities for regional programmes related interventions and innovative development in coordination with the DHoR.
- Analyse, coordinate and support the feasibility of implementing programmes in North Africa.
- Perform any other relevant duty assigned by the DoHR

## **Education**

Required

- Relevant academic degree or equivalent experience from the field

Preferred

- Knowledge on any other thematic areas such as Disaster Risk Management, Migration, protection will be considered as an asset

## **Experience**

Required

- A minimum of 7 years of actual field experience in programme management or related project implementation.
- Proven experience in programme management in developing and/or conflict-affected countries.
- Information management and analytical skills, in assessment, project design, and programme financial management.
- Coordination skills, with an emphasis on working through and building the capacity of national partners.

Preffered

- Relevant post-graduate university degree in Health preferably or equivalent studies
- Experience of working in the Middle East in development or humanitarian contexts.
- Experience of working within the Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement
- Experience in narrative and financial reporting and proposal writing

## **Knowledge, Skills and Languages**

Required

- Self-supporting in computers (Email, Internet, spread sheets, word-processing, etc.)
- Excellent communication, organization and facilitation skills
- Confidence in situations of occasional stress, and able to handle a substantial but varied workload for a long period.
- Results-orientated and self-motivated but at the same time a patient, cooperative, innovative, and flexible team player.
- Understanding that process and ownership are key to achieving results in culturally and politically sensitive environments.

jobs.description:
The Global Safeguarding Manager is a senior technical specialist in AKF’s global safeguarding team, working closely with and under the supervision of the Global Safeguarding Lead. The postholder leads the day-to-day delivery of investigations and case management, provides hands-on technical support to Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points in AKF units, and turns learning from cases into practical improvements across AKF and, where applicable, the wider integrated AKF.

**Hybrid working, based in our London office, with an expectation to attend in person on a regular basis. This global role reports to HQ in Geneva, Switzerland, with regular international travel (approx. 20%), including to fragile contexts.**

**Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK; AKF will not sponsor visa applications.**

**4. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND CORE TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES**

**4.1 Investigations and Case Management (approximately 50%)**

- **Intake and Triage:** Manage the intake, triage and risk assessment of concerns received by the global function.
- **Investigations:** Plan and conduct complex and sensitive investigations into sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEAH), bullying, harassment, discrimination and related workplace misconduct, producing clear, evidence-based reports.
- **Oversight of Investigations:** Scope, commission and quality-assure investigations carried out by unit and external investigators, and develop the internal investigator pool.
- **Case Management:** Manage the global case register and ensure cases are handled in a survivor-centred, fair and confidential way, with outcomes followed through with HR and management.
- **Case Support to Units:** Provide case supervision to unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points and support units, in person or remotely, in responding to serious incidents.
- **Reporting and Learning:** Prepare routine incident notifications to donors and regulators, and analyse case trends to recommend improvements.

**4.2 Technical Support, Capacity Building and Policy Development (approximately 40%)**

- **Technical Advice:** Advise and support unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points, on site and remotely, to put global safeguarding standards into practice in their context, such as risk assessments, safeguarding in programmes and community-level safeguarding and reporting mechanisms.
- **Capability Building:** Identify capability gaps among unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points and provide mentoring, coaching and technical learning.
- **Training and Awareness:** Develop training content and lead awareness and capacity building for staff across AKF, including specialised training for different stakeholder groups, to reinforce a culture of integrity and ethics.
- **Policies and Procedures:** Lead the review and improvement of safeguarding policies, procedures, guidance and practical tools, drawing on case learning and sector, donor and regulatory standards.
- **Partners:** Advise on safeguarding due diligence and capacity strengthening for partners and contractors.

**4.3 Assurance (approximately 10%)**

- **Assurance Support:** Support delivery of the safeguarding assurance framework, including unit reviews and follow-up of improvement actions.

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive, and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties that align with their skills and experience.

**5. QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE, BEHAVIOURS, ATTRIBUTES**

**5.1 Qualifications:**

- Degree in law, criminology, social work, psychology, human rights, international development or a related field, or equivalent experience.
- Recognised investigation qualification, such as CHS Alliance IQTS Tier 3 or equivalent (essential).
- Ethics and compliance certification, such as CCEP or ISO 37301/37002 (desirable).

**5.2 Experience:**

- At least seven years’ safeguarding, ethics and compliance or workplace investigations experience in international development, humanitarian or comparable multi-country organisations, covering both technical support and investigations (essential).
- At least five years leading complex, high-risk investigations into SEAH, bullying, harassment, discrimination or related workplace misconduct, including cases involving senior staff, and quality-assuring investigations by others (essential).
- Demonstrated experience of providing technical support on general safeguarding to country or field teams, such as risk assessments, safeguarding in programmes, community reporting mechanisms and partner safeguarding (essential).
- Proven experience of designing and delivering safeguarding training and capacity building for different audiences, and of mentoring safeguarding staff across countries (essential).
- Experience of developing practical safeguarding procedures, guidance and tools (essential).
- Experience in ethics and compliance, speak-up/whistleblowing programmes or workplace investigations, including in corporate, public or regulated sectors (desirable).
- Donor and regulatory reporting; experience in humanitarian, development, health, education or child-focused settings (desirable).

**5.3 Knowledge and Skills:**

- Expert knowledge of safeguarding and PSEAH frameworks and sector standards (e.g. IASC Six Core Principles, CHS, Keeping Children Safe), survivor-centred practice and procedural fairness.
- Excellent investigative interviewing, analytical and report-writing skills, and sound judgement under pressure.
- Ability to coach, influence and constructively challenge colleagues at all levels and across cultures.
- Fluent English essential; French, Portuguese, Russian, Dari, Urdu, Arabic or Swahili an asset.

**5.4 Behaviours:**

- **Politically aware & discreet:** Navigates complex, multicultural environments with strong stakeholder awareness, sound judgment, and a high level of confidentiality and discretion.
- **Clear & effective communicator:** Communicates complex information with clarity, adapts messaging to diverse audiences, and ensures timely, transparent communication.
- **Collaborative & low-ego mindset:** Builds strong relationships, works seamlessly across teams, and adopts a hands-on approach with a focus on collective outcomes over hierarchy.
- **Reliable execution & accountability:** Takes ownership to ensure cases and agreed actions move forward with local management in each country, manages multiple priorities with strong attention to detail, and follows through consistently.
- **Agile & resilient under pressure:** Adapts to changing priorities and organisational contexts, operates effectively in high-pressure environments, and remains solution oriented.

**6. KEY RELATIONSHIPS**

**Internal Relationships**

- Global Director of Operations
- Global Safeguarding Coordinator
- Global HR, Procurement, Programmes, Finance
- Unit Safeguarding Managers/Focal Points
- Unit leadership and HR teams
- Safeguarding counterparts in AKDN agencies

**External Relationships**

- External investigators and consultants
- Survivor support and referral services
- Implementing partners
- Inter-agency safeguarding networks
- Institutional donors and regulators

**7. APPLICATION DETAILS**

- Send a CV and a supporting statement (max. one side of A4) on why you want the role and how you meet the essential requirements, with your preferred salary and notice period.
- Application link: [PLEASE APPLY HERE](https://krb-xjobs.brassring.com/TGnewUI/Search/home/HomeWithPreLoad?partnerid=30025&siteid=5750&PageType=JobDetails&jobid=2299513#jobDetails=2299513_5750)
- Closing Date: **6TH December 2026**
- Salary commensurate with experience + benefits
- Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK; no visa sponsorship.

**Scope of the role**

Violent extremism is a direct threat to international security, economic growth, and development. GCERF works to prevent violent extremism by investing in people. As the only global fund dedicated to preventing violent extremism (PVE), we connect local communities to global resources and support grassroots initiatives that are often out of reach for international donors. We fund community-centric initiatives led by civil society organisations to address the local social, economic, and political drivers of violent extremism.

The Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist will be part of GCERF’s dynamic and high-performing team of Monitoring and Evaluation experts. This role is responsible for ensuring the quality of monitoring, evaluation and evidence across assigned grants, including results frameworks, assessments, and evaluations. Provides technical support to the Performance & Impact unit in line with the role holder’s expertise.

We expect this to require at least 6 years of progressively responsible experience in a similar role. At least two years’ professional experience in one of GCERF’s partner countries or similar contexts.

Make a difference

GCERF values diversity, equality and inclusion, and we hire globally. Overview of position

**Nature of the consultancy:**

**Deliverable Based Consultancy (output-based)**

Research, data, consultation and in-person facilitation support to the International Consultant for the gender-sensitive Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic for Somalia and for the co-creation and validation of the Climate Mobility Programme for integration into the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible.

**Project Context and Scope:**

**Background**

Recurrent droughts, floods and environmental degradation, combined with fragility and conflict, drive large-scale human mobility and displacement in Somalia. The National Adaptation Plan (NAP 2.0, 2026–2030) and the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) both recognise human mobility in the context of climate change as a priority. However, limited consolidated data and institutional capacity make it difficult to turn these commitments into investment-ready interventions, and human mobility is not yet well reflected in the NDC 3.0 Investment Plan 2025–2030 launched by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MoECC) at COP 30. The MoECC has asked the client to help address this.

This consultancy is part of the client’s Development Fund project “Strengthening Climate Mobility Investment Readiness in Somalia: Advancing NAP and NDC Implementation”, under Output 1.1 (Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic) and Output 1.2 (Climate Mobility Programme).

Role objectives

**Working arrangement**

The assignment is delivered by two consultants working as one team. The **International Consultant** (home-based) leads the technical work and presents online at all workshops (unless travel is confirmed). The **National Consultant** (Somalia-based) starts one month earlier to compile data and map stakeholders, supports the data collection and consultations and organizes and facilitates all workshops and events in person, with logistical support from the client’s project team. All work is carried out with the MoECC and its Inter-Ministerial NDC Taskforce. The client’s Climate Action Department and Regional Climate Action Unit (Nairobi) provide technical support and quality assurance.

**Main tasks**

Under the supervision of the client and the day-to-day technical guidance of the International Consultant, the National Consultant will:

**Data and evidence:** compile a literature review and secondary data (climate, socio-economic, displacement and human mobility) from national and international sources, and complete a stakeholder mapping.

**Consultations:** adapt and translate (English/Somali) the KII/FGD guides developed by the International Consultant, and conduct consultations with government, technical agencies and communities, including women and girls and other vulnerable groups.

**Workshops and events:** organize and facilitate in person, with logistical support from the client’s project team and the International Consultant presenting online: (i) the inception workshop; (ii) a combined workshop to validate the Country Diagnostic and co-create the Climate Mobility Programme; and (iii) the Programme validation workshop. Provide interpretation, minutes and a consolidated summary of feedback for each.

**Coordination with the MoECC:** support a climate mobility working group under the existing Inter-Ministerial NDC Taskforce, and liaise with the MoECC to obtain and compile relevant information on the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

Community Stabilization Unit, Transition and Recovery Pillar (TRP), the client.

Project: “Strengthening Climate Mobility Investment Readiness in Somalia: Advancing NAP and NDC Implementation” – project code SO10P0800, funded by the client’s Development Fund (IDF).

**Tangible and measurable outputs** **of the work assignment**

The National Consultant will deliver the following outputs on a three-instalment payment basis. Months refer to the months of this contract (Month 1 = the month the Consultant starts); the International Consultant starts in Month 2:

**Deliverable 1 – Workplan and Stakeholder Mapping (max. 10 pages).** – Deliverable by email by mid-Month 1.

**Deliverable 2 – Literature Review and Secondary Data Compilation (max. 20 pages, plus dataset):** ready for the International Consultant when they start in Month 2. – **First instalment payment (Deliverables 1–2)** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 1.

**Deliverable 3 – Inception Workshop and Stakeholder Consultations Report (max. 20 pages):** inception workshop facilitated in person (end of Month 2) with minutes; translated tools; consultations conducted and findings summarized. – Deliverable by email by end of Month 3.

**Deliverable 4 – Validation and Co-Creation Workshop:** workshop facilitated in person in late Month 4 to validate the Country Diagnostic findings and co-create the Climate Mobility Programme; minutes and consolidated results. – **Second instalment payment (Deliverables 3–4)** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 4.

**Final Deliverable 5 – Programme Validation Workshop:** workshop facilitated in person (mid-Month 6); minutes and consolidated feedback for the final Programme; compiled information on the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible. – **Third and final instalment payment** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 6.

Each deliverable may go through more than one draft; it is considered complete once the client’s feedback has been incorporated and the client has approved it.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

Deliverables submitted on time and approved by the client.

Data compilation and consultations complete, well-sourced and inclusive of women, girls and other vulnerable groups.

All three workshops held as planned, with MoECC and Taskforce participation, and minutes and feedback delivered within one week.

Effective coordination with the International Consultant and the client’s project team.

**Payment terms and conditions**

Lump-sum fee paid in three instalments against approved deliverables:

**First instalment – 25% :** Deliverables 1–2 – Workplan and Stakeholder Mapping; Literature Review and Secondary Data Compilation (Month 1).

**Second instalment – 50% :** Deliverables 3–4 – Inception Workshop and Consultations Report; Validation and Co-Creation Workshop (Month 4).

**Third and final instalment – 25%:** Deliverable 5 – Programme Validation Workshop (Month 6).

Payments are released upon the client’s approval of the respective deliverables, together with a short progress report (achievements, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations against the approved workplan), and are subject to satisfactory confirmation by the Programme Manager. - Exciting senior leadership opportunity on a flagship FCDO-funded HEROS 2.0 programme
- Fixed Term
- London, United Kingdom

## **About us**

With over 40 years of humanitarian and development experience, [Tetra Tech](https://www.tetratech.com/) is a trusted humanitarian delivery partner globally. We have tried and tested **a humanitarian response capability, spanning** logistics, humanitarian advisory, operational and technical expertise, and people who can deploy rapidly. We are a gold-level supplier to the FCDO and the lead contractor for the DFAT-funded **Australia Assists Phase 2, Humanitarian Logistics Capability Phase II, and the Pacific Humanitarian Warehousing Program** **Infrastructure Specialist Unit ISU**.

Tetra Tech International Development Europe is Tetra Tech’s European business unit focused on international development project management, technical advisory, and monitoring and evaluation services. We have a 40-year history of successfully delivering humanitarian and international development projects on behalf of donors around the world, including the UK’s Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the European Union (EU), Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), the United States Department of State (DOS), development banks and multilateral institutions. We are a trusted provider of humanitarian and emergency response assistance globally. Our people are focused on improving lives and work side by side with local partners to support sustainable economic growth, stability, governance, and environmental and climate practices. You can find out more about our international development work with UK and European clients [here](https://intdev.tetratecheurope.com/).

## The Programme

The upcoming Humanitarian Emergency Response Operations and Stabilisation programme (HEROS 2.0) will enable FCDO to respond rapidly, at scale, to global humanitarian disasters and support work on protracted crises, chronic emergencies and humanitarian reform. It will provide FCDO with a flexible model to support the UK Government’s conflict, stabilisation and security work in fragile and conflict-affected states, both during steady state periods and in response to new crises. HEROS 2.0 will deliver the following overarching capabilities:

1\. Humanitarian & Conflict Early Warning & Analysis (EWAR): Expert analytical capability to provide horizon-scanning for global humanitarian and conflict risk drivers, presenting this information and analysis to FCDO.

2\. Standing Humanitarian Expertise: Technical expert capacity to provide advice, analysis, and evidence products in support of FCDO’s humanitarian planning, preparedness and response. This capacity will be deployable globally to provide ‘first response’ support to sudden-onset humanitarian crises, in addition to supporting protracted crises and system reform. This capacity will cover a range of technical specialisms alongside a core generalist humanitarian skill set (Indicative specialisms include: Shelter, WASH, Health, Cash, Preparedness, Protection & Inclusion, Resilience, Localisation & Participation).

3\. Scalable Expertise: Capability to deploy, at pace, technical expertise for FCDO to fulfil specific, time-limited advisory and analytical requirements across humanitarian, conflict and security objectives.

4\. Humanitarian Logistics: End-to-end logistics function to plan, scope, source and deploy equipment and humanitarian supplies in response to crises, as required by FCDO. This capability may include the management of UKAid stockpiles, in the UK and globally, as well as rapid sourcing and delivery in response to crisis demand.

## The Role

Duties and Responsibilities

This is a unique role and opportunity to lead one of FCDO’s largest humanitarian programmes providing leadership to a flagship humanitarian support activity. The **HEROS 2.0 Director** will provide senior leadership and overall management of the HEROS 2.0 programme, leading the core delivery team and acting as the main counterpart to the FCDO. The role will ensure effective delivery across all programme components, including early warning and analysis, expert advisory support, deployments, procurement and logistics, standby partnership deployments, and UNDAC-related support. The Director will be responsible for strategic oversight, stakeholder engagement, programme performance, risk management, and ensuring the programme remains ready to respond rapidly to humanitarian emergencies and protracted crises.

## The Person

*Essential:*

- Minimum 15 years of relevant experience in the humanitarian sector
- Proven experience in humanitarian delivery, including first-phase emergency response.
- Demonstrated experience working with FCDO in the UK and overseas Posts.
- Proven experience in senior leadership positions, with responsibility for teams, strategy, and delivery.
- Experience leading or working within humanitarian networks and coordination mechanisms.
- Knowledge of the UN humanitarian system and experience of working with UN programmes and agencies.
- Strong leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills.

*Desirable*

- SC or DV security clearance
- Technical knowledge of conflict and stabilisation
- Direct experience of humanitarian assistance implementation with NGOs
- Previous Team Leader experience on FCDO programmes
- Prior experience of HSOT delivery or similar humanitarian response programmes
- Familiarity with the UNDAC deployments
- Familiarity with humanitarian procurement, logistics and warehouse management
- Confidence with MIS solutions and technological developments in the humanitarian space

**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Vacancy Closure Date: 23 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zPWKGabdFSzUtF9pkcm7vR_poJ8-_L84/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zPWKGabdFSzUtF9pkcm7vR_poJ8-_L84/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

To this end, there is a need to strengthen the human resource function itself, including its organization, processes, policies, systems, and service delivery arrangements. A strengthened HR function is essential to support workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, career progression, and other core personnel processes, while also providing the institutional capacity required to support the wider CDR reform programme. In this context, the HR function needs to move beyond the administration of personnel matters toward a more structured and integrated approach to workforce management aligned with CDR's functions, organizational structure, and operational priorities.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Human Resources Expert to support CDR in implementing the human resource measures under Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will review and update the existing and proposed job descriptions against the applicable legislative framework and operational requirements, reassess the HR function identified, and translate the findings into an HR Strategy, HR Policies and Procedures Manual, and target operating model for the Human Resources Department. The assignment will also ensure that the HR Strategy incorporates the human resource requirements arising from other reform areas, including change management and the development and implementation of a Human Resource Information System.

Through this assignment, the Expert will contribute to establishing a clearer, more functional, and sustainable human resource framework for CDR, with defined roles and responsibilities, updated job descriptions, appropriate HR policies and procedures, and an operating model capable of supporting both CDR's immediate staffing needs and the longer-term institutional reforms identified in the roadmap.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Human Resources Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Assessment of the Human Resource Function and HR Strategy**

- Review human resource arrangements, relevant institutional findings and proposed reform priorities to establish the baseline for the assessment.
- Review the legal and regulatory framework that governs CDR staff, including Decree No. 10941 of 2003, Decree No. 10942 of 2003, Section 54 of the 2004 Budget Law, the Council of Ministers freeze on hiring and promotion, the allowance decrees issued between 2021 and 2025, the Council of Ministers decision of 19 June 2025 and the internal regulations of CDR, and record for each human resource process the rule that governs it and the authority that approves it.
- Validate the workforce baseline with the Administrative Affairs Division, covering filled and vacant mandated posts, individual contractors, project implementation unit personnel, projected retirements, resignations and multi-role assignments, and identify any figures that are not substantiated by the available records.
- Assess the mandate, organization, staffing and capacity of the Human Resources Department within the Administrative Affairs Division.
- Map the human resource processes as they operate today, covering workforce planning, recruitment and onboarding, personnel records, attendance and leave, performance evaluation and promotion, training, discipline, and separation and end-of-service, and record where a process is informal, paper-based or undocumented.
- Identify the gaps between current practice, the legal framework and the needs of the reformed structure, and distinguish the gaps that CDR can close within the current legal framework from those that depend on the amendment of Decree No. 10941 and Decree No. 10942.
- Establish the baseline and the method of measurement for human resource indicators including the employee-satisfaction baseline survey, coordinated with the staff survey used for the change indicators so that staff are surveyed once.
- Prepare the HR Strategy for CDR, setting out its objectives, priority measures, responsibilities and sequence, aligned with the Target Roadmap and the Interim Arrangements, and addressing the vacancy, multi-role and key-person dependency risks identified.
- Set out in the Strategy the recruitment route for the transitional period and the longer-term recruitment model, consistent with the position on the Civil Service Board mandate.
- Define the target operating model of the Human Resources Department, comprising its functions, roles, reporting lines and staffing, and its role as business owner of the Human Resource Information System.
- Set out in the Strategy the human resource input to the Change Management Committee on the resistance factors linked to restructuring, redeployment and remuneration, and coordinate the staff messages on these matters with the Change Management and Communications Expert.
- Set out in the Strategy the business requirements of the Human Resources Department for the Human Resource Information System identified, validating the human resource process definitions, the business rules for attendance, leave and missions, and the employee data structure, and confirming the legal basis of the end-of-service calculation before any procurement.
- Prepare the action plan that implements the Strategy, with responsibilities assigned by post and timing reconciled with the master roadmap.

**Workstream 2. Review and Update of Job Descriptions**

- Compile the inventory of the job descriptions already prepared, comprising those prepared by the Administrative Affairs Division including identified positions, Terms of Reference, job description summaries and IT Department job descriptions, and identify the existing and new posts for which no description exists.
- Review each JD against the applicable legislation, including the ranks, sub-grades and qualification requirements under Decree No. 10942, the divisional and departmental mandates under Decree No. 10941 and the reformed structure, and, for procurement posts, the requirements of Law No. 244 of 2021 on the competencies and career paths of procurement staff.
- Review each description against the operational needs of CDR, testing with the Heads of Division whether the scope of work, reporting lines, decision rights and qualifications correspond to the work the role performs under the redesigned business processes.
- Harmonize the descriptions into a single template that records, for each post, the interim placement within the current structure and the position under the reformed structure, so that the same document serves recruitment now and redeployment later.
- Update the descriptions on the basis of the review, remove overlaps between posts, reflect the segregation of duties required in the financial management, procurement and ICT processes, and complete the descriptions for the posts not yet covered.
- Reconcile the rank assigned to each post with the indicative costing identified, and record each discrepancy for the remuneration and financing proposal.
- Confirm the updated descriptions with the Heads of Division and prepare the submission through which the Board approves them.
- Prepare the procedure through which the Administrative Affairs Division maintains the descriptions as the structure changes, and brief the Division on its application.

**Workstream 3. HR Policies, Performance Management and Capacity Development**

- Prepare the HR Policies and Procedures Manual, documenting each human resource process with its steps, responsibilities, approvals, time standards and forms, and removing steps whose risk does not justify them before the process is digitized.
- Review the performance-evaluation system for promotion reactivated in 2025, and propose how it draws on the updated job descriptions within the promotion rules of Decree No. 10942.
- Prepare the human resource provisions on employee protection, covering discrimination and workplace misconduct, conflict-of-interest declarations for staff holding more than one role, and disciplinary consequences for retaliation, in coordination with the Audit Committee, which owns the whistleblower policy set out, and with the Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert.
- Prepare the competency-based capacity development strategy, consolidating the role-based learning pathways with the identified function-specific training and defining the training-needs assessment method, the format of the annual training plan and the pre- and post-training assessment of competency.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 11 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within three months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Human Resources Management, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Management, Public Policy, Law, or a related field.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) assessing and strengthening human resource functions and organizational structures, including workforce planning, HR processes, job descriptions, performance management, recruitment, staff development and HR policies; and (ii) designing and implementing HR strategies, operating models, policies and procedures, including HR information systems and competency-based capacity development frameworks.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Protection from Violence Programme Development Manager Ethiopia Addis Ababa
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC Ethiopia is looking for a dynamic and strategic **Protection from Violence (PFV) Programme Development Manager (PDM)** to provide technical leadership and drive the growth, quality and impact of its Protection from Violence programming.

In this role, you will lead the technical development and strategic direction of the PFV Core Competency, spearhead programme development and fundraising initiatives, and ensure high-quality programme delivery across the operation. You will also strengthen technical capacity through staff mentoring, training and coaching, while providing oversight of programme quality, MEAL, budget management and procurement to ensure effective implementation and accountability.

We are looking for a leader who can translate protection priorities into impactful programmes, build strong technical teams and drive sustainable programming that responds to the needs of people affected by displacement and violence.

*Please note: This opportunity is open exclusively to Ethiopian nationals.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your generic responsibilities:

- Develop and implement the Protection from Violence strategy for NRC Ethiopia including Macro Log frames that are aligned with country and global strategies priorities.
- Develop technical standards, SOPs, guidance documents for PFV across NRC Ethiopia, under the guidance of NRC’s PFV Global Advisers
- Promote the rights of conflict- and displacement-affected people in line with the advocacy strategy. Undertake Protection Advocacy initiatives.
- Contribute to fundraising, develop and revise funding proposal, budgets and donor reports.
- Overall technical management and mentorship of project staff across NRC Ethiopia
- Provide systematic training and build capacity of technical staff, in approaches including cash-based interventions and market-based programme
- Oversee PFV project(s) implementation across NRC Ethiopia, including development and oversight of Community Feedback Mechanism
- Lead the localization agenda of NRC Ethiopia for PFV. Identify meaningful partners for strategic cooperation aiming to advance PFV portfolio across Ethiopia.
- Follow up on compliance with contractual commitments within PFV, ensure high technical quality products
- Ensure that key learnings are extracted from Protection from Violence implementation, and incorporate them in Protection from Violence and staff development processes
- Represent NRC in relevant forums/clusters, including with national authorities and donors

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAt92z8Iv4rSqzgkeTdghASAZNyyCLKN07CJRmwR94cBx8?e=poxnT3) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Graduate degree with minimum 5 years of relevant experience from a senior level project implementation position in a humanitarian/recovery context.
- Excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency and displacement situations
- Detailed knowledge of humanitarian and protection principles and guidelines for humanitarian assistance
- Good understanding of Protection Cluster coordination mechanisms
- Strong coordination, representation skills and inter-personal skills, working well both in teams and independently
- Self-motivated and excellent observer of protection issues
- Able to work under pressure and good at timely decision making
- Excellent written and spoken English
- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets
- Strong experience in programme development and management
- Experience in training facilitation and capacity-building
- Experience in Ethiopia mandatory
- Willingness to spend a significant period of time at NRC’s Area Offices
- This position is open to Ethiopian nationals only.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
- Contract: 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH
