jobs.description:
***About FHI 360 and AFGHS-FHI 360***

FHI 360 is a nonprofit human development organization dedicated to improving lives in lasting ways by advancing integrated, locally driven solutions. Our staff includes experts in health, education, nutrition, economic development, youth, research, technology, communication, and social marketing—creating a unique mix of capabilities to address today’s interrelated development challenges. FHI 360 serves more than 60 countries and all U.S. states and territories.

The **America First Global Health Strategy – FHI 360 (AFGHS-FHI 360)** project is initially a 13-month project (2026 – 2027) with the ability to be extended for up to five years (though 2031). Funded by the United States (US) Department of State (DOS), AFGHS-FHI 360 is a global fixed amount award (FAA) and operates in approximately 50 countries, addressing key public health challenges such as HIV/AIDS, global health security (GHS), maternal and neonatal child health (MNCH), malaria, tuberculosis (TB), polio, supply chain (SC) and health systems strengthening (HSS). In Thailand, AFGHS-FHI 360 will continue to build off the country’s progress to date to future strengthen the country’s health systems responses to HIV/AIDS, GHS, and malaria. AFGHS-FHI 360 is recruiting a Project Director located in Bangkok, Thailand. This position is open to Thai nationals only.

***Job Summary:***

The AFGHS-FHI 360 Thailand Project Director provides overall leadership, management and strategic direction of the AFGHS-FHI 360 project in Thailand. The Project Director will oversee the implementation of the AFGHS-FHI 360 HIV/AIDS, GHS, and malaria portfolio in Thailand with a focus on health systems strengthening. They will ensure that project goals and objectives are achieved within the prescribed project milestones, time frame and funding parameters. They will serve as the primary point of contact for AFGHS-FHI 360 activities in Thailand and provide technical and management leadership to the country project and ensure successful implementation of the work plan to achieve project milestones, monitoring of expenditures in lines with the approved budget, achievement of the project’s targets and goals, and identification, mitigation and escalation of risk. They will be required to coordinate and work with a diverse group of organizations and stakeholders, such as the Ministry of Health, senior government officials, country health staff, international and national development partner organizations, and the United States Government (USG) donor representatives.

Reporting to the Regional Director, the Project Director works in close collaboration with the AFGHS-FHI 360 headquarters (HQ) team, planning and directing project implementation, milestone success, and monitoring budget/spending from startup through closeout. Under a matrixed structure, they lead the country project team in the planning of project activities ensuring completion of the project on schedule and within budget constraints.

***Accountabilities:***

- Direct overall project vision, design, planning and implementation; ensures that goals and objectives are accomplished within prescribed time frame and contractual parameters.
- Ensure internal management systems for contracting, recruitment, and delivery; move rapidly to respond to the demands for service delivery on the ground.
- Foster innovation and new ideas for better targeted, and more cost-efficient and effective strategies to reach project beneficiaries and retain them in services, as applicable to scope.
- Develop, manage, and strengthen strategic relationships with government entities, implementing partners, local organizations, and other stakeholders to advance project objectives and foster collaboration.
- Ensure achievement of contractual targets, milestones, and deliverables by leading effective milestone and performance management processes, monitoring progress, mitigating risks, and ensuring activities remain on schedule, within budget, and compliant with donor requirements.
- Identify and pursue opportunities to leverage complementary donor, governmental, and organizational resources through strategic partnerships, collaboration agreements, and aligned programming.
- Provide leadership and management to project staff within a matrixed management structure, ensuring clear priorities, effective teamwork, staff onboarding, performance management, professional development, and accountability for the timely delivery of high-quality project results.
- Work closely with AFGHS-FHI 360 HQ on the development of annual work plans, milestone plans and budgets for timely submission to and approval by USG to implement those plans.
- Serve as the primary contact to the global AFGHS-FHI 360 HQ project team.
- Serve as the primary liaison with the Regional Strategic Assistance Section (RSA)/DOS Thailand staff, maintaining strong donor relationships and ensuring effective communication, responsiveness, and coordination between the project team and donor representatives.

- Serve as a member of the FHI 360 Thailand Senior Leadership Team and provide input and assistance to the management of the country program, develop country program strategy, business plans, operational plans and budgets.
- Research sources for potential funding and contribute to proposal development, as requested.
- Responsible for creating, promoting, and maintaining safe and equitable work environments for all personnel, including a harassment- and violence-free work culture, and systems for safeguarding project participants.
- Support performance management and professional development of direct reports, including ongoing feedback, coaching, and career support.
- Potentially serve as FHI 360’s Country Representative (CR) for the country depending on current country project portfolio.
- Other tasks as appropriate to the position.

***Applied Knowledge & Skills:***

- Comprehensive knowledge of theories, concepts and practices with project management, process development and execution.
- Excellent and demonstrated project management skills.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills.
- Strong consultative and negotiation skills.
- Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to plan, organize, and manage resources for successful completion of projects.

***Problem Solving & Impact:***

- Decisions and actions have a significant impact on management and division operations.

***Education: \*\****

***Experience: \*\****

jobs.title: Hydrology Database Manager
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Geoscience Energy and Maritime (GEM) Division** provides advice, technical assistance, research and training support to Pacific Island countries and territories (PICTs). There are four (4) areas of scientific programming within this division:

1. **Oceans and Maritime Programme (OMP)** – assists member countries with services that provide applied ocean science and knowledge for evidence-based policy-making and technical solutions for improved ocean and maritime governance, management and capacity development.
2. **Georesources and Energy Programme (GEP)** – assists member countries by applying technical knowledge in the areas of geoscience and sustainable energy use.
3. **Disaster and Water Resilience Programme (DWRP)** – assists member countries to demonstrate strengthened resilience through integrated action on disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, natural resource management and increased access to water and sanitation.
4. **Earth and Ocean Observation Services** – Promoting spatial data and systems analysis and capacity to improve decision-making to improve resilience and sustainable resource management.

The role – **Hydrology Database Manager** will support the improvement of the integrity, accessibility, and usability of hydrological data across the Pacific region, strengthening information systems and decision-making for drought management.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Technical Advice and Support**

- Provide high-quality technical advice and support on water resource related technical and research needs at the regional, national and local levels.
- Provide high-quality technical advice and support to manage and maintain hydrological databases, including data quality assurance, data integration, data analysis and processing, user support and training, system development and upgrades, data sharing and accessibility, documentation and compliance.

**Networking and Communications**

- Establish and develop effective communication and relationships within member countries, development partners, and SPC to promote drought monitoring, and water resource assessment, development, and management for the region.
- Ensure accurate, audience focused sensitive water resource information is accessible and available to a wide variety of relevant stakeholders.

**Capacity Building**

- Design and implement a structured approach to capacity building in participating member countries to strengthen the long-term capacity of country counterparts in drought monitoring, hydrology, data management, data analysis other water resource assessment and analysis skills.

**Provision of high-quality technical reporting**

- Provision of high-quality technical reports ensuring SPC standards are met for publication.

**Support project implementation**

- Project implementation actions and requirements are undertaken and completed with efficiency, and within SPC policy and procedures.
- Provide support for resource mobilisation for ongoing sustainability.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A bachelor of science degree with a specialisation in a relevant field such as hydrology, hydrogeology, geophysics or water resources engineering or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7-8 years of experience in hydrological services and demonstrated experience working with hydrological databases.
- Experienced in the application and analysis of hydrological data, and database management to develop information products.
- Demonstrated experience in the use and application of GIS.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement and report writing skills.
- Demonstrated project management and organisational skills, including working and managing projects in remote locations.
- Knowledge of Gender Equity and Social Inclusion (GESI), and People Centred Approaches (PCA) in delivery of projects.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **1 year** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Hydrology Database Manager** is a band 10 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 2,703‒3,379 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 8,354–10,442 (USD 3,623-4,528; EUR 3,269-4,086). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Technical Head of Program Ukraine M/F/X
jobs.description:
**Place: Kyiv, Ukraine**
**Starting Date : February 2027**
**Length of contrat : 12 months**

**We will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.**

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview.

**CONTEXTUALISATION**

From February 2022, HI has re-opened a Country Programme in Ukraine to respond to the humanitarian needs triggered by the full-scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation.

In 2026, HI pillars of interventions are:

- Health: HI aims to improve access to quality physical rehabilitation and mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS) for conflict-affected vulnerable population.
- Protection: Given the scale of humanitarian and protection needs, HI intervenes at various levels to ensure that vulnerable conflict-affected populations have access to multi-sectoral services tailored to their needs. In addition, HI aims to foster a disability-inclusive humanitarian response.
- Humanitarian Mine Action: Ongoing attacks dangerously exacerbated Explosive Ordnance (EO) contamination in Ukraine. HI implements EORE/CPP, Advocacy, NTS/TS/Clearance, VA (Victim Assistance)

HI has 2 hubs, one in the East (based in Dnipro), one in the North East (based in Kharkiv), and the coordination office is in Kyiv.

The position is based in Kiev. The security situation in Ukraine remains relatively stable, although air alert is frequently active. However, markets, restaurants and cafes are open, and life continues as normal. There is a strict curfew, the hours depend on the region

**Technical Head of Program**

**1. Main Mission**

Under the responsibility of the Country Director, the Technical Head of Programme contributes to the implementation of Humanité & Inclusion's mandate and 10-year strategy within his/her programme.

He/she is the driving force behind the programmatic development of social missions within his/her technical scope, and ensures that the quality and impact of the projects implemented in the programme are optimised, in line with the priorities defined in the Technical Strategies.

The Technical Head of Program is responsible for a team of specialists (Technical Field Specialist, Business Developer, MEAL and quality assurance).

**Mission 1: Management**

- Embodies HI's values on a daily basis, and is a role model.
- Understands the strategy, makes it explicit, translating it into operational objectives for the team, leads the necessary changes.
- Organises the operational management of his or her team, structures the work around identified processes, steers performance, and facilitates problem solving.
- Contributes to the development of its employees, creating the conditions to enable their commitment, their professionalism and their attachment to HI.

**2. Responsibilities**

**2.1. Strategy and Management**

- Proposes the development of the programmatic framework of the programme's StratOp, based on an analysis of the sectoral context and following the StraTechs and Development Plans of the Emergency, Atlas and Impact-Innovation-Information divisions, in conjunction with the operational teams.
- Ensures the deployment of cross-cutting approaches within programming, promotes cross-sectoral synergies and intervention themes.
- Proposes the design and evolution of the programme's technical support, based on the skills of the technical specialists and technical profiles assigned to the projects, and according to the key priority sectors and the skills of the project managers.
- Contributes, at least once a year, (regarding its projects and data) to the annual monitoring of the StratOp and to the planning of the following year's programmes (i.e. support missions and evaluations).
- Ensures the MEAL part of the Operational Strategy, pilots the related action plan and the strategy monitoring tool.

**2.2. Development of the Social Mission and Programmatic Vision**

Defines the programme's funding strategy for new themes or innovations in existing sectors, ensures the development of opportunities for each theme within its scope, proposes the geographical development of HI sectors, and ensures the conformity of the technical proposal with nexus issues.

- Provides support to the Country Director and Ops Manager in considering the development of new value propositions (including needs assessment, feasibility, strategic alliances, major contracts).
- Contributes to the development of the fundraising strategy, in coordination with the Operations Manager / Senior Grant Officer.
- Leads the transformation of financial opportunities into projects.
- Produces and drives the design of major projects (multiple countries, one or more themes) or new strategic projects in the Country.
- Identifies and develops regional or local partnerships and/or consortia with NGOs, institutions, companies on technical priorities or important themes in the region in collaboration with the Ops Manager.

**2.3. Quality Standards and Expertise with the MEAL and Technical Profiles of the Programme**

Controls and monitors the technical quality and relevance of HI activities within its scope:

- Ensures that project managers receive appropriate technical and methodological guidance and support from MEAL team members and specialists based at headquarters or at programme level.
- Ensures quality control of projects and the programme and raises alerts and recommendations.
- Follows up the implementation of recommendations from support missions, evaluation or audit, as appropriate.
- Ensures a local sectoral watch and collects good practices.

**Responsibilities Related to MEAL**

- Ensures the improvement of the quality of project management processes, as defined by the Planning Monitoring and Evaluation (PME) policy.
- Leads the improvement of HI's response, including the implementation of impact and effect measurement tools.
- Establishes mechanisms for accountability to beneficiaries.
- Ensures the appropriation of programmes and HI’s frameworks and learning methodologies globally.
- Supports the monitoring of projects.

**Technical Expertise, Learning and Innovation**

- Ensures that specialists develop a local professional channel/talent pool and contributes to the animation of the professional channel of the technical divisions and the MEALs.
- Ensures the development of research and innovation projects in the region, when appropriate.
- Ensures deployment and compliance with global frameworks, institutional policies and standards.

**2.4. External Representation and Promotion of HI's Expertise**

- Represents HI's expertise in all relevant networks (including clusters).
- Supports the specialists and the Country Director in the representation towards partners, institutional donors and authorities.
- Contributes to advocacy (including evidence-based) on specific issues, in line with the StratOp and federal advocacy priorities.
- Contributes locally to communication messages, in line with the StratOp and federal communication priorities.

**2.5. Emergency Preparedness and Response**

- Leads the emergency preparedness actions in his/her department and, in case of emergency, reorganizes the priorities of his/her team according to the humanitarian imperative, in order to ensure a rapid and effective response from HI.

## Requirements

- Master’s degree in one of HI's technical sectors of intervention and/or international cooperation and/or humanitarian development
- You have a minimum of 5 years’ experience in humanitarian development with experience in project management (multi or complex) and experience(s) in one of HI's technical sectors of intervention.
- Excellent english language skills
- You have strong managerial skills: Being able to develop team members: developing the ability of staff to work independently.
- You know how to position yourself to make things happen
- Excellent organization and time management skills: you know how to simplify and prioritize
- You’re a good communicator, Ability to manage stress, Empathy, Autonomy and flexibility

## Benefits

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission:

- 12 months International contract starting from 15h, January 2027;
- The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
- Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
- Pension scheme;
- Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
- Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
- Salary from 2869 gross/month upon experience;
- Perdiem: 597€ net/month - paid in the payroll
- Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary;
- Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
- R&R: according to the level of the mission Level 3: 5 days every 8 weeks => + possible transport/package support;
- Position:
- **Unaccompanied:**
- Payment for travel costs (air ticket & visa) and transport of your personal effects; (from 12 months of mission)
- Mission of more than 12 months: a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child (from the second child) paid in the payroll;
- Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI;
- If you are resident in the country: local package.

jobs.description:
**Request For Quotation for supplying office cleaning materials and cleaning service for the ILO Erbil Office**

1\. Background
The International Labour Organization (ILO) requires professional cleaning services for its office located at the World Trade Center in Erbil, Iraq. The objective of this assignment is to maintain a clean, hygienic, safe, and professional working environment for ILO personnel and visitors throughout the contract period.

2\. Service Location
ILO Erbil Office
World Trade Center Erbil, Iraq Office Area: Approximately 204 m²

3\. Objective
To engage a qualified service provider to assign one dedicated cleaner to provide daily cleaning and housekeeping services for the ILO Erbil Office and ensure continuity of service throughout the contract duration and providing cleaning materials.

4\. Scope of Services
The contractor shall provide cleaning materials and one dedicated cleaner to perform the following services daily:
• Clean and disinfect desks, workstations, office furniture, and common areas.
• Sweep, vacuum, and mop all floor surfaces.
• Clean and sanitize washrooms, kitchens, and pantry areas.
• Empty waste bins and remove waste to designated disposal areas.
• Dust furniture, shelves, windowsills, equipment, and other accessible surfaces.
• Clean meeting room and ensure they remain presentable at all times.
• Report any observed maintenance, safety, or facility-related issues to the designated ILO focal point.
• Maintain cleanliness of all office areas in accordance with professional office-cleaning standards.
• All details are indicated in the below BOQ

5\. Working Schedule
The assigned cleaner shall be available as follows:
• Working Days: Sunday to Thursday
• Working Hours: 08:30 AM to 04:30 PM
• Services shall be provided during official working days unless otherwise instructed by the ILO.

6\. Contractor Responsibilities
The contractor shall:
• Assign one full-time cleaner exclusively for the ILO Erbil Office (the assigned personal should be agreed with the ILO in advance).
• Ensure uninterrupted service delivery throughout the contract period.
• Provide a qualified replacement cleaner during leave periods, illness, absence, resignation, or any other circumstance affecting service delivery.
• Provide initial induction and ongoing supervision of personnel.
• Ensure that cleaning personnel comply with professional conduct, confidentiality, and workplace safety requirements.
• Provide uniforms and identification badges for cleaning personnel.
• Maintain attendance records and provide reports upon request.
• Ensure compliance with all applicable labour laws, social security requirements, and occupational health and safety regulations.

7\. Cleaning Materials and Supplies

• Provide cleaning materials as per the details indicated in the BOQ below

8\. Personnel Requirements
ILO keeps right to ask the supplier to change the cleaner to meet the requirement ILO office criteria’s as:
• Have previous experience in office cleaning services.
• Maintain professional behaviour and appearance while on ILO premises.
• Follow all safety, security, and building access requirements.
• Respect confidentiality of information encountered during the performance of duties.

9\. Quality Standards
The contractor shall ensure:
• Consistent and high-quality cleaning services.
• Compliance with health and hygiene standards.
• Timely attendance and performance of assigned duties.
• Immediate replacement of personnel when required.
• Continuous monitoring and supervision of service quality.
10\. Contract Duration
Contract Period: Twelve (12) months From: 01 January 2027
To: 31 December 2027
The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funds, and mutual agreement between the parties.
11\. Deliverables
The contractor shall provide:
1\. One dedicated full-time cleaner.
2\. Daily cleaning and housekeeping services.
3\. Replacement personnel, when required, without interruption of services.
4\. Appropriate supervision and quality assurance arrangements.
5\. Attendance records upon request.
6\. Compliance with all contractual obligations and applicable regulations.
7\. Cleaning materials as per the details and the quantities listed in the BOQ below
12\. Financial Proposal
The bidder shall submit a financial proposal covering all costs related to:
• Personnel salaries and benefits.
• Supervision and management costs.
• Uniforms and identification badges.
• Replacement personnel.
• Administrative costs.
• Any other expenses required for satisfactory implementation of the services.

jobs.title: Project Officer (Distribution_MPCA-Hygiene and MHM) - Hasaka
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Project Officer (Distribution – MPCA, Hygiene and MHM) is responsible for the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities related to Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), hygiene distributions, and Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHM). The position ensures that assistance is delivered in a timely, safe, transparent, inclusive, and accountable manner, in line with approved project objectives, workplans, budgets, donor requirements, World Vision policies, and relevant humanitarian standards.

The Project Officer oversees distribution preparations and field implementation, coordinates beneficiary verification and distribution arrangements, supervises Distribution Workers and other assigned field personnel, and works closely with Logistics, Finance, MEAL, Protection, WASH, and other relevant teams. The position also ensures that assistance is responsive to the needs of affected communities, including women and adolescent girls, persons with disabilities, older people, and other vulnerable groups, while promoting dignity, safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Project Planning, Coordination and Distribution Implementation 25%**

- Support the development and implementation of activity workplans, distribution plans, schedules, and operational arrangements for MPCA, hygiene, and MHM interventions.
- Coordinate with relevant internal teams and field staff to ensure the timely availability of resources, supplies, beneficiary lists, distribution sites, and other requirements.
- Organize and oversee distribution activities in accordance with approved plans, standard operating procedures, eligibility criteria, and donor requirements.
- Conduct field visits to monitor implementation, verify readiness, assess site accessibility and safety, and ensure that distributions are conducted in an orderly and dignified manner.
- Supervise Distribution Workers and other assigned personnel, provide operational guidance, and ensure that responsibilities are clearly understood.
- Coordinate with Logistics and Warehouse teams regarding the receipt, storage, transportation, dispatch, and reconciliation of hygiene and MHM supplies.
- Coordinate with Finance and relevant service providers regarding MPCA delivery arrangements, ensuring that approved payment mechanisms and controls are followed.
- Identify implementation delays, operational challenges, and resource gaps and propose appropriate solutions to the supervisor.

**Multipurpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) Implementation and Follow-up 20%**

- Support the implementation of MPCA activities in accordance with approved targeting criteria, vulnerability assessments, transfer values, payment schedules, and project procedures.
- Coordinate with MEAL, Protection, and other relevant teams to support beneficiary identification, verification, validation, and referral processes in line with approved protocols.
- Ensure that beneficiary lists and required documentation are reviewed through established verification and approval procedures before being submitted to authorized personnel for processing.
- Coordinate with Finance and authorized financial service providers to monitor payment readiness, delivery schedules, and reported payment completion, while ensuring that financial transactions remain under authorized controls.
- Monitor payment-related issues, including unsuccessful transfers, beneficiary access barriers, reported discrepancies, and complaints, and coordinate appropriate follow-up.
- Ensure that beneficiaries receive clear information regarding assistance amounts, payment procedures, collection arrangements, eligibility requirements, and available feedback mechanisms.
- Coordinate post-distribution monitoring and other approved follow-up activities to assess access to assistance, beneficiary experience, and emerging protection or operational concerns.
- Maintain accurate records of MPCA implementation progress, including planned and completed assistance, verified payment status, outstanding cases, and reported challenges.
- Immediately escalate suspected fraud, unauthorized deductions, coercion, exploitation, or other irregularities through established reporting channels.

**Hygiene Distribution and Menstrual Health and Hygiene (MHM) Activities 20%**

- Coordinate the planning and implementation of hygiene and MHM distributions in accordance with approved project specifications, beneficiary needs, technical guidance, and distribution schedules.
- Coordinate with WASH, Protection, Logistics, Procurement, and other relevant teams to ensure that hygiene and MHM items meet approved specifications and are available in the required quantities and within the agreed timeframe.
- Verify distribution readiness, including the availability and quality of supplies, beneficiary lists, distribution documentation, staffing, and appropriate distribution arrangements.
- Oversee the distribution of hygiene kits, menstrual hygiene supplies, and other approved items, ensuring that quantities and items provided correspond to approved entitlements.
- Ensure that MHM assistance considers the dignity, privacy, safety, preferences, and specific needs of women and adolescent girls, including appropriate access arrangements and culturally sensitive communication.
- Coordinate with relevant technical staff to ensure that hygiene and MHM messaging is accurate, age-appropriate, inclusive, and consistent with approved technical guidance.
- Support awareness-raising activities on menstrual health, hygiene practices, safe use and disposal of menstrual hygiene materials, and other relevant topics within the approved project scope.
- Monitor the suitability and accessibility of distributed items and collect feedback regarding product quality, appropriateness, and beneficiary satisfaction.
- Report shortages, damaged or unsuitable items, distribution discrepancies, and other quality concerns and coordinate corrective action with responsible teams.

**Monitoring, Accountability, Data Management and Reporting 15%**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of planned, ongoing, and completed activities, beneficiary reach, distribution quantities, and implementation progress.
- Ensure that distribution documentation, beneficiary acknowledgment records, stock reconciliation records, and MPCA implementation records are complete and submitted within agreed deadlines.
- Coordinate with MEAL staff to implement approved monitoring tools, post-distribution monitoring, beneficiary satisfaction assessments, and other relevant data collection activities.
- Review monitoring findings, beneficiary feedback, and implementation data to identify gaps, recurring challenges, access barriers, and opportunities for improvement.
- Ensure that complaints and feedback received during distributions are documented and referred through approved accountability mechanisms, respecting confidentiality and informed consent requirements.
- Prepare regular activity updates, distribution reports, progress summaries, and supporting documentation for the Project Coordinator and other authorized personnel.
- Contribute to donor reporting by providing accurate quantitative and qualitative information, supporting evidence, and explanations of implementation progress and challenges.
- Support data quality checks and ensure that reported figures are consistent with approved beneficiary records, distribution documentation, and monitoring data.
- Ensure that beneficiary information is collected, stored, accessed, and shared securely and only for authorized purposes.

**Coordination, Safeguarding, Protection Mainstreaming and Compliance 20%**

- Coordinate with relevant project teams, Logistics, Finance, MEAL, Protection, WASH, partners, and authorized local stakeholders to facilitate effective implementation of activities.
- Participate in relevant coordination meetings, field planning sessions, and technical discussions as assigned by the supervisor.
- Ensure that distribution arrangements consider protection risks, accessibility, gender sensitivity, age, disability inclusion, and potential tensions between community groups.
- Apply Do No Harm and conflict-sensitive approaches throughout beneficiary engagement, targeting, distribution, and follow-up activities.
- Ensure compliance with World Vision policies, the Code of Conduct, safeguarding requirements, child protection standards, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), fraud prevention procedures, and relevant donor requirements.
- Ensure that staff and Distribution Workers understand and follow established procedures for beneficiary interaction, confidentiality, reporting concerns, and responsible use of project resources.
- Identify and promptly report safeguarding concerns, suspected fraud, exploitation, security incidents, and other serious risks through established organizational channels.
- Monitor compliance with approved workplans, budgets, procurement and distribution procedures, and applicable documentation requirements.
- Support lessons-learned exercises and contribute to identifying practical improvements in distribution processes and beneficiary experience.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**
- At least 2–3 years of relevant professional experience in humanitarian or development programming, preferably involving cash assistance, distributions, WASH, hygiene promotion, MHM, or related community-based interventions.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating field activities, distribution processes, beneficiary verification, and implementation follow-up.
- Experience working with beneficiary registration, distribution documentation, monitoring tools, and activity reporting.
- Experience coordinating with Logistics, Finance, MEAL, Protection, and other relevant teams to support effective activity implementation.
- Experience working with vulnerable and crisis-affected communities, including internally displaced persons, returnees, and host communities, is an advantage.
- Experience supervising field teams, Distribution Workers, volunteers, or community mobilizers is desirable.
- Experience with post-distribution monitoring, accountability to affected populations, and beneficiary feedback mechanisms is an advantage.
- Experience supporting cash and voucher assistance, including coordination with financial service providers, is desirable.
2. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**
- Bachelor's degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Business Administration, Public Health, Economics, Humanitarian Affairs, or another relevant field.
- Relevant training in cash and voucher assistance, humanitarian distribution management, WASH, MHM, accountability to affected populations, safeguarding, or protection mainstreaming is an advantage.
- Training in project cycle management, monitoring and evaluation, or humanitarian standards is desirable.
3. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**
- Good knowledge of FSL programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
- Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
- Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
- Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.
- Ability to work effectively with partners, community representatives, education
4. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

Non

**BACKGROUND**

Throughout the past years with increasing economic vulnerabilities, heightened tensions, and depleting basic services resulting from the multidimensional crisis that Lebanon has gone through, the public sector is facing multiple challenges affecting all government entities, particularly the security institutions. To mitigate the risks of a collapse of national public institutions, UNDP prioritizes the critical continuation of formal security services at community level by consolidating and strengthening the frontline stabilization role of the Internal Security Forces (ISF – Lebanon’s national police force). The effective functioning of the ISF is critical to ensuring public order, promoting smooth movement of populations, and enforcing eventual restrictions or securing of certain sites. ISF’s visible presence and service delivery significantly contributes to creating a safer, more inclusive and stable environment. In order to support the continued provision of formal security services, the ISF must ensure its physical presence on field as frontline responders. As part of its efforts within this context, UNDP procured the installation of spare and labour for 35 ISF Nissan cars. Under these efforts, UNDP seeks to recruit a consultant to oversee and coordinate the procured installation of spare and labour for the 35 ISF Nissan cars.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the guidance and supervision of the Rule of Law and Governance Chief Technical Advisor/ Project Officer, and in line with the ISF technical standards, and taking into account and complementing previous and ongoing UNDP led efforts the key responsibilities and scope of work include, but are not limited to, the following workstreams:

**I. Oversight on the authenticity of the spare parts installed.**

The Consultant must ensure and confirm to UNDP that all installed spare parts are authentic and exclusive Nissan Spare Parts

**II. Oversight of the technical compliance of the installed spare parts and labour**

Based on their expertise, the Consultant must ensure technical compliance and craftsmanship of the installed spare parts and the procured labour.

**III. Coordination with the UNDP and reporting on the authenticity and compliance of spare parts and labour**

The Consultant must report to UNDP compliance and authenticity or lack thereof of the installed spare parts and the attached labour. The Consultant must flag to UNDP any wrongdoings or unauthentic/ used parts installed.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities, noting that the total of the contract is 18 working days spread over a period of 1 month from contract signature.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the overall guidance of the Governance and Rule of Law Chief Technical Advisor/ Project Officer.
- The title rights, copyrights and all other rights whatsoever nature in any material produced under the provisions of this TOR will be vested exclusively in UNDP. UNDP has full ownership of the activity and of its final product. Thus, any public mention (including through social media) about the activity should state clearly that ownership. In addition, any public appearance related to the activity should be coordinated and approved by UNDP.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough, and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible for providing clarifications and facilitation of work.
- The consultant shall rely on his/her own means of communication and shall commute from/to place of residence to duty station at his own expense.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is One month with 18 working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The assignment is based at the RYMCO service center with occasional meetings at UNDP offices if need be.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tkqdPp56q0JTeJdafnncpcNJZENAtB3P/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tkqdPp56q0JTeJdafnncpcNJZENAtB3P/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has faced a prolonged economic, financial and social crisis. This includes the 2019 financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion and, most recently, more than a year of armed conflict. These shocks have severely weakened state institutions, which face major resource constraints and a significant loss of skilled staff. As a result, their capacity to regulate and to deliver on reform priorities has been limited.

In early 2024, UNDP launched the Lebanon Public Administration Reform and Digitalization Project (L-PARDP). The project supports the Government of Lebanon in restoring core functions and implementing priority reforms.

Lebanon’s economic recovery requires effective public institutions and a regulatory environment that promotes fair competition, market access and private-sector development. Through the Lebanon Public Administration Reform and Digitalization Project (L-PARDP), UNDP supports priority institutional and regulatory reforms, including support to the Ministry of Economy and Trade in implementing the Competition Law. A key priority is establishing the procedural framework through which the National Competition Authority will consider and adjudicate competition-law violations. Clear and enforceable procedures are essential to translate the law into effective regulatory practice, ensure consistent and transparent decision-making, and safeguard the rights of parties.

UNDP therefore seeks to engage a national legal consultant to prepare the draft decrees and accompanying explanatory notes governing referral, hearings and adjudication procedures under Article 36 of the Competition Law.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

The Consultant shall draft the procedural framework governing the referral of violations to the National Competition Authority, the conduct of hearings and the adjudication of cases, in accordance with Article 36 of the Competition Law.

The assignment shall include the preparation of the required draft decrees and accompanying explanatory notes, covering, at a minimum:

- Case referral and registration;
- Notification of parties and submission of written observations;
- Rights of defense and access to the case file;
- Conduct of hearings;
- Deliberation and decision-making;
- Notification and publication of decisions; and
- Other procedural safeguards necessary for the fair and effective adjudication of competition-law violations.

The Consultant shall ensure that the proposed procedures form a coherent, legally sound and operationally applicable framework, and shall finalize the draft texts in consultation with UNDP and the Ministry of Economy and Trade.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and deliver the following outputs within 2 months (without exceeding 8 working days per month):

- **Deliverable 1 – Referral and Pre-Hearing Procedures:** Draft decree provisions and accompanying explanatory notes covering case referral and registration, notification of parties, submission of written observations, rights of defense and access to the case file.
- **Deliverable 2 – Hearings and Adjudication Procedures:** Draft decree provisions and accompanying explanatory notes covering the conduct of hearings, deliberation and decision-making, notification and publication of decisions, and other procedural safeguards necessary for the fair and effective adjudication of competition-law violations.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the overall guidance of the UNDP Senior Economist and L-PARDP Project Manager and in close coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Trade and the National Competition Authority.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day to Day transportation from home to office (& vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his/her own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 2 months (without exceeding 8 working days per month).

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within 2 months from the contract signature date. to be completed no later than 31 January 2027.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will be home-based with regular coordination meetings at the Ministry of Economy and Trade in Beirut, as required.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree in Law, preferably with specialization in public, international, economic or commercial law, or a closely related field.
- **Experience:** At least 6 years of proven of experience in legislative drafting, legal and regulatory review, and legal advisory work relating to public-sector governance or economic regulation, including demonstrated experience drafting or reviewing laws, decrees, regulations or other legal instruments.

**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Vacancy Closure Date: 22 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PEij4BrLtVsJvbSTy-MlQ-3bne_6WNKS/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PEij4BrLtVsJvbSTy-MlQ-3bne_6WNKS/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has faced a prolonged economic, financial and social crisis. This includes the 2019 financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion and, most recently, more than a year of armed conflict. These shocks have severely weakened state institutions, which face major resource constraints and a significant loss of skilled staff. As a result, their capacity to regulate and to deliver on reform priorities has been limited.

In early 2024, UNDP launched the Lebanon Public Administration Reform and Digitalization Project (L-PARDP). The project supports the Government of Lebanon in restoring core functions and implementing priority reforms.

Lebanon’s economic recovery requires effective public institutions and a regulatory environment that promotes fair competition, market access and private-sector development. Through the Lebanon Public Administration Reform and Digitalization Project (L-PARDP), UNDP supports priority institutional and regulatory reforms, including support to the Ministry of Economy and Trade in implementing the Competition Law. A key priority is equipping the Competition Authority with clear and operational investigation procedures. A coherent investigation framework is essential to identify and substantiate potential violations, ensure the lawful collection and preservation of evidence, and protect confidential information and the rights of parties.

UNDP therefore seeks to engage a national legal consultant to develop a comprehensive Investigation Procedures Manual under Article 51 of the Competition Law, for issuance by regulatory decision of the National Competition Authority (NCA). The Consultant will also support the review and approval process, including addressing observations received from the Council of State and preparing the revised final version for adoption.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

The Consultant shall develop a comprehensive Investigation Procedures Manual setting out the detailed rules and procedures governing investigations conducted by the Competition Authority, in accordance with Article 51 of the Competition Law.

Specifically, the Consultant shall:

1. Develop the procedures for initiating investigations and gathering evidence, covering:
- Initiation and planning of investigations;
- Requests for information and documents;
- Interviews and statements;
- Collection, handling and preservation of evidence; and
- Inspections and dawn raids.
2. Develop the procedures governing safeguards, reporting and institutional coordination, covering:
- Confidentiality and protection of sensitive information;
- Preparation of investigation records and reports;
- Applicable procedural safeguards; and
- Interaction between the investigative function and the National Competition Authority.
3. Consolidate these procedures into a coherent and operationally applicable Manual and support the Authority throughout the review and approval process, including addressing comments and observations from the Council of State and preparing the revised final version for adoption.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and deliver the following outputs within 2 months (without exceeding 8 working days per month):

- **Deliverable 1 – Investigation and Evidence-Gathering Procedures:** Manual sections covering initiation and planning of investigations, requests for information and documents, interviews and statements, collection, handling and preservation of evidence, and inspections and dawn raids.
- **Deliverable 2 – Safeguards, Reporting and Final Consolidated Manual:** Manual sections covering confidentiality and protection of sensitive information, investigation records and reports, procedural safeguards, and interaction with the National Competition Authority; together with the consolidated final Manual incorporating comments received during the review and approval process, including observations from the Council of State, ready for adoption.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the overall guidance of the UNDP Senior Economist and L-PARDP Project Manager and in close coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Trade and the National Competition Authority (NCA).
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day to Day transportation from home to office (& vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his/her own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 2 months (without exceeding 8 working days per month).

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within 2 months from the contract signature date to be completed no later than 31 January 2027.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will be home-based with regular coordination meetings at the Ministry of Economy and Trade in Beirut, as required.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s Degree in Law. or equivalent)
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of proven professional legal experience in commercial, administrative or criminal law, including litigation before Lebanese courts and/or arbitration.
