jobs.title: Monitoring and Reporting Officer
jobs.description:
Background and organization context

The position is located in the Crisis Response Division (CRD), Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate for the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention; and facilitate sustainable solutions.

This multiple-duty-station temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Monitoring and Reporting Officer and is located across a number of OCHA Humanitarian Financing Units (in Uganda, kenya and Mozambique). Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office, the incumbent reports to the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager.

The Humanitarian Fund Units in OCHA Regional and Country Offices manage multi-donor country-based pooled funds under the leadership of the Humanitarian Coordinator/Resident Coordinator.

These funds receive unearmarked contributions from donors. The funds are allocated to humanitarian actors for ongoing humanitarian operations and to respond to new emergencies.

Position Purpose

Under the supervision of the regional humanitarian pooled fund manager, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will play a central role in strengthening accountability, effectiveness, and learning within the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU). The position is responsible for leading the implementation of monitoring, evaluation, and accountability frameworks that ensure compliance with established standards, promote transparency, and deliver measurable impact among partners and stakeholders.

The Monitoring and Reporting Officer will support evidence-based decision-making by developing and piloting innovative monitoring approaches, documenting best practices, and generating insights on the operationalization of localization strategies. Through active engagement with coordination forums and close collaboration with humanitarian partners, including local and national NGOs, the role facilitates inclusive participation, capacity strengthening, and knowledge sharing across the humanitarian system.

The position will also contribute to the planning and execution of monitoring missions, provide technical guidance to partners, and ensure systematic documentation and dissemination of results, lessons learned, and success stories. By maintaining strong coordination with field offices and stakeholders, the M&E Officer enhances program quality, promotes risk-sharing initiatives, and supports continuous improvement in fund management and delivery.

Overall, the role aims to ensure that the HFU operates in a results-oriented, accountable, and collaborative manner, while advancing localization and strengthening the effectiveness of humanitarian response efforts.

Key Duties and Accountabilities

Under the supervision of the Head of Humanitarian Financing Unit/Fund Manager, the Monitoring and Reporting Officer will be responsible for the following duties:

1.) Strengthen accountability, coordination, and monitoring effectiveness of the Humanitarian Funding Unit (HFU).

• Provide strategic leadership in advancing the HFU’s commitment to accountability, impact, and compliance by ensuring the robust and consistent application of the Accountability and Integrity Tool (AIT). This includes promoting transparency, reinforcing adherence to established operational standards, and fostering a culture of results-oriented performance among implementing partners and stakeholders.

• Represent the HFU in a broad range of coordination mechanisms, including Working Groups, area-based coordination platforms, sector-specific forums, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) structures. Actively contribute to discussions, influence decision-making processes, and ensure that HFU priorities and perspectives are effectively integrated into inter-agency coordination efforts.

• Identify, conceptualize, and pilot innovative and context-appropriate monitoring models and approaches aimed at strengthening oversight, improving data quality, and enhancing the overall effectiveness and efficiency of Country Fund interventions.

• Work in close collaboration with Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO) area offices, UNHCR, and implementing partners to strategically plan and execute monitoring missions. Provide hands-on technical assistance during these missions to ensure compliance, strengthen partner capacity, and enhance programme delivery on the ground.

• Maintain continuous and proactive engagement with the broader humanitarian community by participating in joint field missions alongside HFU and OCHA field staff, fostering collaboration, information sharing, and coordinated responses to emerging humanitarian needs.

2.) Enhance knowledge management, reporting, and localization efforts within the HFU framework.

- Design, coordinate, and facilitate webinars and other knowledge-sharing platforms aimed at strengthening the technical and operational capacities of partners, while promoting the exchange of experiences, expertise, and innovative practices across the humanitarian ecosystem.

- Systematically identify, compile, and analyze localization models and best practices implemented by other humanitarian funds, agencies, and organizations. Ensure that these insights are effectively documented and disseminated to inform strategic decision-making and continuous improvement within the HFU.

- Generate, synthesize, and disseminate evidence on the operationalization of the Uganda Humanitarian Fund’s localization approach by documenting both successful implementation models and key challenges or bottlenecks encountered in practice.

- Develop high-quality analytical products, including case studies, success stories, and practical examples, to effectively communicate lessons learned and showcase impact to the Fund’s Advisory Board and other strategic stakeholders.

- Contribute substantively to the preparation of a wide range of knowledge and communication products, including annual reports, policy and guidance documents, briefing notes, presentations, social media content, and official correspondence, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and alignment with organizational standards.

3.) Provide technical support, foster partnerships, and promote collaborative engagement.

- Deliver tailored, context-sensitive technical guidance and capacity-building support to Local and National NGOs through structured one-on-one consultations, group training sessions, and ongoing advisory support, with the aim of strengthening their operational effectiveness and compliance capacity.

- Support the design, development, and implementation of risk-sharing initiatives with Local and National partners, ensuring that such approaches are aligned with broader programmatic goals while promoting equitable partnerships and sustainable localization outcomes.

- Actively promote and sustain a high level of team cohesion and synergy within the HFU by encouraging collaborative, complementary, and cross-functional approaches to programme implementation and problem-solving.

- Establish and maintain strong, trust-based partnerships and communication channels with a wide range of stakeholders, including UN agencies, NGOs, and government counterparts, to facilitate coordinated, efficient, and impactful programme delivery.

- Undertake additional responsibilities and assignments as required by the HFU Manager, contributing flexibly and proactively to broader OCHA priorities and responding effectively to evolving operational demands and emerging humanitarian contexts..

jobs.title: Mensajero/a
jobs.description:
Aproximación por Niveles (Tiered Approach)

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organización, la mayoría de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicación por niveles (tiers) en donde:

- Nivel 0: personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos sáran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serán rescindidos o no renovados durante el año 2026

- Nivel 1: otro personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

- Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas

- Nivel 3 o sin nivel indicado: todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos

Por favor tenga en cuenta del nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si lo hay, y asegúrese de que cumple con la elegibilidad para aplicar.

Descripción Oficina

El Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) apoya el fortalecimiento de capacidades nacionales y subnacionales en Bolivia y promueve el logro de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS), los derechos humanos y la igualdad de género. A través de asistencia técnica, el PNUD busca fomentar el desarrollo humano sostenible cerrando brechas para que nadie se quede atrás. El PNUD construye alianzas en todos los niveles de la sociedad para ayudar a las naciones a resistir crisis y promueve un crecimiento inclusivo que mejora la calidad de vida de todas las personas. Con presencia en aproximadamente 170 países y territorios, el PNUD ofrece una perspectiva global y experiencia local al servicio de las personas y las naciones.

Alcance del Trabajo

Bajo la supervisión directa de el/la Asistente de Servicios Generales, el/la titular del cargo de Mensajero/a prestará sus funciones a la Oficina, enfocándose en el logro de las siguientes actividades y/o resultados

1. Brindar apoyo general a la oficina

- Mantener actualizado el registro de correspondencia y acontecimientos relevantes durante su turno, realizando las anotaciones necesarias en el cuaderno de registro y comunicando oportunamente la información pertinente al personal autorizado, resguardando la confidencialidad de datos personales y números telefónicos, los cuales no podrán ser proporcionados sin autorización.

- Apoyar en la atención telefónica institucional, canalizando llamadas y mensajes de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos.

- Proporcionar apoyo logístico y operativo para reuniones, talleres y actividades institucionales, incluyendo el armado, adecuación y limpieza básica de salas de reuniones.

- Apoyar en la organización, adecuación y acondicionamiento de oficinas, incluyendo el movimiento de mobiliario y apoyo en el cambio de luminarias u otros requerimientos menores de infraestructura, así como el apoyo al conteo físico de activos y el registro de los inventarios de la oficina del PNUD y sus depósitos.

2. Manejo de documentación

- Brindar servicios de mensajería interna y externa dentro de la ciudad de La Paz.

- Recepción, registro, escaneo (según el límite de páginas acordado con la Unidad de Servicios Generales)

- Distribución de correspondencia y documentación física, tanto oficial como personal, asegurando su entrega oportuna a la Unidad, Proyecto o funcionario.

3. Comunicación efectiva

- Mantener la comunicación con los miembros del equipo y las partes interesadas externas.

- Participar en las reuniones de equipo y contribuir a las discusiones.

- Proporcionar actualizaciones sobre las tareas y responsabilidades según sea necesario.

4. Otras responsabilidades

- Colaborar en actividades de prevención, respuesta y control básico de emergencias, incluyendo la prevención y extinción de incendios, así como el mantenimiento preventivo de las instalaciones, en coordinación con las áreas correspondientes.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización

Competencias

Esenciales

Lograr Resultados:

Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente:

Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente:

Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad:

Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación:

Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse:

Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión:

Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación

Competencias Transversales y Técnicas

Área Temática

Nombre

Definición

Administración y operaciones

Gestión de registros y correspondencia

Capacidad para recoger, registrar, mantener y entregar el correo y la valija del PNUD, así como para gestionar archivos.

Administración y operaciones

Gestión de documentos y registros

Gestión general de documentos (ya sean físicos o electrónicos); política de registro y conservación,

incluido el almacenamiento y archivo

Desarrollo institucional

Comunicación

Comunicarse de forma clara, concisa y precisa, tanto de manera escrita como verbal; personalizar los mensajes y

seleccionar los métodos de comunicación según la audiencia. Capacidad para gestionar las comunicaciones internas y externas a través de los medios de comunicación, las redes

sociales y otros canales apropiados.

Desarrollo institucional

Satisfacción/gestión de los clientes

Capacidad para responder de manera oportuna y adecuada, con sentido de urgencia, proporcionar soluciones coherentes y ofrecer resultados y soluciones de calidad en un plazo apropiado para satisfacer y comprender las necesidades reales de los clientes. Contribuir al desarrollo de la estrategia de servicio al cliente. Buscar maneras de añadir un valor adicional que sobrepase las solicitudes inmediatas de los clientes. Capacidad de anticipar las necesidades y preocupaciones futuras del cliente.

Ética

Conocimiento de las políticas de las Naciones Unidas en materia de ética

Conocimiento y comprensión del Estatuto y Reglamento del Personal de las Naciones Unidas y otras políticas relacionadas con la ética y la integridad.

Habilidades y experiencia requeridas

Requisitos académicos:

- Educación Secundaria (Bachiller en Humanidades) es requisito.

Experiencia:

- No se requiere experiencia especifica

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en el manejo de computadoras y programas de oficina (Microsoft 365, correo, archivos) nivel usuario.

Habilidades deseadas, adicionales a las competencias mencionadas en la sección de competencias:

- Estudios universitarios (Licenciatura universitaria) en administración, contabilidad y/o ramas afines.

- Experiencia en mensajería.

- Experiencia en manejo de correspondencia relacionada a trámites aduaneros.

- Experiencia apoyo administrativo en general.

- Experiencia como operador de telefonía.

- Experiencia en atención al cliente.

Lenguaje(s) Requerido(s)

- Fluidez en el idioma Español es requisito.

Certificados Profesionales

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de solicitar documentación física de verificación a los postulantes que calificaran a la última etapa o al ganador/a del proceso de selección

Información importante para las/os postulantes

Al momento de su postulación, si bien el portal le dejará adjuntar su CV, agradecemos que en la plataforma no olvide registrar sus conocimientos de idiomas, incluyendo el español (Spanish), así como tambien, le pedimos complete con detalle sus experiencias laborales y estudios.

Considere por favor que la vacante cierra bajo horario de New York (evitar enviar postulaciones a ultima hora).

El PNUD sólo se contactará con las personas pre-seleccionadas.

Igualdad de Oportunidades

El PNUD, como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que opera. En este sentido, se alienta a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postularse a las vacantes de la organización. Las decisiones de empleo se basan en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación de ningún tipo.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un entorno laboral inclusivo en el que todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a la misión institucional, sea valorado, pueda desarrollarse plenamente y acceder a oportunidades profesionales en igualdad de condiciones.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, el acoso sexual, la explotación, la discriminación ni el abuso de autoridad. Todas las personas seleccionadas estarán sujetas a verificaciones pertinentes y deberán cumplir con las normas, políticas y principios aplicables del sistema de las Naciones Unidas.

Derecho a seleccionar múltiples candidato/as

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar uno/a o más candidato/as a partir de este anuncio de vacante. También podremos conservar las aplicaciones y considerar a los/las candidato/as que apliquen a este puesto para otros puestos similares en el PNUD con el mismo nivel y con descripciones de puesto, requisitos de experiencia y formación académicas similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos

Se exhorta a las personas postulantes a consultar la guía del PNUD sobre el uso responsable de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos de selección y contratación.

Alerta de estafa

El PNUD no cobra ninguna tarifa en ninguna etapa de sus procesos de reclutamiento. Para mayor información, visite www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Knowledge Management and Communications Analyst (Home Based) [Open to Internal and External Applicants]
jobs.description:
Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP has achieved significant progress in making gender equality and women’s empowerment integral to its work on human development. It’s Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029 builds on the lessons and achievements of previous gender equality strategies and advances gender equality as a core accelerator of human development. The Strategy aims to support governments in transforming the systems, institutions, and power structures that perpetuate gender inequalities by placing gender equality at the center of political, economic, and environmental decision-making.

The Gender Team (BPPS) has the leading role in the implementation of the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029. The Gender Equality Global Programme (GEGP) serves as a key vehicle for advancing this agenda, including Outcome 1: Economies are inclusive, and women are economically empowered. Under this outcome, UNDP supports countries in developing and implementing gender-responsive economic and fiscal policies, strengthening public finance systems, expanding investments in the care economy, and generating evidence on the impacts of taxation, public expenditure, and social protection policies on gender equality. Through research, policy advisory services, and capacity development, the Programme contributes to ensuring that public resources and fiscal reforms support more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable development outcomes for gender equality.

Scope of Work

The Knowledge Management & Communications Analyst under the supervision of the Gender Specialist on Inclusive Economies, will:

Facilitate the development and implementation of communication strategy for the Inclsuive Economies portfolio

- Support the design and execution of a communication strategy to advance the Inclusive Economies portfolio, including public finance, care and labor market and economic policy reform.

- Develop tailored communications plans and campaigns to increase the visibility, influence, and reach of programme initiatives and results.

- Identify strategic communications opportunities to strengthen stakeholder engagement and position the portfolio as a thought leader on inclusive economies and gender equality.

- Facilitate internal coordination and information sharing cross regional and country-level initiatives to foster cross-pillar collaboration and knowledge exchange.

- Monitor communications performance and provide recommendations to strengthen outreach, engagement, and impact.

Ensure content development and dissemination for knowledge products and strategic communications

- Gather and translate technical content, programme results, and evidence into compelling communications products for diverse audiences.

- Develop and edit a range of materials, including policy briefs, feature stories, impact stories, blogs, newsletters, presentations, speeches, etc.

- Produce high-quality communications content that showcases programme achievements, innovation, lessons learned, and policy influence.

- Work closely with technical teams to ensure communications materials accurately reflect evidence, programme priorities, and strategic objectives.

Manage digital communications, website content, and social media engagement

- Lead the planning, development, and management of digital communications activities across websites, social media channels, and other online platforms

- Create and maintain engaging digital content, including multimedia materials, social media campaigns, web stories, and promotional assets.

- Coordinate website content updates and ensure information is accurate, timely an accessible.

- Monitor and analyze website and social media performance metrics to inform content strategies and improve audience engagement.

Provide communications and coordination support for the implementation of the Gender Team’s priorities related to inclusive economies and gender equality

- Support strategic communications and visibility efforts for key Gender Team initiatives, events, partnerships, and advocacy campaigns.

- Coordinate the collection of programme achievements, success stories, and results for internal and external reporting purposes.

- Provide communications support for donor engagement, resource mobilization efforts, and strategic partnerships.

- Attend management and team meetings as required, prepare agendas, document key decisions, and support follow-up on agreed actions.

- Support the Gender Team's strategic positioning and external engagement by ensuring consistent and effective dissemination of key messages and achievements.Perform any additional tasks related to this assignment as required by the supervisor.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Institutional Arrangement

The Knowledge Management & Communications Analyst works under the general supervision of the Gender Specialist on Inclusive Economies.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

2030 AGENDA: PROSPERITY Inclusive Growth

Women's Economic Empowerment

COMMUNICATIONS Advocacy strategy and implementation

Ability to create and implement advocacy strategies which lead to impactful change

COMMUNICATIONS Writing and Editing

Ability to create and/or edit written content in different UN languages

PARTNERSHIP MANAGEMENT Relationship Management

Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Knowledge Generation

Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

BUSINESS MANAGEMENT Knowledge Facilitation

Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

BUISNESS DIRECTION AND STRATEGY System Thinking

Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Minimum Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Communications, International Development, Gender Equality or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Minimum years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in relevant professional experience in knowledge management or communications related to gender equality.

Required skills

- Proven track record of strong writing and editing skills for varied audiences.

- Experience managing digital knowledge platforms, websites, collaboration tools, and content management systems.

- Demonstrated experience in strong storytelling and content packaging skills across multiple communication channels.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Experience with visual storytelling — infographics, data visualization, or basic design tools (Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, Figma).

- Familiarity with digital communications channels — newsletters, social media, web content management systems.

- Editorial/proofreading experience to maintain consistency and quality across knowledge products.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in English is required

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. jobs.title: Risk Analyst (Open Internal & External Applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Resident Coordinator in Somalia plays a critical role in the oversight in the implementation of UN Human Rights Due Diligence Policy (HRDDP) across support provided by UN agencies, funds and programmes to non-UN security forces and institutions as well as in the context of procurement processes. The Resident Coordinator’s Office (RCO), through its Risk Management Unit (RMU), supports the role of the Resident Coordinator in relation to the implementation of the HRDDP in Somalia. In that context, RMU is entrusted with a coordination role, that includes collecting and consolidating information on the status of support provided to non-UN security forces and progress towards the implementation of HRDDP mitigation measures recommended in the context of support provided by UN agencies, funds and programmes and UN procurement processes under the purview of the Resident Coordinator.

Somalia’s risk landscape remains highly complex and volatile, characterized by food insecurity, climate shocks, mass displacement, access constraints, armed hostilities, clan violence and corruption which permeates virtually every aspect of the Somali society. RMU continues to monitor and assess the changing complex environment and to convey critical information and analysis to inform stakeholders’ decision making.

The RMU supports all UN entities in Somalia and support is aimed towards the common goals of risk informed decision making, do no harm and increased accountability for better impact.

The Risk Analyst (HRDDP) is a key member of the Risk Profiling and Analysis team within the RMU, and is based in Mogadishu Somalia. He/she will be responsible for supporting the oversight role of the Resident Coordinator in relation to HRDDP implementation by UN AFPs in the context of their support to non-UN security forces and institutions as well as procurement processes under the Resident Coordinator.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Risk Management Specialist and the overall supervision of the Chief of RMU, the Risk Analyst (HRDDP) contributes substantively to the coordination of information and data gathering, analysis and compilation on HRDDP implementation by UN AFPs in the context of HRDDP. S/he will contribute to risk profiling and analysis services of the workstream, especially on security forces and/or security institutions, oversee day-to-day work related to HRDDP, and lead the engagement with UN AFPs in relation to their compliance with HRDDP and follow-up of HRDDP mitigation measures.

The Risk Analyst (HRDDP) also works in close collaboration with staff of the RMU, UN entities including UNSOS, UNDSS, UNDP, OHCHR and others, as well as peacebuilding, development, and humanitarian (nexus) partners, in the delivery of services provided to internal and external clients as it relates to HRDDP. S/he promotes a client, quality and results-oriented approach through the functions outlined below.

Duties and Responsibilities

The list of functions and tasks included in this terms of reference will be jointly reviewed and adjusted as necessary between the incumbent and their supervisor during the assignment. The Risk Analyst (HRDDP) will perform the following duties and responsibilities:

- Develop and deliver key HRDDP coordination and risk profiling and analysis functions. Monitor, research, collect, verify, analyze and synthesize significant amounts of information of relevance to HRDDP, including from open sources, UN entities and recipients of support. Work collaboratively with the integrated HRDDP capacity within the UN system in Somalia, notably UNSOS, and key UN entities including OHCHR and UNDSSand support the coordinated implementation of the HRDDP in UN AFPs, including by leading the engagement with HRDDP focal points in AFPs, supporting the mapping of recipients of support and advising on the implementation and monitoring of mitigation measures. Participate in discussions with relevant stakeholders in UN AFPs, RMU as well as security actors with a view to and advise on the prevention of and/or response to violations of international human rights or humanitarian law. Draft reports, briefings and other types of communications relating to HRDDP in compliance with established standards. Integrate UN developed methodology in the human rights monitoring, reporting and investigation activities related to HRDDP implementation, including ensuring a gender-perspective. Continuously assess Somalia’s evolving risk landscape, shifts in UN AFP HRDDP needs and update status of implementation of HRDDP mitigation measures, UN support, risk profiles and reports as needed and in line with the SOP on HRDDP implementation in Somalia to enhance decision-making by the Resident Coordinator.

- Contribute substantively to the strategic direction and overall management of the risk profiling and analysis workstream. Support the development and implementation of strategies, policies, protocols and guidelines for standardisation of key risk profiling and analysis functions in relation to HRDDP implementation. Support the formulation and implementation of the substantive work programme of risk profiling and analysis as it relates to HRDDP implementation by UN AFPs and/or procurement processes. Uphold highest ethical standards for information management to promote trust, respect, and accountability in RMU and United Nations HRDDP Task Force information management practices. Demonstrate transparency about how information is collected. Adhere to SOP on HRDDP implementation in Somalia. Maintain the integrity of information by ensuring its authenticity, reliability, and consistency (which includes the prevention of data tampering and/or manipulation).

- Contribute substantively to policy advice and support regarding risk profiling and analysis . Support the establishment, maintenance and strengthening of strategic relationships with key internal and external stakeholders including other UN entities, governments (national and regional), and civil society to build synergy, collaboration, and momentum on risk informed decision making to support HRDDP implementation. Contribute to capacity building of national stakeholders on matters related to HRDDP.

- Facilitate knowledge sharing Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on HRDDP implementation related issues. Facilitate the development of tools for dissemination of knowledge on HRDDP implementation within the context of these ToRs, and develop knowledge resources and products to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Identify the direct supervisor (s) and attach a general overview (or Organigram) in an Annex to show the position of this function within the office and unit structure (without indicating names of individuals).

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies (insert up to 7 competencies)

2030 Agenda: Peace

- Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Human Rights Institutions Access to Justice Safeguarding human rights and protecting vulnerable groups

2030 Agenda: Engagement and Effectiveness

- Effectiveness Systems and tools for managing risk

Data

- Data Data analysis Ability to extract, analyse and visualize data (including Real-Time Data) to form meaningful insights and aid effective decision making .

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Required Skills and Experience

- Min. Education requirements Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Law, Political Science, International Relations, Social Sciences, or related field is required, or A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

- Min. years of relevant work experience A minimum of two (2) years (with master’s degree) or four (4) years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant progressively responsible experience in the implementation of the HRDDP in the context of Somalia is required.

- Required skills At least 2 years of experience advocating, building the capacity and liaising with non-UN security forces and institutions in the context of Somalia, is required. Experience with the United Nations in a conflict and/or post-conflict setting is required. Experience collecting, collating, analysing and interpreting a wide range of complex information from a variety of sources (including large data sources) is required. Experience in paying attention to detail and ability to identify patterns, inconsistencies, or red flags such as violations of international human rights and humanitarian law and aid diversion is required.

- Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section Demonstrated experience in good networking and partnership development is desired. Experience in identifying, assessing, and managing various types of operational and/or project risks is desired.

- Required Language(s) Fluency in English is required Fluency in Somali is required

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. The Fiji multi-country office covers ten countries including Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu as well as provides support to regional initiatives.

The multi-country programme document for the Pacific (MCPD, 2023-2027) is in full alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023–27), with the 2030 agenda, 2050 Blue Pacific Continent Strategy. The MCPD strategic priorities are encapsulated under three outcome areas: (i) Planet, (ii) Prosperity, and (iii) Peace. The programme portfolio includes mutually reinforcing work streams crafted around three clusters (i) Resilience and Climate Change; ii) Inclusive growth; and iii) Effective governance, supported by a policy, communication and innovation team, Operations team, Management and Oversight team providing strategic guidance on results , knowledge management and communication support.

Within the Pacific Office Multi-Country Office (MCO), the Programme Team has a responsibility of developing, providing oversight, and ensure adherence to the quality standards of UNDP’s projects and programmes in full alignment with the priorities set out in the MCPD and UNSDCF during the design, implementation, and closure of projects and programme. The Management and Oversight Team, under the overall guidance on the effective oversight of programme and project management and ensuring the Office’s compliance with UNDP policies. The team provides cost-efficiency analysis of the country programme delivery and capabilities required, consolidates MCO financial planning and financial and resource management performance and undertakes monitoring and addressing issues related to management performance trends.

The Programme and Management Analyst role will focus on managing programme financial and resource management oversight and compliance activities of the sub-office, providing advice on quality and financial assurance activities, supports programmatic oversight work, and contributes to the successful portfolio delivery of the sub-office.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct and overall supervision of the UNDP Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) based in the FSM, the Programme and Management Analyst will undertake the following tasks:

Ensure effective and strategic resource planning, management, monitoring and reporting of development initiatives

- Ensure monitoring and oversight of internal control mechanisms and compliance of project and programme resource management actions, at the design, implementation and closure stages, to ensure that they are implemented consistently and in accordance with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies and procedures (POPP);

- Provide support in the implementation of standard operating procedures and business processes for quality of the project budgets formulation and delivery, including costing of results, availability of resources, and reporting requirements to enable adequate monitoring and oversight;

- Provide strategic contribution to the achievement of programme and project objectives and outcomes through active oversight, assessment of reliability and integrity of financial information provided in project reports and corporate systems, and the provision of support in quality and financial assurance activities;

- Ensure provision of quality support to programme teams on effective use of tools and methodologies for resource planning, monitoring and reporting to better orient environment vertical fund projects and other donor-funded projects against UNDP corporate and donor policies related to programme and project management, finance performance analytics, and other available sources of lessons and best practices;

- Support transparency and accountability in programme and project resource management, and overall programme management and carry out targeted reviews to ensure targets are met; and make appropriate recommendations for improvement;

- Regular analysis and reporting on sub-office annual programme delivery, availability of resources, pipeline projections and noting deficiencies and elaborating corrective actions in consultation with CO management;

- Ensure proper quality assurance for resource management and allocations, including financial reporting and proper project budgets set up in line with approved project multi-year workplans, all ERP/PIMS/Quantum and other platforms financial data is entered accordingly and maintained regularly;

- Monitoring and strategic advisory support to programme planning, resource allocation, and consolidated project budget planning, and ensure the corporate systems are up to date and reflect accurate data on resources.

Support accountability, risk management, quality control, and effective oversight of the assigned sub-office portfolio

- Support regular monitoring and analysis of the programme results, timely adjustment of projects activities, measuring of the impact of the projects, and that results, and lessons learned to inform analysis, policy and programme, and project work;

- Ensure efficient oversight (planning, budgeting, implementation, evaluation, reporting and monitoring) of the assigned portfolio of projects, tracking use of financial resources and their compliance with programme and operations policies and procedures (POPP) and quality assurance standard to meet the set targets contributing to the CO’s performance in corporate and regional KPIs;

- Ensure effective application of results-based management tools and high-quality reporting of results for internal and external audience, including entry of appropriate programme and project information, inputs, and results into corporate systems such as Quantum, Quantum+, and PIMs+;

- Provide quality assurance of the entire cycle of programming and management of portfolios;

- Implement Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfer (HACT) framework covering clearance measures on cash transfers, micro assessments, assurance plans and assurance activities and carries out programmatic monitoring visits, ensuring appropriate remedial actions are implemented;

- Applie UNDP’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework in the assigned portfolio, including the application of the Social and Environmental Standards in each project and ensures adequate safeguards measures;

- Ensure UNDP’s support to development institutions working towards addressing national development priorities in collaboration with the Government and other strategic partners.

Facilitate effective capacity development and knowledge facilitation

- Provide training and facilitates effective knowledge dissemination across the office and projects to ensure colleagues have easy access to resources and tools;

- Conduct analysis of sub-office data and case evidence to distil relevant lessons on programme and project management and implementation;

- In close collaboration with the MCO, contribute to development and delivery of modular training packages to strengthen sub-office, national counterparts, and partners’ capacities in the programmatic and operational oversight and implementation of the MCO portfolios;

- Contributes to development of training materials and organizes workshops, as required by the supervisor.

The Programme and Management Support Analyst performs other duties deemed in line with office and organizational needs as requested by the supervisor.

Institutional Arrangement

The Programme and Management Analyst will be working under the direct and overall supervision of the UNDP Deputy Resident Representative (DRR) based in the FSM. S/he promotes a collaborative, client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations and works in close cooperation with Management, Programme, Operations and other Teams within the MCO. This position will be required to travel to countries within the MCO for up to 15% of the time.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Demonstrate focus on achieving quality results and impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Look beyond conventional approaches and established methods

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Actively pursue opportunities for learning and self-development professionally and personally

Adapt with Agility :LEVEL 1: Be flexible in handling change, and adopt new ideas, approaches and ways of working

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Pursue everything with motivation and drive

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Act in a way that demonstrates empathy and emotional intelligence, showing consideration for the needs and feelings of others

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Treat all individuals with respect, consider ethical implications and respond sensitively to all differences among people

Business Management: Project Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Business Management: Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

Data: Data Analysis: Ability to extract, analyze and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision making

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Experience:

Desired Skills:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

UNDP South Sudan serves as an important actor in supporting development and humanitarian initiatives, including managing Global Fund grants aimed at combating HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and other communicable diseases. UNDP, as Principal Recipient, ensures effective financial and programmatic management, coordination with government ministries and partners, and achievement of programme objectives in line with UNDP's mandate to promote sustainable development and resilience in the country.

In South Sudan, UNDP's partnership with the Global Fund operates in a complex and fragile context, characterized by ongoing conflict, and displacement. Alongside ensuring continuity of essential HIV and TB services, UNDP works closely with the Ministry of Health, national programmes and partners to strengthen health systems, build national implementation capacities and advance the sustainability of health investments. This includes supporting a phased, country-led approach to capacity development and transition, taking into account the operational and institutional challenges facing South Sudan.

Position Purpose

Under the guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative (Programme), the Programme Manager (Global Fund) is responsible for the overall strategic planning, programmatic and operational management, and oversight of Global Fund projects under the GC8 grant in South Sudan. This includes ensuring achievement of programme goals, targets, and efficient delivery of interventions in HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and other relevant health sectors. The position requires close coordination with relevant national ministries, UN agencies, civil society partners, and other stakeholders to ensure effective grant implementation and compliance with Global Fund requirements.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

- Lead programme planning, management, monitoring and oversight, focusing on achievement of the following results: Provide strategic direction and management oversight to the consolidated Global Fund PMU across programme, M&E, finance, procurement and support functions. Lead the development and implementation of the GC8 work and operational plan for the US$73.8 million HIV, TB and RSSH portfolio, ensuring alignment with the Grant Agreement and UNDP’s Strategic Plan. Oversee preparation and quality assurance of Programme Update, Discontinuation and Progress Reports and other grant reporting to the Global Fund. Ensure achievement of planned targets (coverage, prevention, treatment) through quarterly monitoring of performance frameworks and timely corrective action. Coordinate with MOH, SSAC, the National TB Programme and other national stakeholders to harmonize Global Fund-supported interventions with national strategies. Provide leadership in grant revisions, reprogramming and budget modifications in line with Global Fund guidelines. Represent UNDP in CCM, LFA and Global Fund Country Team meetings and consultations. Manage risks proactively, including risk registers, mitigation plans and exception reporting to the Country Office and the Global Fund. Oversee the implementation of RSSH investments that strengthen laboratory, procurement, data and human-resource systems underpinning the HIV and TB responses. Promote the use of data for decision-making, including review of M&E and data-quality reports with the Programme & M&E unit. Monitor implementation of the GC8 operational plan budget and work closely with the Finance Specialist on budget utilization, reprogramming and value-for-money measures. 2. Exercise fiduciary oversight and grant risk management, focusing on achievement of the following results: Exercise oversight of grant portfolio to ensure effective, transparent execution of resources in compliance with UNDP rules and Global Fund requirements. Oversee UNDP direct payments under the no-cash restriction for MOH and SSAC and the administration of health-care-worker incentive payments. Review and clear programme and project transactions as required under UNDP’s delegation of authority, ensuring segregation of duties within the PMU. Ensure timely follow-up on Office of Audit and Investigations and sub-recipient audit recommendations and implementation of agreed action plans. Review periodic financial exception reports and grant performance ratings; escalate anomalies to the DRR and the Global Fund. Ensure compliance with Global Fund guidelines on budgeting, reporting and resource utilization, including timely submission of cash forecasts and financial reports. Ensure effective management of implementing partner capacities in financial management, including capacity assessments and support plans. 3. Lead, supervise and develop the PMU team, focusing on achievement of the following results: Supervise and develop the PMU staff across the Programme & M&E, Finance & QA, PSM & Procurement and Support units. Foster integration of programme and M&E functions and co-location of finance with programmatic quality assurance. Lead the PMU transition roadmap, including documentation of SOPs and roll-out of the eLMIS. Ensure surge arrangements and cross-functional backstopping for critical functions (finance, PSM, M&E) during leave or vacancies. Manage staff performance through work planning, regular feedback, learning and development, and annual appraisals. Promote staff well-being and safety and security compliance for PMU personnel travelling to field locations. Coordinate with the HR and Operations units on recruitment, onboarding and separation of PMU personnel. 4. Manage sub-recipients and external partnerships, focusing on achievement of the following results: Oversee the implementation of SR sub-grants and ensure compliance with SR agreements and 100% verification of SR expenses. Coordinate implementation of the capacity development and transition plan with MOH, SSAC and national partners, including agreed milestones for strengthening financial management, procurement, programme oversight and national ownership, while supporting the long-term sustainability of HIV and TB services. Maintain regular strategic engagement with MOH leadership, SSAC and national programmes to jointly review grant performance, address implementation bottlenecks and align Global Fund investments with national health priorities. Undertake regular field visits to supported facilities to monitor implementation and validate reported results. Ensure annual SR audits and timely follow-up on audit findings. Advance collaboration with the USG transition agenda under the MOU with the US Government. Develop and implement a capacity development plan for sub-recipients covering programmatic, financial, procurement and M&E functions. Lead the SR risk assessment process and apply differentiated oversight proportionate to SR capacity and performance. Facilitate joint annual work planning and review meetings with SRs and national programmes. Engage key populations, communities and civil society in programme design, implementation and monitoring. 5. Drive efficiency, value-for-money and strategic positioning, ensure facilitation of knowledge building and sharing in the CO and provide guidance to stakeholders on programmatic and operational issues, focusing on achievement focusing on achievement of the following results: Leverage the Global Fund Partnership and Health Systems Team (GFPHST) for advisory support. Lead resource mobilization, grant revisions and strategic initiatives to protect and expand the portfolio. Monitor PMU operational costs and implement efficiency measures to stay within the approved management budget envelope. Contribute to UNDP corporate reporting, country programme documents and resource mobilization initiatives related to health and HIV. Promote innovation and the use of digital solutions (eLMIS, DHIS2, dashboards) to improve efficiency and transparency. Identify and synthesize lessons learned and best practices from the HIV, TB and RSSH portfolio. Provide guidance to stakeholders on programmatic, financial and operational issues. Contribute to UNDP corporate knowledge networks and communities of practice on Global Fund implementation. Promote a culture of learning, documentation and innovation within the PMU. Document and disseminate success stories, lessons learned and knowledge products on Global Fund implementation in South Sudan. Organize learning events, peer exchanges and dissemination workshops with national counterparts and partners. Provide guidance to stakeholders on UNDP policies, Global Fund requirements and corporate initiatives.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervise professional and support personnel of the Global Fund PMU (13 direct reports across four units).

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigating complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies:

Business Management — Monitoring & Evaluation:

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively.

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools.

- Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks.

- Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Management — Resource Management: Allocate and use resources in a strategic or tactical. way in line with business needs and priorities and principles of accountability and integrity.

2030 Agenda: People — Health: Support to Global Fund and other Health Programmes.

2030 Agenda: People — Health: Promoting Effective and Inclusive Governance for HIV and Health.

Business Direction & Strategy — System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

2030 Agenda: People — Health: Health Resilience and Sustainable Systems for Health.

- Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity.

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Experience in managing Global Fund grants or other international health financing programmes is an advantage.

jobs.title: Conscious Food Systems Alliance (CoFSA) Community Engagement & Hubs Activation Intern, Planet Hub, BPPS (Home-based)
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organisation for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realise the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

UNDP’s 2026–2029 Strategic Plan reaffirms our continued commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals by accelerating structural transformations that advance poverty eradication, reduce inequalities, strengthen resilience, and drive sustainable, climate-aligned development.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora, including public-private dialogues, government, and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas.

As part of GPN in BPPS, UNDP's Healthy Planet Hub promotes and scales up an integrated approach to deliver UNDP’s environment portfolio across nature, climate, energy, and chemicals and waste, supporting countries in advancing implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and related multilateral environmental agreements. It coordinates UNDP’s flagship offers—Nature Pledge, Climate Promise, and Energy Moonshot, and Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention initiatives—to meet strong country demand across more than 140 countries. The Hub enables joined-up policy, programming, and financing solutions that accelerate low-emission, nature-positive, and pollution-free development, while strengthening resilience and advancing sustainable, inclusive growth in line with the Strategic Plan.

UNDP has developed its new Strategy for Food Systems to focus its vision and enhance its support to transform Food Systems. Food Systems is fundamental to the sustainable development of the 170 countries UNDP supports. Food Systems are often the largest contributor to their economies; food and nutrition are fundamental for citizen health; and Food Systems has a key role to play in achieving the SDGs. Yet, Food Systems are in crisis and need to be radically transformed to become sustainable. UNDP, building on its experience, has for the first time consolidated its Food Systems support and vision into this Strategy. The challenges and need for change related to Food Systems have been highlighted by a suite of reports by many research and international organizations and think tanks. The production practices and consumption patterns of food and agricultural commodities are taking these systems on an unsustainable trajectory with multiple impacts on human development, the environment, and economies; from ecosystem degradation, conflicts over land and natural resources, reduced capacity and resilience to climate and other shocks, persistent poverty, food insecurity and related people displacement and migration, to malnutrition including overweight and obesity. There is a clear need to work in a systemic and integrated manner to transform the Food Systems towards sustainability.

UNDP´s Vision for Food Systems 2030 is, through partnerships, to transform food and agricultural commodity systems into resilient; equitable; healthy, inclusive; environmentally, socially, and economically sustainable systems. Working on Food Systems will contribute to not only recovery from the COVID-19 crisis, by creating sustainable and resilient livelihoods for many along the Food Systems supply chains, but also to preventing further zoonoses from emerging in the future. This will require a change in the current paradigm of agricultural production focusing on maximizing productivity to a new paradigm based on diversified agroecological systems that work simultaneously on achieving economic, environmental, social, and health outcomes, with smallholders as a key part of the solution in their role as the engine of economic development. A Food Systems practice has been established within UNDP´s Nature, Climate, and Energy team, which is tasked to support UNDP Country Offices with Food Systems-related challenges in a way that is aligned with UNDP´s Food Systems strategy.

As part of its work on systems change, the Food Systems practice has developed the “Conscious Food Systems Alliance" (CoFSA), a movement of food, agriculture, and consciousness practitioners, convened by UNDP, and united around a common goal: to support people from across food and agriculture systems to cultivate the inner capacities that activate systemic change and regeneration. Launched publicly in October 2022 after two years of incubation with partners, the Alliance now has more than 400 members and 3000 followers.

UNDP FS is seeking to recruit a Conscious Food Systems Alliance (CoFSA) Community Engagement and Hubs Activation Intern to support the development and implementation of community engagement and hub activation activities across the CoFSA network. The intern will contribute to strengthening relationships with regional hubs, supporting community communications and engagement initiatives, and coordinating activities that foster collaboration and participation. The role will also provide operational and logistical support for key CoFSA events and initiatives, including coordinating post-summit follow-up activities and supporting the implementation of outcomes and ongoing engagement following the Conscious Food Systems Summit, hosted in Bhutan in Q3 2026. The successful candidate will report to the CoFSA Community Analyst.

Duties and Responsibilities

The intern will support the CoFSA Team in the community engagement and hubs activation, with responsibilities including:

Community engagement and hubs activation

- Assist in coordinating with regional and national hub focal points including scheduling meetings, following up on agreed actions, and maintaining communication channels (e.g. WhatsApp groups, email lists, Microsoft Teams);

- Support the development and dissemination of targeted communications and engagement materials for CoFSA members and hubs;

- Maintain community databases, mailing lists, and collaboration platforms to facilitate member engagement and knowledge sharing.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan. As part of GPN in BPPS, UNDP's Planet Hub promotes and scales up an integrated approach to deliver UNDP’s environment portfolio across nature, climate, energy, and chemicals and waste, supporting countries in advancing implementation of the Paris Agreement, the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and related multilateral environmental agreements. Food Systems are fundamental to the sustainable development of the 170 countries UNDP supports underpinning economies, nutrition, livelihoods, and progress towards the SDGs. However, unsustainable production and consumption patterns are driving environmental degradation, poverty, food insecurity, vulnerability to climate shocks, and malnutrition. Recognizing the urgent need for systemic transformation, UNDP has consolidated its experience and vision into a dedicated strategy to support the transition to more sustainable, resilient, and inclusive food systems.

UNDP´s Vision for Food Systems 2030 is to transform food and agricultural systems into resilient, equitable, healthy, inclusive, and sustainable systems through partnerships. This transformation aims to support economic recovery, strengthen livelihoods, improve resilience to future shocks, and promote environmental sustainability by shifting towards diversified agroecological approaches. To advance this agenda, UNDP has established a dedicated Food Systems practice to support Country Offices in implementing its Food Systems Strategy.

Since 2014, the Food Systems Community, hosted on the INVOLVE digital platform, fulfils a pivotal learning, connectivity and knowledge management function towards, the Food Systems, Land Use and Restoration (FOLUR) Impact Programme led by the World Bank, the Food Systems Integrated Programme (FS-IP) led by FAO and IFAD, the Blue and Green Islands Integrated Programme (BG-IP) led by UNDP and a growing number of other initiatives and projects.. c) Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and sharing, focusing on achievement of the following results:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:
